1679      // Have we already opened an XMTok? Then insert into it.
1680      Ok(Some(self.open_math_text_internal(object)?))
1681    // Else create the XMTok now.
1682    } else {
1683      // Odd case: constructors that work in math & text can insert raw strings in Math mode.
1684      let font_math_opt = match props.get("font") {
1685        Some(Stored::Font(fnt)) => Some(Cow::Borrowed(&**fnt)),
1686        Some(Stored::FontDirective(FontDirective::Asset(fnt))) => Some(Cow::Borrowed(&**fnt)),
1687        Some(Stored::FontDirective(FontDirective::Closure(code))) => Some(Cow::Owned(code(None)?)),
1688        _ => None,
1689      };
1690      if let Some(font_math) = font_math_opt {
1691        Ok(Some(self.insert_math_token(
1692          object,
1693          HashMap::default(),
1694          Some(&font_math),
1695        )?))
1696      } else {
1697        Ok(Some(self.insert_math_token(
1698          object,
1699          HashMap::default(),
1700          None,
1701        )?))
1702      }
1703    }
1704  }
1705  //%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
1706
1707  /// Perl: insertElementBefore — insert a new element before a given point node.
1708  /// Creates a new element with the given qname and attributes, inserts it
1709  /// before `point` in the DOM tree, and returns the new node.
1710  pub fn insert_element_before(
1711    &self,
1712    point: &Node,
1713    qname: &str,
1714    attrib: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
1715  ) -> Result<Node> {
1716    // Create element in LTX namespace (matching Perl's setNamespace($LTX_NS,'',1))
1717    let mut new_node = Node::new(qname, None, &self.document)?;
1718    if let Some(attrs) = attrib {
1719      for (key, value) in attrs {
1720        let _ = new_node.set_attribute(&key, &value);
1721      }
1722    }
1723    // insertBefore: add new_node before point
1724    let mut point_mut = point.clone();
1725    point_mut.add_prev_sibling(&mut new_node).ok();
1726    Ok(new_node)
1727  }
1728
1729  /// Insert a construction-time position mark: an empty internal element (`*_Capture_`-suffixed, admitted anywhere by
1730  /// the model, never in the output) at the current point, as [`Document::insert_element`] does, its name recorded
1731  /// first. A mark of a name a pass gates on with [`Document::made_mark`] (`_Frontmatter_Capture_`,
1732  /// `_CoverTitleBegin_Capture_`, `_CoverTitleEnd_Capture_`) must be made only here (or copied from one made here), so a
1733  /// pass looking for marks of a name none was made of has none to find and skips its scan of the document; other marks
1734  /// (`insert_element`) are not recorded.
1735  pub fn insert_mark(
1736    &mut self,
1737    qname: &str,
1738    attrib: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
1739  ) -> Result<Node> {
1740    if !self.made_mark(qname) {
1741      self.marks_made.push(qname.to_string());
1742    }
1743    self.insert_element(qname, Vec::new(), attrib)
1744  }
1745
1746  /// Was a position mark named `qname` ever made in this document ([`Document::insert_mark`])? False: none is in it.
1747  pub fn made_mark(&self, qname: &str) -> bool { self.marks_made.iter().any(|made| made == qname) }
1748
1749  /// Was a field mark ([`FIELD_MARK_TARGET`]) ever made in this document? False: none is in it — a field mark is made
1750  /// only where a run of field ink opens or closes, and a run's end mark only after its begin mark (a copy is copied
1751  /// from one).
1752  pub fn made_field_marks(&self) -> bool { self.field_run_serial > 0 }
1753
1754  /// Shorthand for open,absorb,close, but returns the new node.
1755  pub fn insert_element(
1756    &mut self,
1757    qname: &str,
1758    content: Vec<&Digested>,
1759    attrib: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
1760  ) -> Result<Node> {
1761    // TODO: Quickly hacked together, needs a careful refactor with all .clone()
1762    // calls removed
1763    let node = self.open_element(qname, attrib, None)?;
1764    // Debug!("Inserting element {:?} with body: {:?}", qname, content);
1765    for digested in content {
1766      self.absorb(digested, None)?;
1767    }
1768
1769    // Walk up from the current insertion point to learn whether `node` is still
1770    // an open ancestor (so it can be closed below). `self.node` may be the
1771    // parentless document root, and an intermediate node may be detached — a
1772    // `None` parent there simply means `node` is NOT an ancestor (stop the walk),
1773    // so don't `.unwrap()`-panic on it. Witnesses: hep-th0201062, 1009.0637.
1774    let mut c = self.node.get_parent();
1775    while c.is_some()
1776      && c.as_ref() != Some(&node)
1777      && c.as_ref().unwrap().get_type() != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode)
1778    {
1779      c = match c.as_ref().unwrap().get_parent() {
1780        None => None,
1781        Some(parent) => match parent.get_type() {
1782          Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) | None => None,
1783          Some(_) => Some(parent),
1784        },
1785      };
1786    }
1787
1788    // In obscure situations, `node` may have already gotten closed?
1789    // close it if it is still open.
1790    if (self.node == node) || (c.as_ref() == Some(&node)) {
1791      self.close_element(qname)?;
1792    }
1793    Ok(node)
1794  }
1795
1796  /// Insert a ProcessingInstruction of the form <?op attr=value ...?>
1797  /// Does NOT move the current insertion point to the PI,
1798  /// but may move up past a text node.
1799  // Rust note: attrib would have been best as Vec<(String,String)> but
1800  // currently quote!() doesn't work out of the box on them
1801  pub fn insert_pi(
1802    &mut self,
1803    op: &str,
1804    attributes_opt: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
1805  ) -> Result<()> {
1806    let data = attributes_opt.as_ref().map(pi_data).unwrap_or_default();
1807    // self.close_text_internal();  // Close any open text node
1808    let mut pi_node = self
1809      .document
1810      .create_processing_instruction(op, &data)
1811      .unwrap();
1812    // Perl (Core/Document.pm insertPI): a PI always lands before the root
1813    // element. When the root already exists — a mid-body or document-final PI
1814    // (#683's `<?latexml nominal-font-size?>` is emitted at finalization) —
1815    // insert directly before it, whatever the current insertion point. Only
1816    // when NO root has been opened yet (the usual pre-`\begin{document}` case)
1817    // queue the PI in `pending`, to be flushed the moment the root opens
1818    // (`open_element_at`). The old code keyed solely on the insertion point
1819    // being the DocumentNode and so re-queued a post-root PI into `pending`,
1820    // which drains once and never again — the PI was silently lost.
1821    if let Some(mut root) = self.document.get_root_element() {
1822      root.add_prev_sibling(&mut pi_node)?;
1823    } else if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
1824      self.pending.push(pi_node);
1825    } else {
1826      self.node.add_prev_sibling(&mut pi_node)?;
1827    }
1828    Ok(())
1829  }
1830
1831  /// Open a new `qname` element and make it the current insertion point.
1832  ///
1833  /// Where it opens is the model's decision, not the caller's: the insertion
1834  /// point is first moved by [`find_insertion_point`](Self::find_insertion_point),
1835  /// which auto-opens any element the schema requires in between and
1836  /// auto-closes any that cannot contain `qname`. So a binding may open a
1837  /// `ltx:para` without first checking what is currently open.
1838  ///
1839  /// See [`open_element_at`](Self::open_element_at) to open at an explicit node
1840  /// instead, and [`close_element`](Self::close_element) for the counterpart.
1841  pub fn open_element(
1842    &mut self,
1843    qname: &str,
1844    attributes: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
1845    font_opt: Option<&Font>,
1846  ) -> Result<Node> {
1847    // NoteProgress('.') if (self.progress}++ % 25) == 0;
1848    // Debug!(
1849    //   s!("Open element {:?} at {:?}",
1850    //   qname,
1851    //   self.with_node_qname(&self.node))
1852    // );
1853    // a TeX box's constructor opening its own element ([`FIELD_BOX_PROPERTY`]); not one auto-opened on the way
1854    let field_box = std::mem::take(&mut self.field_box_pending);
1855    let mut point = self.find_insertion_point(qname, None)?;
1856    // Perl Document.pm:792 `$attributes{_box} = $LaTeXML::BOX unless
1857    // $attributes{_box}`: an element opened at the insertion point is recorded
1858    // with the box being absorbed, ahead of the insertion point's own box
1859    // (which is what a bare `openElementAt` falls back to). Underscore
1860    // attributes such as `_box` and `_font` are bookkept in `node_boxes` /
1861    // `node_fonts` rather than as libxml attributes.
1862    let requested_box = self.box_to_absorb.clone();
1863    let mut newnode = self.open_element_at_with_box(
1864      &mut point,
1865      qname,
1866      attributes,
1867      font_opt.cloned(),
1868      requested_box,
1869    )?;
1870    // An element of a construct that never ended (its group abandoned, `stomach::UNENDED`)
1871    // auto-closes: Perl's per-node `_autoclose` (Document.pm `canAutoClose`). OXIDIZED_DESIGN #542.
1872    // So does an element auto-opened inside such an element (an implicit wrapper its parent's
1873    // close would close).
1874    let unended = self.absorbing_unended_box()
1875      || (newnode.has_attribute("_autoopened")
1876        && newnode
1877          .get_parent()
1878          .is_some_and(|parent| parent.has_attribute(UNENDED_ATTRIBUTE)));
1879    // `_noautoclose` (an `\fbox`'s `ltx:text`, 1210.0368) holds against font switches in a box
1880    // that ends; this one does not.
1881    if unended {
1882      let _ = newnode.remove_attribute("_noautoclose");
1883      let _ = newnode.set_attribute("_autoclose", "true");
1884      // Its closer finds it closed already when the structure after it closed it.
1885      let _ = newnode.set_attribute(UNENDED_ATTRIBUTE, "true");
1886    }
1887    if field_box {
1888      self.mark_field_box(&mut newnode);
1889    }
1890    self.set_node(&newnode);
1891
1892    Ok(newnode)
1893  }
1894
1895  /// Stamp a freshly-opened element with its source range as a
1896  /// `data-sourcepos` attribute, for the `--source-map` feature (issues
1897  /// #47/#92). The range comes from the construct currently being absorbed
1898  /// (`box_to_absorb`); the integer file `tag` is resolved through the
1899  /// document-level `sources` table (`state::source_tag`) so no path is
1900  /// inlined. See `docs/performance/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md` §0/§2.
1901  ///
1902  /// Math is kept **opaque** per the MVP scope: the `ltx:Math` wrapper is
1903  /// stamped, but its `ltx:XM*` MathML internals are skipped (the Marpa
1904  /// math parser has no locator awareness — §7 A.3). Only invoked when the
1905  /// source-map switch is on (the caller gates it).
1906  fn stamp_source_locator(&mut self, node: &Node, qname: &str) {
1907    // Math internals: stamp only the leaf token elements (`ltx:XMTok` — the
1908    // operators / identifiers / numbers) when token-locators gives them a real
1909    // located box locator (the math char's source origin). This is the per-token
1910    // in-equation provenance step (§7 A.3). The structural XM* (XMApp/XMDual/
1911    // XMArray) are rebuilt by the Marpa parser — created directly, not via
1912    // `open_element` — so they never reach here; the remaining digestion-built
1913    // wrappers (XMArg/XMHint/XMText/XMRef/XMWrap) stay opaque. The `data:sourcepos`
1914    // rides the XMTok element through the parser's restructuring (attribute on a
1915    // reparented node) and through the XMath→MathML XSLT.
1916    //
1917    // Gated at compile time: feature-OFF keeps math fully opaque (the MVP scope
1918    // and the golden's math-opacity assertion); only the token-locators build
1919    // exposes the located XMTok leaves.
1920    #[cfg(not(feature = "token-locators"))]
1921    if qname.starts_with("ltx:XM") {
1922      return;
1923    }
1924    #[cfg(feature = "token-locators")]
1925    if qname.starts_with("ltx:XM") && qname != "ltx:XMTok" {
1926      return;
1927    }
1928    // Read the pre-captured Copy locator — never re-borrow the box here.
1929    let Some(loc) = self.current_box_locator else {
1930      return;
1931    };
1932    // Skip locators with no real source position (default/synthetic).
1933    if loc.from_line == 0 {
1934      return;
1935    }
1936    // User-source only (§7.B): emit a navigable locator only into an editable
1937    // user document — `.tex`/`.ltx`, plus the bibliography sources `.bbl` (the
1938    // BibTeX-generated, but author-editable, list of `\bibitem`s) and `.bib`
1939    // (BibTeX database entries). All four are files the editor may legitimately
1940    // scroll into. This skips both synthetic default locators (whose source is
1941    // `…/locator.rs`, from `Locator::default()`'s `file!()`) and foreign
1942    // package/class files (`.sty`/`.cls`/…) — the editor must never scroll into
1943    // those. Foreign/unstamped elements inherit their nearest user-source
1944    // ancestor's range client-side (DOM walk-up). (MVP heuristic; a tracked
1945    // user-input set would be more precise.)
1946    let src = loc.get_source();
1947    let is_user_source = arena::with(src, |s| {
1948      let s = s.to_ascii_lowercase();
1949      s.ends_with(".tex") || s.ends_with(".ltx") || s.ends_with(".bbl") || s.ends_with(".bib")
1950    });
1951    if !is_user_source {
1952      return;
1953    }
1954    let tag = state::source_tag(src);
1955    // Emit in LaTeXML's `data:` namespace (`http://dlmf.nist.gov/LaTeXML/data`,
1956    // registered in `base_schema.rs:19`). The post XSLT's `copy_foreign_attributes`
1957    // path converts a `data:`-prefixed *foreign-namespaced* attribute to the HTML
1958    // `data-sourcepos` attribute (`LaTeXML-common.xsl`: `data:` prefix → `data-…`
1959    // when `USE_DATA_ATTRIBUTES` = true, i.e. HTML5). Faithful to Perl LaTeXML's
1960    // foreign-attribute convention; no XSLT change needed. The general namespaced-
1961    // attribute binding lives in `set_attribute` (shared with `aria:` etc.).
1962    let mut n = node.clone();
1963    let _ = self.set_attribute(&mut n, "data:sourcepos", &loc.to_sourcepos(tag));
1964  }
1965
1966  /// Note: This closes the deepest open node of a given type.
1967  /// This can cause problems with auto-opened nodes, esp. ones for fontswitches!
1968  /// Since this is an "explicit request", we're currently skipping over those nodes,
1969  /// ie. we're automatically closing them, even if they're the same type as we're asking to
1970  /// close!!! This is kinda risky! Maybe we should try to request closing of specific nodes.
1971  /// `close_element`, but a no-op when no `qname` element is open on the
1972  /// current ancestor chain: the strict close (auto-closing or force-closing
1973  /// the intervening descendants) whenever the element is still open, and
1974  /// silence only when content that the element could not hold auto-closed
1975  /// it already. Used for a replacement's closing tag of an element the same
1976  /// replacement opened (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #202).
1977  pub fn close_element_if_open(&mut self, qname: &str) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
1978    if self.is_open_on_chain(qname) {
1979      self.close_element(qname)
1980    } else {
1981      Debug!(
1982        "document",
1983        "close_element",
1984        s!("Element {:?} already closed by its content", qname)
1985      );
1986      Ok(None)
1987    }
1988  }
1989
1990  /// Close the `{quote}`, `{quotation}` or `{verse}` (`ltx:quote`, which does not auto-close) standing between the
1991  /// current point and a place that can hold one of `qsyms` — a display sectioning unit `\part`..`\subsubsection`
1992  /// (`find_insertion_point_qsym`; a run-in `\paragraph`/`\subparagraph` stays in the quote, `is_quote_closing_unit`)
1993  /// or a bibliography and the unit it stands as (latex_constructs `adjust_backmatter_element`). Each of these environments
1994  /// is LaTeX's unlabelled list `\list{}{…}\item\relax` (article.cls:389-408), a margin, no structure: the heading and
1995  /// what follows it are the document's own unit, typeset within the margin (latex.ltx `\@startsection`;
1996  /// `thebibliography` = `\section*` + `\list`, article.cls:565-584). The quotes in the way, from the innermost, are
1997  /// closed only when that alone (with the auto-closing elements between) makes the place reachable — a quote in a list
1998  /// item, or outside the `minipage` the point is in, stays open (probes b_qiq, b_qmq) and the caller reports as before — and each one left empty
1999  /// is dropped. The environment's end then finds its quote closed (`latex_constructs` sect06 `quote_environment`).
2000  /// Returns whether it closed any. User rulings 2026-10-16 (D1, bibliography) and 2026-10-17 (D5, sectioning units: as
2001  /// the item bridge's margin-list exemption), OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #677, #678; witnesses 2203.09193 1904.12066
2002  /// 1610.09996 2109.09861 2403.09260 1609.06434 astro-ph0410583 1504.06728 (bibliography), 0712.1985 (a title page in
2003  /// `{quotation}`). Guards `perfect_kernel_batch69a::{bibliography_in_a_quote_closes_the_quote,
2004  /// section_in_a_quotation_closes_it}`.
2005  pub fn close_quotes_blocking(&mut self, qsyms: &[SymStr]) -> Result<bool> {
2006    let mut node = if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
2007      self.node.get_parent()
2008    } else {
2009      Some(self.node.clone())
2010    };
2011    let mut quotes: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
2012    // Whether the walk has left a box's capture (a `minipage`, a `\parbox`): it takes any content by the model, but a
2013    // bibliography in it is placed outside the box (`adjust_backmatter_element`), so the walk looks further up — and a
2014    // quote outside the box is not closed from within it (probe b_qmq; b_quote_in_minipage's own quote is closed).
2015    let mut left_box = false;
2016    loop {
2017      let Some(current) = node else {
2018        return Ok(false);
2019      };
2020      if current.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
2021        return Ok(false);
2022      }
2023      if is_capture_block(&current) {
2024        left_box = true;
2025        node = current.get_parent();
2026        continue;
2027      }
2028      let current_qname = get_node_qname(&current);
2029      if qsyms.iter().any(|q| {
2030        sym_can_contain_somehow(current_qname, *q).is_some() && holds_in_quote_block(&current, *q)
2031      }) {
2032        break;
2033      }
2034      if current_qname == pin!("ltx:quote") && !can_auto_close(&current) && !left_box {
2035        quotes.push(current.clone());
2036      } else if !can_auto_close(&current) {
2037        return Ok(false);
2038      }
2039      node = current.get_parent();
2040    }
2041    let Some(outermost) = quotes.last().cloned() else {
2042      return Ok(false);
2043    };
2044    self.close_node_internal(&outermost)?;
2045    for quote in quotes {
2046      let empty = quote.get_child_nodes().iter().all(|child| {
2047        child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) && child.get_content().trim().is_empty()
2048      });
2049      if empty {
2050        self.remove_node(quote);
2051      }
2052    }
2053    Ok(true)
2054  }
2055
2056  /// Whether a `qname` element is open on the current ancestor chain (a font-switch `ltx:text`
2057  /// does not count as an open `ltx:text`).
2058  fn is_open_on_chain(&self, qname: &str) -> bool {
2059    let qsym = arena::pin(qname);
2060    let mut node = if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
2061      self.node.get_parent()
2062    } else {
2063      Some(self.node.clone())
2064    };
2065    while let Some(n) = node {
2066      if n.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
2067        break;
2068      }
2069      if get_node_qname(&n) == qsym && !(qsym == pin!("ltx:text") && n.has_attribute("_fontswitch"))
2070      {
2071        return true;
2072      }
2073      node = n.get_parent();
2074    }
2075    false
2076  }
2077
2078  /// Closes a still-open `qname` element whose source groups were ABANDONED (tex.web §1335: the
2079  /// groups open at `\end` are reported once, then dropped): every descendant still open closes
2080  /// with it — running each one's close-time hooks: the bare-`\bibitem` bibliography's heading
2081  /// absorption (repros boxes-groups/abandoned_document_close_runs_bibliography_hooks,
2082  /// …_invents_no_bibliography_title), the empty-para prune (jpnedumathsymbols-doc), the `ltx:p`
2083  /// whitespace trim (tikz-optics). The descendants that do not auto-close are listed in an Info
2084  /// line (biblatex-ms: `itemize`), not a Warning: the abandonment was reported already. A no-op
2085  /// when no `qname` element is open.
2086  pub fn close_abandoned_element(&mut self, qname: &str) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
2087    if self.is_open_on_chain(qname) {
2088      self.close_element_impl(qname, CloseDescendants::Abandoned)
2089    } else {
2090      Ok(None)
2091    }
2092  }
2093
2094  pub fn close_element(&mut self, qname: &str) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
2095    self.close_element_impl(qname, CloseDescendants::Strict)
2096  }
2097
2098  fn close_element_impl(
2099    &mut self,
2100    qname: &str,
2101    descendants: CloseDescendants,
2102  ) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
2103    Debug!(
2104      "document",
2105      "close_element",
2106      s!(
2107        "Close element {:?} at {:?}",
2108        qname,
2109        self.document.node_to_string(&self.node)
2110      )
2111    );
2112    let qsym = arena::pin(qname);
2113    self.close_text_internal()?;
2114    let mut node = self.node.clone();
2115    let mut cant_close = Vec::new();
2116    while node.get_type() != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
2117      let t = get_node_qname(&node);
2118      // autoclose until node of same name BUT also close nodes opened' for font
2119      // switches!
2120      if t == qsym
2121        && !(t == pin!("ltx:text") && node.has_attribute("_fontswitch"))
2122        && !is_trivlist(&node)
2123      {
2124        break;
2125      }
2126      if !can_auto_close(&node) {
2127        cant_close.push(node.clone());
2128      }
2129      match node.get_parent() {
2130        Some(parent) => {
2131          node = parent;
2132        },
2133        None => break, // detached node — treat as not found
2134      }
2135    }
2136
2137    if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
2138      // Didn't find $qname at all!! Unless the construct closing it never ended: its element
2139      // auto-closed already, when the structure after it arrived (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #542).
2140      if self.absorbing_unended_box() {
2141        return Ok(None);
2142      }
2143      let qname_msg: String = match qname {
2144        "#PCDATA" => qname.to_owned(),
2145        _ => s!("</{qname}>"),
2146      };
2147      let message = s!(
2148        "Attempt to close {}, which isn't open. Currently in {}",
2149        qname_msg,
2150        self.get_insertion_context(None)?
2151      );
2152      Error!("malformed", qname, message);
2153      Ok(None)
2154    } else {
2155      // Found node.
2156      if !cant_close.is_empty() {
2157        // Intervening non-auto-closeable nodes!!
2158        let message = s!(
2159          "Closing tag {:?} whose open descendents do not auto-close. Descendants are {:?}",
2160          qname,
2161          cant_close
2162            .into_iter()
2163            .map(|n| n.get_name())
2164            .collect::<Vec<String>>()
2165            .join(",")
2166        );
2167        match descendants {
2168          CloseDescendants::Strict => Error!("malformed", qname, message),
2169          CloseDescendants::Abandoned => {
2170            Info!(
2171              "malformed",
2172              qname,
2173              s!("{message} (their groups were abandoned)")
2174            )
2175          },
2176        }
2177      }
2178      // So, now close up to the desired node.
2179      self.close_node_internal(&node)?;
2180      Ok(Some(node))
2181    }
2182  }
2183
2184  // Check whether it is possible to open $qname at this point,
2185  // possibly by autoOpen'ing & autoClosing other tags.
2186  pub fn is_openable(&self, test_qname: &str) -> bool {
2187    let mut node_opt = Some(self.node.clone());
2188    let test_sym = arena::pin(test_qname);
2189    while let Some(node) = node_opt {
2190      let node_qname = get_node_qname(&node);
2191      if sym_can_contain_somehow(node_qname, test_sym).is_some() {
2192        return true;
2193      } else if !can_auto_close(&node) {
2194        return false; // could close, then check if parent can contain
2195      } else {
2196        node_opt = node.get_parent();
2197      }
2198    }
2199    false
2200  }
2201
2202  /// Check whether it is possible to close each element in @tags,
2203  /// any intervening nodes must be autocloseable.
2204  /// returning the last Some(node) that would be closed if it is possible,
2205  /// otherwise None
2206  pub fn is_closeable<T: IntoVDQS>(&self, tags: T) -> Option<Node> {
2207    let mut tags: VecDeque<SymStr> = tags.into_vdqs();
2208    let mut node_opt = if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
2209      self.node.get_parent()
2210    } else {
2211      Some(self.node.clone())
2212    };
2213    while let Some(qname) = tags.pop_front() {
2214      'inner: loop {
2215        let node: &Node = match node_opt {
2216          None => break,
2217          Some(ref n) => n,
2218        };
2219        let node_type = node.get_type();
2220        if node_type == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) || node_type.is_none() {
2221          return None;
2222        }
2223        let this_qname = get_node_qname(node);
2224        if this_qname == qname && !is_trivlist(node) {
2225          break 'inner;
2226        }
2227        if !can_auto_close(node) {
2228          Debug!(
2229            "It was impossible to autoclose node: {:?}",
2230            self.document.node_to_string(node)
2231          );
2232          return None;
2233        }
2234        node_opt = node.get_parent();
2235      }
2236      if !tags.is_empty()
2237        && let Some(node) = node_opt
2238      {
2239        node_opt = node.get_parent();
2240      }
2241    }
2242    node_opt
2243  }
2244
2245  /// Close `qname`, if it is closeable — the forgiving counterpart to
2246  /// [`close_element`](Self::close_element).
2247  ///
2248  /// Returns the closed node, or `None` when no such element is open (or it
2249  /// cannot be auto-closed from here). That "or nothing happens" is the point:
2250  /// it lets a binding close an element it *may* have opened without having to
2251  /// track whether it did, where `close_element` would report an error.
2252  pub fn maybe_close_element(&mut self, qname: &str) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
2253    match self.is_closeable(qname) {
2254      Some(node) => {
2255        self.close_node_internal(&node)?;
2256        Ok(Some(node))
2257      },
2258      _ => Ok(None),
2259    }
2260  }
2261
2262  /// Closes all nodes until $node becomes the current point.
2263  pub fn close_to_node(&mut self, node: &Node, ifopen: bool) -> Result<()> {
2264    let mut cant_close = Vec::new();
2265    let mut lastopen: Option<Node> = None;
2266    let mut n = self.node.clone();
2267    let mut n_type = n.get_type();
2268    // go up the tree from current node, till we find `node`
2269    while n_type != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) && &n != node {
2270      if !can_auto_close(&n) {
2271        cant_close.push(n.clone());
2272      }
2273      lastopen = Some(n.clone());
2274      match n.get_parent() {
2275        Some(p) => {
2276          n = p;
2277          n_type = n.get_type();
2278        },
2279        _ => {
2280          break;
2281        },
2282      }
2283    }
2284    // A `ltx:_CaptureBlock_` is a completed BOX (`\parbox`/minipage/`\vbox`
2285    // capture, `insert_block`): tex.web's box completeness — nothing stays
2286    // open across a finished box — so its non-auto-closeable descendants are
2287    // closed BY the box, not reported (the close already happened below; the
2288    // Error was a spurious diagnostic over an identical tree, Perl the same:
2289    // testnumberedblock `numVblock` around `verbatim`, algpseudocodex and
2290    // coloredtheorem `algorithmic` lines in a minipage). Guard:
2291    // `perfect_kernel_batch54::capture_box_closes_its_descendants`.
2292    if is_capture_block(node) {
2293      cant_close.clear();
2294    }
2295    if n_type == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
2296      // Didn't find $node at all!!
2297      // Perl: suppress error when $ifopen is true. Nor when the node's construct never ended:
2298      // it auto-closed already (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #542).
2299      if !ifopen && !node.has_attribute(UNENDED_ATTRIBUTE) {
2300        let message = s!("Attempt to close {:?}, which isn't open", node.get_name());
2301        arena::with(get_node_qname(node), |qname_str| {
2302          {
2303            Error!("malformed", qname_str, message)
2304          };
2305          Ok(())
2306        })?;
2307      }
2308    } else {
2309      // Found node.
2310      if !cant_close.is_empty() {
2311        // But found has intervening non-auto-closeable nodes!!
2312        let qname = get_node_qname(node);
2313        let message = s!(
2314          "Closing {:?} whose open descendents do not auto-close. Descendants are: {:?}",
2315          qname,
2316          cant_close
2317            .into_iter()
2318            .map(|n| n.get_name())
2319            .collect::<Vec<String>>()
2320            .join(",")
2321        );
2322        arena::with(qname, |qname_str| {
2323          {
2324            Error!("malformed", qname_str, message)
2325          };
2326          Ok(())
2327        })?;
2328      }
2329      if let Some(lastopen_node) = lastopen {
2330        self.close_node_internal(&lastopen_node)?;
2331      }
2332    }
2333    Ok(())
2334  }
2335
2336  /// Closes all nodes until $node is closed.
2337  pub fn close_node(&mut self, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
2338    self.close_node_with_strictness(true, node)
2339  }
2340  /// Only if needed/possible: closes all nodes until $node is closed
2341  pub fn maybe_close_node(&mut self, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
2342    self.close_node_with_strictness(false, node)
2343  }
2344
2345  pub fn close_node_with_strictness(&mut self, strict: bool, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
2346    // Perl: my ($t, @cant_close) = (); ... while ((($t = $n->getType) != XML_DOCUMENT_NODE) ...
2347    let mut cant_close: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
2348    let mut n = self.node.clone();
2349    let mut t = n.get_type(); // track walker node type, not target
2350    while t.is_some() && t != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) && &n != node {
2351      if !can_auto_close(&n) {
2352        cant_close.push(n.clone());
2353      }
2354      match n.get_parent() {
2355        Some(parent) => {
2356          n = parent;
2357          t = n.get_type();
2358        },
2359        None => {
2360          t = None; // detached node — stop walking
2361        },
2362      }
2363    }
2364
2365    if is_capture_block(node) {
2366      cant_close.clear(); // box completeness, see `close_to_node`
2367    }
2368    if t == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) || t.is_none() {
2369      // Didn't find $qname at all!! (A node whose construct never ended auto-closed already,
2370      // OXIDIZED_DESIGN #542.)
2371      if strict && !node.has_attribute(UNENDED_ATTRIBUTE) {
2372        let qname = get_node_qname(node);
2373        arena::with(qname, |qname_str| {
2374          let message = s!(
2375            "Attempt to close {}, which isn't open. Currently in {:?}",
2376            qname_str,
2377            self.get_insertion_context(None)?
2378          );
2379          {
2380            Error!("malformed", qname_str, message)
2381          };
2382          Ok(())
2383        })?;
2384      }
2385    } else {
2386      // Found node.
2387      // Intervening non-auto-closeable nodes!!
2388      if !cant_close.is_empty() {
2389        model::with_node_qname(node, |qname| {
2390          let message = s!(
2391            "Closing {} whose open descendents do not auto-close. Descendents are {}",
2392            qname,
2393            cant_close
2394              .iter()
2395              .map(Node::get_name)
2396              .collect::<Vec<String>>()
2397              .join(", ")
2398          );
2399          if strict {
2400            Error!("malformed", qname, message);
2401          } else {
2402            Info!("malformed", qname, message);
2403          }
2404          Ok(())
2405        })?;
2406      }
2407      self.close_node_internal(node)?;
2408    }
2409    Ok(())
2410  }
2411
2412  /// Like [`Self::get_tag_action_list`], but keeps the `_Late` bucket
2413  /// separate. Streaming needs the split: a root's early/normal hooks
2414  /// (structural — the pending-resource drain) run at open as usual, while
2415  /// its `_late` hooks (semantically "with digestion complete" — frontmatter
2416  /// placement, root classes) are deferred to end-of-digestion.
2417  pub fn get_tag_action_list_parts(
2418    &self,
2419    tag: SymStr,
2420    when: TagOptionName,
2421  ) -> (Vec<TagConstructionClosure>, Vec<TagConstructionClosure>) {
2422    use self::tag::TagOptionName::*;
2423    let (when_early, when_late) = match when {
2424      AfterOpen => (Some(AfterOpenEarly), Some(AfterOpenLate)),
2425      AfterClose => (Some(AfterCloseEarly), Some(AfterCloseLate)),
2426      _ => (None, None),
2427    };
2428    let mut prompt = Vec::new();
2429    let mut late = Vec::new();
2430    state::with_tag_property(tag, |tag_hash| {
2431      state::with_tag_property(pin!("ltx:*"), |all_hash| {
2432        let collect =
2433          |bucket: &mut Vec<TagConstructionClosure>, opts: Option<&tag::TagOptions>, key| {
2434            if let Some(v) = opts.and_then(|o| o.get(key)) {
2435              bucket.extend(v.iter().cloned());
2436            }
2437          };
2438        if let Some(when0) = &when_early {
2439          collect(&mut prompt, tag_hash, when0);
2440          collect(&mut prompt, all_hash, when0);
2441        }
2442        collect(&mut prompt, tag_hash, &when);
2443        collect(&mut prompt, all_hash, &when);
2444        if let Some(when1) = &when_late {
2445          collect(&mut late, tag_hash, when1);
2446          collect(&mut late, all_hash, when1);
2447        }
2448      });
2449    });
2450    (prompt, late)
2451  }
2452
2453  /// get the actions that should be performed on afterOpen or afterClose
2454  pub fn get_tag_action_list(
2455    &self,
2456    tag: SymStr,
2457    when: TagOptionName,
2458  ) -> Vec<TagConstructionClosure> {
2459    use self::tag::TagOptionName::*;
2460    // my ($p, $n) = (undef, $tag);
2461    // if ($tag =~ /^([^:]+):(.+)$/) {
2462    //   ($p, $n) = ($1, $2); }
2463    let mut when_early = None;
2464    let mut when_late = None;
2465
2466    match when {
2467      AfterOpen => {
2468        when_early = Some(AfterOpenEarly);
2469        when_late = Some(AfterOpenLate);
2470      },
2471      AfterClose => {
2472        when_early = Some(AfterCloseEarly);
2473        when_late = Some(AfterCloseLate);
2474      },
2475      _ => {},
2476    };
2477
2478    let mut actions = Vec::new();
2479    // Borrow the per-tag and `ltx:*` option hashes in place instead of cloning
2480    // the whole `TagOptions` map twice per call (this runs on every element
2481    // open/close — ~8.8M calls across the witness corpus). We only need to copy
2482    // the matched action lists, and those hold `Rc<>` closures, so cloning each
2483    // is just a pointer + refcount bump. `with_tag_property` returns `None` for
2484    // an absent tag, equivalent to an empty `TagOptions` for a read (the only
2485    // difference vs `get_tag_property` is it skips vivifying an empty default,
2486    // which has no observable effect).
2487    state::with_tag_property(tag, |tag_hash| {
2488      state::with_tag_property(pin!("ltx:*"), |all_hash| {
2489        let mut collect = |opts: Option<&tag::TagOptions>, key: &TagOptionName| {
2490          if let Some(v) = opts.and_then(|o| o.get(key)) {
2491            actions.extend(v.iter().cloned());
2492          }
2493        };
2494        if let Some(when0) = when_early {
2495          collect(tag_hash, &when0);
2496          // ns_hash TODO
2497          collect(all_hash, &when0);
2498        }
2499        collect(tag_hash, &when);
2500        // ns_hash TODO
2501        collect(all_hash, &when);
2502        if let Some(when1) = when_late {
2503          collect(tag_hash, &when1);
2504          // ns_hash TODO
2505          collect(all_hash, &when1);
2506        }
2507      });
2508    });
2509    // return (
2510    //   (($v = $$taghash{$when0}) ? @$v : ()),
2511    //   (($v = $$nshash{$when0})  ? @$v : ()),
2512    //   (($v = $$allhash{$when0}) ? @$v : ()),
2513    //   (($v = $$taghash{$when})  ? @$v : ()),
2514    //   (($v = $$nshash{$when})   ? @$v : ()),
2515    //   (($v = $$allhash{$when})  ? @$v : ()),
2516    //   (($v = $$taghash{$when1}) ? @$v : ()),
2517    //   (($v = $$nshash{$when1})  ? @$v : ()),
2518    //   (($v = $$allhash{$when1}) ? @$v : ()),
2519    //   );
2520    actions
2521  }
2522
2523  pub fn serialize_to_string(&self) -> String {
2524    // This line is to use libxml2's built-in serializer w/indentation heuristic.
2525    // Apparently, libxml2 is giving us "binary" or byte strings which we'd prefer
2526    // to have as text. return decode('UTF-8',
2527    // $self->getDocument->toString($format)); } This uses our own serializer
2528    // emulating libxml2's heuristic indentation.
2529    // This uses our own serializer with the correct schema-based indentation rules:
2530    // noindent_children=true when the element can contain #PCDATA per the schema.
2531    let result = self.serialize_aux(&self.document.as_node(), 0, false, false);
2532    // Trim trailing newline (the root element adds \n after </document>
2533    // but Perl doesn't include it)
2534    result.trim_end_matches('\n').to_string() + "\n"
2535  }
2536
2537  /// We ought to try for something close to C14N (<http://www.w3.org/TR/xml-c14n>),
2538  /// but keep XML declaration, comments and don't convert empty elements.
2539  pub fn serialize_aux(
2540    &self,
2541    node: &Node,
2542    depth: usize,
2543    noindent: bool,
2544    heuristic: bool,
2545  ) -> String {
2546    let mut serialized = String::new();
2547    self.serialize_into(&mut serialized, node, depth, noindent, heuristic);
2548    serialized
2549  }
2550
2551  /// Splice a processed segment's text into `out`, resolving NESTED
2552  /// placeholders recursively (final assembly only). A segment spilled by a
2553  /// closing ancestor keeps its children's `<_spilled_ ref=…/>` markers as
2554  /// literal elements — inlining their text at spill time rebuilt multi-GB
2555  /// segments that pass 2 could not re-materialize. Each literal marker
2556  /// occupies either a full line (`indent + element + newline`, the
2557  /// indenting serialization) or an exact element span (noindent contexts);
2558  /// the inner segment text carries its own indentation/newline, so the
2559  /// marker's surrounding whitespace is dropped — but ONLY when the marker
2560  /// is line-positioned, so content spaces in noindent contexts survive.
2561  /// `<` is escaped everywhere in serialized text/attribute content, so the
2562  /// scan cannot match anything but real markers.
2563  fn splice_segment_text(&self, out: &mut String, text: &str) {
2564    let mut rest = text;
2565    while let Some(pos) = rest.find("<_spilled_ ") {
2566      let (before, from) = rest.split_at(pos);
2567      let Some(elem_end) = from.find("/>").map(|e| e + 2) else {
2568        break; // malformed marker: emit as-is below
2569      };
2570      let elem = &from[..elem_end];
2571      let seg_opt = elem
2572        .split_once("ref=\"")
2573        .and_then(|(_, tail)| tail.split_once('"'))
2574        .and_then(|(num, _)| num.parse::<u32>().ok())
2575        .map(crate::sxml::SegmentId);
2576      let inner = seg_opt.and_then(|seg| {
2577        self
2578          .spill_store
2579          .as_ref()
2580          .and_then(|store| store.read_segment(seg).ok())
2581      });
2582      let Some(inner) = inner else {
2583        emit_error(
2584          "spill",
2585          "unresolved",
2586          &format!("a nested disk-staged segment could not be spliced back ({elem})"),
2587        );
2588        out.push_str(before);
2589        out.push_str("<!-- latexml-oxide: LOST staged segment -->\n");
2590        rest = &from[elem_end..];
2591        continue;
2592      };
2593      // Drop the marker's own line whitespace when line-positioned.
2594      let mut cut = before.len();
2595      while cut > 0 && before.as_bytes()[cut - 1] == b' ' {
2596        cut -= 1;
2597      }
2598      let line_positioned = cut == 0 || before.as_bytes()[cut - 1] == b'\n';
2599      if line_positioned {
2600        out.push_str(&before[..cut]);
2601      } else {
2602        out.push_str(before);
2603      }
2604      self.splice_segment_text(out, &inner);
2605      rest = &from[elem_end..];
2606      if line_positioned && rest.starts_with('\n') {
2607        rest = &rest[1..];
2608      }
2609    }
2610    out.push_str(rest);
2611  }
2612
2613  /// Buffer-threaded core of [`serialize_aux`]. Writes the subtree directly into
2614  /// `out` instead of building (and re-copying) a fresh `String` per node — the
2615  /// recursive return-a-String pattern was the single largest byte source in the
2616  /// allocation profile (~2.8 GB across the witness corpus). Output is identical.
2617  fn serialize_into(
2618    &self,
2619    out: &mut String,
2620    node: &Node,
2621    depth: usize,
2622    noindent: bool,
2623    heuristic: bool,
2624  ) {
2625    // Push `depth` levels of two-space indent without the `"  ".repeat(depth)`
2626    // allocation the old code paid on every call (including text nodes).
2627    fn push_indent(out: &mut String, depth: usize) {
2628      for _ in 0..depth {
2629        out.push_str("  ");
2630      }
2631    }
2632    // `spill_flat` means "emit no decorative whitespace", which is exactly what
2633    // `noindent` already means at every emission site — so fold it in ONCE here
2634    // rather than testing it at each. It suppresses formatting only; the
2635    // schema-driven `noindent_children` still governs mixed content, whose
2636    // whitespace is meaningful and was never indented anyway.
2637    let noindent = noindent || self.spill_flat;
2638
2639    match node.get_type() {
2640      Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) => {
2641        out.push_str("<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n");
2642        if let Some(child) = node.get_first_child() {
2643          self.serialize_into(out, &child, depth, noindent, heuristic);
2644          let mut current_child = child;
2645          while let Some(sibling) = current_child.get_next_sibling() {
2646            self.serialize_into(out, &sibling, depth, noindent, heuristic);
2647            current_child = sibling;
2648          }
2649        }
2650      },
2651      Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => {
2652        // Get the qualified name (prefix:localname) for namespace-prefixed elements
2653        let local_name = node.get_name();
2654        // Streaming assembly: a spill placeholder serializes as the processed
2655        // segment's text, spliced verbatim from disk (same depth/noindent by
2656        // construction — the segment was serialized with the exact values this
2657        // recursion carries here). A placeholder that cannot be resolved is
2658        // LOST CONTENT: flag it loudly in the log AND the output, never drop
2659        // it silently (fail toward flagging).
2660        if local_name == SPILL_PLACEHOLDER && !self.literal_placeholders {
2661          let resolved = self
2662            .spill_store
2663            .as_ref()
2664            .zip(node.get_attribute("ref"))
2665            .and_then(|(store, r)| {
2666              let seg = crate::sxml::SegmentId(r.parse::<u32>().ok()?);
2667              store.read_segment(seg).ok()
2668            });
2669          match resolved {
2670            Some(text) => self.splice_segment_text(out, &text),
2671            None => {
2672              // `Error!` can early-return and this serializer returns `()`,
2673              // so raise through the logger; the marker keeps the loss
2674              // visible in the output itself.
2675              emit_error(
2676                "spill",
2677                "unresolved",
2678                &format!(
2679                  "a disk-staged segment could not be spliced back (ref={:?})",
2680                  node.get_attribute("ref")
2681                ),
2682              );
2683              out.push_str("<!-- latexml-oxide: LOST staged segment -->\n");
2684            },
2685          }
2686          return;
2687        }
2688        // (a literal_placeholders doc falls through: the placeholder is an
2689        // ordinary childless element and serializes as itself)
2690        let tag = if let Some(ns) = node.get_namespace() {
2691          let prefix = ns.get_prefix();
2692          if prefix.is_empty() {
2693            local_name
2694          } else {
2695            s!("{}:{}", prefix, local_name)
2696          }
2697        } else {
2698          local_name
2699        };
2700        let children = node.get_child_nodes();
2701        let mut open_tag = s!("<{tag}");
2702
2703        let nsnodes = node.get_namespace_declarations();
2704        for ns in nsnodes {
2705          let prefix = ns.get_prefix();
2706          let prefix_declaration = if prefix.is_empty() {
2707            s!("xmlns")
2708          } else {
2709            s!("xmlns:{}", prefix)
2710          };
2711          let href = ns.get_href();
2712          write!(open_tag, " {prefix_declaration}=\"{href}\"").ok();
2713        }
2714
2715        let anodes = node.get_attributes();
2716        // `get_attributes()` reports LOCAL names, so an `xml:id` attribute comes
2717        // back keyed as "id" -- by name alone indistinguishable from a genuine
2718        // plain `id`, which the model really does declare (see
2719        // `LaTeXML-bib.rnc:335,353`: `ltx:bib-identifier/@id`,
2720        // `ltx:bib-review/@id`). `get_node_document_qname` resolves the
2721        // attribute's NAMESPACE, so it returns "xml:id" for the former and "id"
2722        // for the latter; SERIALIZE that qname. Ordering stays keyed on the
2723        // local name, which is what the goldens encode (`xml:lang` files under
2724        // "lang", so it precedes `role`), with `xml:id` forced last -- the
2725        // previous code got that by appending it separately, which is also what
2726        // rewrote every plain `id` into an invalid-NCName `xml:id`
2727        // (witness arXiv 2508.17585).
2728        let mut anodes_keys: Vec<(SymStr, &String)> = anodes
2729          .keys()
2730          .map(|key| {
2731            let qname = node
2732              .get_attribute_node(key)
2733              .map(|a| model::get_node_document_qname(&a))
2734              .unwrap_or_else(|| arena::pin(key));
2735            (qname, key)
2736          })
2737          .collect();
2738        // Rank: xmlns:* declarations first (matching Perl's output order), then
2739        // the ordinary attributes by local name, then xml:id last.
2740        let rank = |qname: SymStr, key: &String| -> u8 {
2741          if key.starts_with("xmlns:") {
2742            0
2743          } else if arena::with(qname, |q| q == "xml:id") {
2744            2
2745          } else {
2746            1
2747          }
2748        };
2749        anodes_keys.sort_by(|(a_sym, a_key), (b_sym, b_key)| {
2750          rank(*a_sym, a_key)
2751            .cmp(&rank(*b_sym, b_key))
2752            .then_with(|| a_key.cmp(b_key))
2753        });
2754        for (key_sym, key) in anodes_keys {
2755          // Reuse the value already in `anodes` instead of re-fetching it with
2756          // `get_property` — `get_attributes()` read each value from the
2757          // attribute node directly, so a by-name `xmlGetProp` re-scan (plus a
2758          // fresh `CString` and result `String`) here is pure redundant FFI
2759          // churn (top `get_property` caller in the alloc profile).
2760          let val_serialized = serialize_attr(anodes.get(key).map(String::as_str).unwrap_or(""));
2761          arena::with(key_sym, |key_str| {
2762            write!(open_tag, " {key_str}=\"{val_serialized}\"")
2763          })
2764          .ok();
2765        }
2766
2767        let noindent_children: bool = if heuristic {
2768          // libxml2's heuristic: inline (noindent) if ANY direct child is a text node.
2769          // Crucially, this does NOT propagate the parent's noindent — each element
2770          // independently checks its own children for text nodes.
2771          children
2772            .iter()
2773            .any(|e| e.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode))
2774        } else {
2775          // This is the "Correct" way to determine whether to add indentation
2776          let node_qname = get_node_qname(node);
2777          model::can_contain_sym(node_qname, pin!("#PCDATA"))
2778        };
2779
2780        let noindent_children = noindent_children || self.spill_flat;
2781        if !noindent {
2782          push_indent(out, depth);
2783        }
2784        out.push_str(&open_tag);
2785        // Perl serializes elements with children (including empty text nodes) as
2786        // <tag>...</tag>, and truly childless elements as <tag/>. Match this behavior.
2787        if !children.is_empty() {
2788          // with contents.
2789          out.push('>');
2790          if !noindent_children {
2791            out.push('\n');
2792          }
2793          for child in children {
2794            self.serialize_into(out, &child, depth + 1, noindent_children, heuristic);
2795          }
2796          if !noindent_children {
2797            push_indent(out, depth);
2798          }
2799          write!(out, "</{tag}>").ok();
2800        } else {
2801          // empty element.
2802          out.push_str("/>");
2803        }
2804        if !noindent {
2805          out.push('\n');
2806        }
2807      },
2808      Some(NodeType::TextNode) => {
2809        out.push_str(&serialize_string(&node.get_content()));
2810      },
2811      Some(NodeType::PiNode) => {
2812        // should code this by hand, as well...
2813        if !noindent {
2814          push_indent(out, depth);
2815        }
2816        out.push_str(&self.document.node_to_string(node));
2817        if !noindent {
2818          out.push('\n');
2819        }
2820      },
2821      Some(NodeType::CommentNode) => {
2822        write!(out, "<!-- {}-->", serialize_string(&node.get_content())).ok();
2823      },
2824      _ => {},
2825    }
2826  }
2827
2828  /// Move the current insertion point to `node` — Perl `Document.pm:setNode`
2829  /// L74-87.
2830  ///
2831  /// A document fragment is not itself an insertion point: as in Perl, a
2832  /// single-child fragment is descended into, and a fragment with several
2833  /// children is an error (reported, not fatal — see the body comment on why
2834  /// this returns `()`).
2835  pub fn set_node(&mut self, node: &Node) {
2836    // Perl Document.pm:setNode L74-76: close any open text node first, so its ligatures run — moving the insertion
2837    // point (a `^` float such as a footnote's `<ltx:note>` lifting to the paragraph) abandoned it unligated, and a
2838    // paragraph's text before a `\footnote` kept `‘‘a’’ b--c` (Perl and pdflatex “a” b–c). The error is libxml's
2839    // `set_content` on a live text node, as in every other close. Guard
2840    // `perfect_kernel_batch60::text_before_a_footnote_is_ligatured`.
2841    let _ = self.close_text_internal();
2842    // Perl Document.pm:setNode L77-87: if the candidate is a
2843    // DOCUMENT_FRAG_NODE, validate that it has exactly one child and
2844    // descend to that child. The original Rust port had this check
2845    // commented-out with a wrong-node-type marker (`DocumentNode`
2846    // instead of `DocumentFragNode`); revived with the correct enum.
2847    let mut chosen = node.clone();
2848    if chosen.get_type() == Some(NodeType::DocumentFragNode) {
2849      let children = chosen.get_child_nodes();
2850      // Wrap the Error!/note_status side-effects in an IIFE to swallow the
2851      // `Result<()>` the macro returns (it can early-return Err if the
2852      // MAX_ERRORS cap is hit). `set_node` returns `()` and is called from
2853      // 32 call-sites; threading `Result` through all of them is out of
2854      // scope for an audit-fix. The hot path stays the same; the rare
2855      // hit-the-cap case loses one escape attempt but the next Error!
2856      // anywhere else will trigger the cap regardless.
2857      let _ = (|| -> Result<()> {
2858        if children.len() > 1 {
2859          Error!(
2860            "unexpected",
2861            "multiple-nodes",
2862            "Cannot set insertion point to a DOCUMENT_FRAG_NODE"
2863          );
2864        } else if children.is_empty() {
2865          Error!(
2866            "unexpected",
2867            "empty-nodes",
2868            "Cannot set insertion point to an empty DOCUMENT_FRAG_NODE"
2869          );
2870        }
2871        Ok(())
2872      })();
2873      if let Some(first) = children.into_iter().next() {
2874        chosen = first;
2875      }
2876    }
2877    self.node = chosen;
2878  }
