2880  // Internals
2881  /// Scan for RDFa attributes in the document and set the `prefix` attribute
2882  /// on the root element based on which RDFa prefixes are actually used.
2883  fn set_rdfa_prefixes(&mut self) {
2884    // Collect the RDFa prefix mapping from state
2885    let prefix_map: HashMap<String, String> = state::with_mapping_keys("RDFa_prefixes", |keys| {
2886      let mut map = HashMap::default();
2887      for key_sym in keys {
2888        let key_str = arena::to_string(key_sym);
2889        if let Some(stored) = state::lookup_mapping("RDFa_prefixes", &key_str) {
2890          map.insert(key_str, stored.to_string());
2891        }
2892      }
2893      map
2894    });
2895    if prefix_map.is_empty() {
2896      return;
2897    }
2898
2899    let non_rdf_prefixes: HashSet<&str> = ["http", "https", "ftp"].iter().copied().collect();
2900    let rdf_term_attrs = [
2901      "about", "resource", "property", "typeof", "rel", "rev", "datatype",
2902    ];
2903
2904    // Build XPath to find elements with any RDFa term attribute
2905    let xpath = format!(
2906      "descendant::*[{}]",
2907      rdf_term_attrs
2908        .iter()
2909        .map(|a| format!("@{a}"))
2910        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
2911        .join(" or ")
2912    );
2913
2914    let mut used_prefixes: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();
2915
2916    let nodes = self.findnodes(&xpath, None);
2917    for node in &nodes {
2918      for attr_name in &rdf_term_attrs {
2919        if let Some(value) = node.get_attribute(attr_name) {
2920          for term in value.split_whitespace() {
2921            if let Some(colon_pos) = term.find(':') {
2922              let prefix = &term[..colon_pos];
2923              if !non_rdf_prefixes.contains(prefix) && prefix_map.contains_key(prefix) {
2924                used_prefixes.insert(prefix.to_string());
2925              }
2926            }
2927          }
2928        }
2929      }
2930    }
2931
2932    for prefix in &self.extra_rdfa_prefixes {
2933      if !non_rdf_prefixes.contains(prefix.as_str()) && prefix_map.contains_key(prefix) {
2934        used_prefixes.insert(prefix.clone());
2935      }
2936    }
2937
2938    if !used_prefixes.is_empty()
2939      && let Some(mut root) = self.document.get_root_element()
2940    {
2941      let prefix_str = used_prefixes
2942        .iter()
2943        .map(|p| format!("{}: {}", p, prefix_map[p]))
2944        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
2945        .join(" ");
2946      let _ = root.set_attribute("prefix", &prefix_str);
2947    }
2948  }
2949
2950  pub fn insert_math_token(
2951    &mut self,
2952    text: &str,
2953    mut attributes: HashMap<String, String>,
2954    font_opt: Option<&Font>,
2955  ) -> Result<Node> {
2956    // Perf: avoid allocating the "role" String key unless the entry is missing.
2957    // HashMap::entry() takes an owned K, which forces allocation even on the
2958    // common path where "role" is already present.
2959    if !attributes.contains_key("role") {
2960      attributes.insert(String::from("role"), String::from("UNKNOWN"));
2961    }
2962    // Remove internal-only properties that should not become XML attributes.
2963    // In Perl, these are filtered by canHaveAttribute (model validation),
2964    // but we filter them explicitly here.
2965    attributes.remove("mode");
2966    attributes.remove("isMath");
2967    attributes.remove("cached_width");
2968    attributes.remove("cached_height");
2969    attributes.remove("cached_depth");
2970    attributes.remove(ABSORB_WARNING_PROPERTY);
2971    // attributes.remove("stretchy");
2972
2973    let is_space = attributes.contains_key("isSpace");
2974    let qname = if is_space {
2975      MATH_HINT_NAME
2976    } else {
2977      MATH_TOKEN_NAME
2978    };
2979    let cur_qname = get_node_qname(&self.node);
2980    let text = if is_space && !text.is_empty() && text.chars().all(|c| c.is_whitespace()) {
2981      "" // Make empty hint, of only spaces
2982    } else {
2983      text
2984    };
2985    if qname == MATH_TOKEN_NAME && cur_qname == pin!("ltx:XMTok") {
2986      // Already INSIDE a token!
2987      if !text.is_empty() {
2988        self.open_math_text_internal(text)?;
2989      }
2990    } else {
2991      let mut node = self.open_element(qname, Some(attributes), None)?;
2992      // let tbox  = $attributes{_box} || $LaTeXML::BOX;
2993      let font = match font_opt {
2994        Some(f) => f.clone(),
2995        None => match self.box_to_absorb {
2996          Some(ref tbox) => match tbox.get_font()? {
2997            Some(f) => (*f).clone(),
2998            None => Font::math_default(), // should never happen?
2999          },
3000          None => Font::math_default(), // should never happen?
3001        },
3002      };
3003      self.set_node_font(&mut node, &font)?;
3004      if let Some(ref digested) = self.box_to_absorb {
3005        // TODO: The Rc<Digested> node boxes still have some way to go until they are fully
3006        // ergonomic...
3007        self.set_node_box(&node, digested.clone());
3008      }
3009      if !text.is_empty() {
3010        self.open_math_text_internal(text)?;
3011      }
3012      self.close_node_internal(&node)?; // Should be safe.
3013    }
3014    Ok(self.node.clone())
3015  }
3016
3017  /// Create a libxml2 comment node and attach it to `anchor` according to
3018  /// the supplied Placement. Called from `insert_comment`. Thin wrapper
3019  /// around the safe rust-libxml API (`Node::new_comment` +
3020  /// `add_child`/`add_prev_sibling`) — earlier versions of this method
3021  /// made direct FFI calls, which is now forbidden by the D3b policy.
3022  fn add_comment(document: &XmlDoc, anchor: &Node, comment_text: &str, placement: Placement_) {
3023    let Ok(mut comment) = Node::new_comment(comment_text, document) else {
3024      return;
3025    };
3026    let mut anchor = anchor.clone();
3027    match placement {
3028      Placement_::AppendChild => {
3029        let _ = anchor.add_child(&mut comment);
3030      },
3031      Placement_::PrevSibling => {
3032        let _ = anchor.add_prev_sibling(&mut comment);
3033      },
3034    }
3035  }
3036
3037  /// Insert a new comment, or append to previous comment.
3038  /// Does NOT move the current insertion point to the Comment,
3039  /// but may move up past a text node.
3040  /// Perl: Document.pm lines 678-698
3041  pub fn insert_comment(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<Node> {
3042    let trimmed = text.trim_end();
3043    let clean = DASHES_RE.replace_all(trimmed, "__");
3044    // Perl does NOT close the text node here — it uses getElement() to find
3045    // the nearest element, then inserts the comment relative to element children.
3046    // This preserves self.node as the current text node, so subsequent text
3047    // appends correctly and ligatures fire on the full text run.
3048
3049    let comment_text = s!(" {} ", clean);
3050
3051    if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
3052      Self::add_comment(
3053        &self.document,
3054        &self.node,
3055        &comment_text,
3056        Placement_::AppendChild,
3057      );
3058    } else {
3059      if let Some(node) = self.get_element() {
3060        // Get the nearest element node (Perl: getElement)
3061        let prev = node.get_last_child();
3062        let prevtype = prev.as_ref().and_then(|n| n.get_type());
3063
3064        if prevtype == Some(NodeType::CommentNode) {
3065          // Merge with previous comment
3066          if let Some(mut prev_comment) = prev {
3067            let existing = prev_comment.get_content();
3068            let merged = s!("{}\n     {} ", existing, clean);
3069            prev_comment.set_content(&merged).ok();
3070          }
3071        } else if prevtype == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
3072          let prev_node = prev.unwrap();
3073          // If the node before the text is already a comment, just append new comment
3074          // Otherwise, insert before the text to avoid splitting text runs
3075          let before_text = prev_node.get_prev_sibling();
3076          let before_is_comment =
3077            before_text.as_ref().and_then(|n| n.get_type()) == Some(NodeType::CommentNode);
3078
3079          if before_is_comment {
3080            Self::add_comment(
3081              &self.document,
3082              &node,
3083              &comment_text,
3084              Placement_::AppendChild,
3085            );
3086          } else {
3087            Self::add_comment(
3088              &self.document,
3089              &prev_node,
3090              &comment_text,
3091              Placement_::PrevSibling,
3092            );
3093          }
3094        } else {
3095          Self::add_comment(
3096            &self.document,
3097            &node,
3098            &comment_text,
3099            Placement_::AppendChild,
3100          );
3101        }
3102      }
3103    }
3104    Ok(self.node.clone())
3105  }
3106
3107  // **********************************************************************
3108  // Middle level, mostly public, API.
3109  // Handlers for various construction operations.
3110  // General naming: 'open' opens a node at current pos and sets it to current,
3111  // 'close' closes current node(s), inserts opens & closes, ie. w/o moving
3112  // current
3113
3114  // Tricky: Insert some text in a particular font.
3115  // We need to find the current effective -- being the closest  _declared_ font,
3116  // (ie. it will appear in the elements attributes).  We may also want
3117  // to open/close some elements in such a way as to minimize the font switchiness.
3118  // I guess we should only open/close "text" elements, though.
3119  // [Actually, we'd like the user to _declare_ what element to use....
3120  //  I don't like having "text" built in here!
3121  //  AND, we've assumed that "font" names the relevant attribute!!!]
3122
3123  /// Perl `openText`'s whitespace rule (Document.pm:747-749): whitespace is dropped at the document
3124  /// start and in an element that cannot hold text.
3125  pub fn drops_whitespace_here(&self) -> bool {
3126    match self.node.get_type() {
3127      Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) => true,
3128      Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => !can_contain(&self.node, "#PCDATA"),
3129      _ => false,
3130    }
3131  }
3132
3133  pub fn open_text(&mut self, text: &str, font: &Font) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
3134    let node_type = self.node.get_type();
3135    {
3136      // Ignore initial whitespace
3137      if (text.is_empty() || ONLY_SPACE_RE.is_match(text)) && self.drops_whitespace_here() {
3138        // ...EXCEPT whitespace that is verbatim CONTENT rather than ignorable
3139        // lexical padding: (a) TYPEWRITER-font spaces — fancyvrb/fvextra map
3140        // every verbatim space to a digested space box (`\FV@Space` →
3141        // `\FV@SpaceCatTen`, a braced ordinary space), so the line-LEADING
3142        // indentation of a code block arrives here at a not-yet-opened
3143        // paragraph, and dropping it deleted JSON-schema indentation and
3144        // collapsed space-only verbatim lines out of the height budget
3145        // (2605.00468 Prompt boxes: flush-left schemas, 15-33px frame
3146        // spills); (b) an EXPLICIT control space `\ ` (Box name="space"),
3147        // which TeX always typesets. Line-leading cat-10 SOURCE spaces never
3148        // reach this point (the mouth's state-N skip eats them), so this
3149        // does not resurrect source-formatting whitespace. Same-host Perl
3150        // cannot convert the fancyvrb constructs at all (raw
3151        // fvextra+breaklines exceeds 7 min on a 6-line file) — surpass-Perl
3152        // scope, not a parity break. Fall through: the normal insertion
3153        // machinery auto-opens the paragraph and keeps the spaces as text.
3154        // Not inside SVG, where Perl's rule stands (DIVERGENCES #47): pgf pads
3155        // every protocol literal with a `\space` (pgfsysprotocol.code.tex:33),
3156        // which `\pgfsys@invoke` hands on to digestion (Perl's constructor
3157        // absorbs it the same way, pgfsys-latexml.def.ltxml:832-836), and
3158        // under `\ttfamily` each one opened a whitespace-only
3159        // `svg:foreignObject` — 185 in 2605.01517, 2605.07323, 2605.27124;
3160        // Perl none. A node text's leading `\ ` is dropped there too, as Perl
3161        // drops it; the rendered node is the same. Nor where no auto-opened element reaches text (Perl's rule there
3162        // too): an `{algorithmic}` set in `\ttfamily` (WileyNJDv5.cls:6953 `\algrenewcommand\ALG@beginalgorithmic
3163        // {\ttfamily}`) put the space before its first `\item` straight into the `ltx:listing`, whose model is
3164        // `listingline*` (2608.15322, 2602.03247, 2607.19926: schema-invalid).
3165        let explicit_space = node_type == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
3166          && !text.is_empty()
3167          && can_contain_node_somehow(&self.node, "#PCDATA").is_some()
3168          && (font.family.as_deref() == Some("typewriter")
3169            || self.box_to_absorb.as_ref().is_some_and(|b| {
3170              b.get_property("name")
3171                .is_some_and(|n| n.to_string() == "space")
3172            }))
3173          && !arena::with(get_node_qname(&self.node), |qname| {
3174            qname.starts_with("svg:")
3175          });
3176        if !explicit_space {
3177          return Ok(None);
3178        }
3179        // open_text_internal has its own whitespace-only gate (mirroring
3180        // Perl L1146: insert only if `\S` or direct #PCDATA) — hand it the
3181        // decision so the spaces survive the auto-open.
3182        self.verbatim_space_pending = true;
3183      }
3184    }
3185    if matches!(&font.family.as_deref(), Some("nullfont")) {
3186      return Ok(None);
3187    };
3188    Debug!(
3189      "document",
3190      "open_text",
3191      s!(
3192        "Insert text {:?} at {:?}",
3193        text,
3194        self.document.node_to_string(&self.node)
3195      )
3196    );
3197
3198    // Get the desired font attributes, particularly the desired element
3199    // (usually ltx:text, but let Font override, eg for \emph)
3200    let declared_font = self.get_node_font(&self.node);
3201    let pending_declaration = font.relative_to(declared_font);
3202    let elementname = match pending_declaration.get("element") {
3203      Some((k, _v)) => k,
3204      None => FONT_ELEMENT_NAME,
3205    };
3206    let element_sym = arena::pin(elementname);
3207    // If not at document begin. And not appending text in same font.
3208    //
3209    // Defense-in-depth (issue #217): a current TextNode should always have a
3210    // parent element, so this used to be `self.node.get_parent().unwrap()`.
3211    // Match the `None` instead of unwrapping — if the current node were ever a
3212    // detached text node, skip this un-anchorable insert rather than panic.
3213    // (The macOS corruption that could produce such a node was root-caused
3214    // and fixed in open_text_internal's text-merge detection.)
3215    let text_same_font = if node_type == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
3216      match self.node.get_parent() {
3217        Some(parent) => font.distance(self.get_node_font(&parent)) == 0,
3218        None => return Ok(None),
3219      }
3220    } else {
3221      false
3222    };
3223    if node_type != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) && !text_same_font {
3224      // then we'll need to do some open/close to get fonts matched.
3225      let node = self.close_text_internal()?; // Close text node, if any.
3226      let mut bestdiff = 99;
3227      let rc_node = Rc::new(node);
3228      let mut closeto: Rc<Node> = Rc::clone(&rc_node);
3229      let mut n: Rc<Node> = Rc::clone(&rc_node);
3230      while n.get_type() != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
3231        let node_font = self.get_node_font(&n);
3232        let d = font.distance(node_font);
3233        if d < bestdiff {
3234          bestdiff = d;
3235          closeto = n.clone();
3236          if d == 0 {
3237            break;
3238          }
3239        }
3240        // Stop if not a font element, or if marked _noautoclose, or if
3241        // this is an explicit (non-fontswitch) text wrapper. A constructor-
3242        // opened `<ltx:text class='...'>` (e.g. `\uline{...}`) MUST NOT be
3243        // closed-out-of by a font-distance heuristic just because the parent
3244        // happens to score better — that produces an empty wrapper and
3245        // siblings the inner content (driver: 2402.16319 `\uline{\textbf{2}}`
3246        // inside `\sc` tabular). Only auto-opened fontswitch wrappers are
3247        // safe to walk past.
3248        if get_node_qname(&n) != element_sym
3249          || n.has_attribute("_noautoclose")
3250          || !n.has_attribute("_fontswitch")
3251        {
3252          break;
3253        }
3254        match n.get_parent() {
3255          Some(p) => n = Rc::new(p),
3256          None => break,
3257        }
3258      }
3259
3260      // Move to best starting point for this text.
3261      if *closeto != *rc_node {
3262        self.close_to_node(&closeto, false)?;
3263      }
3264      if bestdiff > 0 {
3265        // Open if needed.
3266        self.open_element(
3267          elementname,
3268          Some(string_map!("_fontswitch" => "true", "_autoopened" => "true")),
3269          Some(font),
3270        )?;
3271      }
3272    }
3273
3274    // Finally, insert the darned text. Before a run in another encoding or family, the open text node's
3275    // ligatures are applied under its own runs' font (`text_run_font`); the node stays open — closing it would
3276    // let libxml merge the next text node into it, out of reach of the ligatures. Each run's ligatures reach only
3277    // that run, from its start in the node: TeX ligates only characters of one font, and a later run's (LMC's
3278    // `”о` → ө) took the closing quote of an earlier one (`a''{\mnr o}`, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #438; witness
3279    // montex/montex).
3280    let previous = self.node.clone();
3281    let ligated = self.ligated_text.take();
3282    let ligated_len = |node: &Node| match &ligated {
3283      Some((ligated_node, len)) if ligated_node == node => *len,
3284      _ => 0,
3285    };
3286    let mut run_start = ligated_len(&previous);
3287    if previous.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode)
3288      && let Some((run_node, run_font, start)) = self.text_run_font.take()
3289      && run_node == previous
3290    {
3291      if run_font.get_encoding() != font.get_encoding()
3292        || run_font.get_family() != font.get_family()
3293      {
3294        self.apply_text_ligatures(&run_font, start)?;
3295        run_start = self.node.get_content().len();
3296      } else {
3297        run_start = start;
3298      }
3299    }
3300    let outnode = self.open_text_internal(text)?;
3301    if outnode.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
3302      // A closed text node the insertion re-entered (`swap_comment_text_if_needed` sets the node back on it) was
3303      // ligated up to where `close_text_internal` left it; a text sibling libxml merged the insertion into
3304      // (`open_text_internal`) holds this run at its end.
3305      let start = if outnode == previous {
3306        run_start
3307      } else {
3308        match &ligated {
3309          Some((ligated_node, len)) if *ligated_node == outnode => *len,
3310          _ => outnode.get_content().len().saturating_sub(text.len()),
3311        }
3312      };
3313      self.text_run_font = Some((outnode.clone(), font.clone(), start));
3314    }
3315    self.record_constructed_node(&outnode);
3316    Ok(Some(outnode))
3317  }
3318
3319  /// The text ligatures (`TEXT_LIGATURES`) whose font test accepts `font`, applied to the open text node from byte
3320  /// `start`, where the run set in `font` begins.
3321  fn apply_text_ligatures(&mut self, font: &Font, start: usize) -> Result<()> {
3322    // Characters set one per box form no ligature: a listing's code (listings' fixed columns, `_noligatures` on its
3323    // lines and inline listings, listings_sty.rs).
3324    let mut ancestor = self.node.get_parent();
3325    while let Some(element) = ancestor {
3326      if element.has_attribute("_noligatures") {
3327        return Ok(());
3328      }
3329      ancestor = element.get_parent();
3330    }
3331    let whole = self.node.get_content();
3332    // A start no longer in the node (its content rewritten before the run) falls back to the whole node.
3333    let start = if whole.is_char_boundary(start) {
3334      start
3335    } else {
3336      0
3337    };
3338    let mut head = whole;
3339    let ocontent = head.split_off(start);
3340    let mut content = Cow::Borrowed(&ocontent);
3341    state::with_value("TEXT_LIGATURES", |value_opt| {
3342      if let Some(Stored::VecDequeStored(ligatures)) = value_opt {
3343        for stored_ligature in ligatures.iter() {
3344          if let Stored::Ligature(ligature) = stored_ligature {
3345            if let Some(ref font_test) = ligature.font_test
3346              && !(font_test)(font)
3347            {
3348              continue; // if the font test fails, skip the ligature
3349            }
3350            content = Cow::Owned((ligature.code.as_ref().unwrap())(&content));
3351          }
3352        }
3353      }
3354    });
3355    if *content != ocontent {
3356      self.node.set_content(&format!("{head}{content}"))?;
3357    }
3358    Ok(())
3359  }
3360
3361  pub fn close_text_internal(&mut self) -> Result<Node> {
3362    if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
3363      // Current node is text? A detached one (a rename's reinsert, a rescue moving away from a dead point) has
3364      // nothing to close into.
3365      let Some(parent) = self.node.get_parent() else {
3366        return Ok(self.node.clone());
3367      };
3368      // The font its runs were inserted with (the last run's), else its parent's, as Perl
3369      // (Document.pm `closeText_internal`).
3370      // Only this node's run entry: a text node opened and closed while another is open (for example a rename's
3371      // reinsert) leaves the outer node's in place.
3372      let (font, start) = match self.text_run_font.take_if(|(node, ..)| *node == self.node) {
3373        Some((_, font, start)) => (font, start),
3374        _ => (self.get_node_font(&parent).clone(), 0),
3375      };
3376      self.apply_text_ligatures(&font, start)?;
3377      self.ligated_text = Some((self.node.clone(), self.node.get_content().len()));
3378      self.node = parent.clone(); // Effectively closed (->setNode, but don't recurse)
3379      Ok(parent)
3380    } else {
3381      Ok(self.node.clone())
3382    }
3383  }
3384
3385  /// Close `node`, and any current nodes below it.
3386  /// No checking! Use this when you've already verified that `node` can be closed.
3387  /// and, of course, `node` must be current or some ancestor of it!!!
3388  pub fn close_node_internal(&mut self, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
3389    let closeto = match node.get_parent() {
3390      Some(p) => p,
3391      None => {
3392        // Node has been detached — nothing to close up to.
3393        return Ok(());
3394      },
3395    };
3396    let mut n = self.close_text_internal()?; // Close any open text node.
3397    while n.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
3398      self.close_element_at(&mut n)?;
3399      self.auto_collapse_children(&mut n)?;
3400      if *node == n {
3401        break;
3402      }
3403      match n.get_parent() {
3404        Some(parent) => {
3405          n = parent;
3406        },
3407        None => {
3408          // Node was detached during close/collapse — bail out safely.
3409          break;
3410        },
3411      }
3412    }
3413    self.set_node(&closeto);
3414    Ok(())
3415  }
3416
3417  /// Avoid redundant nesting of font switching elements:
3418  /// If we're closing a node that can take font switches and it contains
3419  /// a single FONT_ELEMENT_NAME node; pull it up.
3420  fn auto_collapse_children(&mut self, node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
3421    let qname = get_node_qname(node);
3422    if qname != pin!("ltx:_Capture_") {
3423      let mut c = node.get_child_nodes();
3424      // with single child, AND, $node can have all the attributes that the child has (but at least
3425      // "font") BUT, it isn"t being forced somehow
3426      if c.len() == 1
3427        && (get_node_qname(&c[0]) == pin!("ltx:text"))
3428        && model::can_have_attribute(qname, pin!("font"))
3429        && c[0]
3430          .get_attributes()
3431          .keys()
3432          .filter(|x| !x.starts_with('_'))
3433          .all(|v| {
3434            model::can_have_attribute(qname, arena::pin(v))
3435              && !(NON_MERGEABLE_ATTRIBUTES.contains(v.as_str()))
3436          })
3437        && !c[0].has_attribute("_force_font")
3438      {
3439        let c_first = c.pop().unwrap();
3440        let c_first_font = self.get_node_font(&c_first).clone();
3441        self.set_node_font(node, &c_first_font)?;
3442        for mut gc in c_first.get_child_nodes().into_iter() {
3443          gc.unlink();
3444          node.add_child(&mut gc)?;
3445        }
3446        // Re-record ids once, after ALL grandchildren are moved. Calling this
3447        // per-grandchild inside the loop re-scanned the whole growing `node`
3448        // subtree each iteration — O(G²) `descendant-or-self::*[@xml:id]` XPath
3449        // scans per merge (115k scans / ~50% of build wall on a PiCTeX paper).
3450        // record_id_with_node is idempotent for already-correct nodes and the
3451        // final set/document-order is identical, so one post-loop call is
3452        // output-equivalent. See PERFORMANCE.md.
3453        self.record_node_ids(node)?;
3454        // Merge the attributes from the child onto $node
3455        self.merge_attributes(&c_first, node, None)?;
3456        // a TeX box's element merged up (an `\mbox` alone in its paragraph): all `node` holds is that box's material
3457        // (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #715; merge_attributes skips bookkeeping)
3458        if c_first.has_attribute(FIELD_BOX_ATTRIBUTE) {
3459          let _ = node.set_attribute(FIELD_BOX_ATTRIBUTE, "true");
3460        }
3461        self.remove_node(c_first);
3462      }
3463    }
3464    Ok(())
3465  }
3466
3467  pub fn merge_attributes(
3468    &mut self,
3469    from: &Node,
3470    to: &mut Node,
3471    force: Option<&HashSet<&'static str>>,
3472  ) -> Result<()> {
3473    // Key order, so the attributes merged onto `to` land deterministically.
3474    let mut attrs: Vec<(String, String)> = from.get_attributes().into_iter().collect();
3475    attrs.sort();
3476    for (key, val) in attrs.iter() {
3477      // Skip internal attributes
3478      if key.starts_with('_') {
3479        continue;
3480      }
3481      // Normalize key: get_attributes() returns "id" for xml:id attributes.
3482      // Check both "xml:id" and bare "id" with XML namespace for the special case.
3483      let is_xml_id = key.as_str() == "xml:id"
3484        || (key.as_str() == "id"
3485          && from
3486            .get_attribute_ns("id", "http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace")
3487            .is_some());
3488      let effective_key = if is_xml_id { "xml:id" } else { key.as_str() };
3489      let is_forced = force.is_some_and(|f| f.contains(effective_key));
3490      // Special case attributes
3491      if is_xml_id {
3492        // Use the replacement id. record_id_with_node returns a
3493        // deduplicated id when a DIFFERENT node already claims the
3494        // same one; must use the return value, not the original `val`.
3495        let to_has_id = to.has_attribute("xml:id")
3496          || to
3497            .get_attribute_ns("id", "http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace")
3498            .is_some();
3499        if !to_has_id || is_forced {
3500          self.unrecord_id(val);
3501          let deduped = self.record_id_with_node(val, to);
3502          to.set_attribute("xml:id", &deduped)?;
3503        }
3504      } else if MERGE_ATTRIBUTE_SPACEJOIN.contains(key.as_str()) {
3505        self.add_ss_values(to, key, val)?;
3506      } else if MERGE_ATTRIBUTE_SEMICOLONJOIN.contains(key.as_str()) {
3507        if let Some(existing) = to.get_attribute(key) {
3508          let merged = format!("{existing}; {val}");
3509          to.set_attribute(key, &merged)?;
3510        } else {
3511          to.set_attribute(key, val)?;
3512        }
3513      } else if MERGE_ATTRIBUTE_SUMLENGTH.contains(key.as_str()) {
3514        if let Some(val2) = to.get_attribute(key) {
3515          // Parse and sum pt values
3516          let v1 = val.trim_end_matches("pt").parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(0.0);
3517          let v2 = val2.trim_end_matches("pt").parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(0.0);
3518          to.set_attribute(key, &format!("{}pt", v1 + v2))?;
3519        } else {
3520          to.set_attribute(key, val)?;
3521        }
3522      } else if !to.has_attribute(key) || is_forced {
3523        // Else if attribute not present on $to, or if we specifically override it, just copy
3524        to.set_attribute(key, val)?;
3525      }
3526    }
3527    Ok(())
3528  }
3529
3530  fn open_text_internal(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<Node> {
3531    // Consume the verbatim-space handoff (see `verbatim_space_pending`);
3532    // taking it here keeps the flag from leaking into unrelated calls.
3533    let force_whitespace = std::mem::take(&mut self.verbatim_space_pending);
3534    if text.is_empty() {
3535      return Ok(self.node.clone());
3536    }
3537    // Sibling guard to open_math_text_internal: libxml's append_text uses
3538    // CString and panics on embedded NULs (forbidden in XML text per spec).
3539    // Strip them — and the rest of the XML-invalid control class — up-front
3540    // so all downstream append_text calls are safe and the output stays
3541    // well-formed (shared policy with `set_attribute`, see `xml_sanitize`).
3542    if let Cow::Owned(cleaned) = xml_sanitize(text) {
3543      self.verbatim_space_pending = force_whitespace; // re-arm for the recursion
3544      return self.open_text_internal(&cleaned);
3545    }
3546    if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
3547      // current node already is a text node.
3548      Debug!(
3549        "document",
3550        "open_text_internal",
3551        s!(
3552          "Appending text {:?} to {:?}",
3553          text,
3554          self.document.node_to_string(&self.node)
3555        )
3556      );
3557
3558      let parent = self.node.get_parent().unwrap();
3559      if self.box_to_absorb.is_some() && parent.get_attribute("_autoopened").is_some() {
3560        // Perl L1136-1137: appendNodeBox to accumulate boxes for autoopened elements
3561        let bta = self.box_to_absorb.clone().unwrap();
3562        self.append_node_box(&parent, &bta);
3563      }
3564      // K10: under the byte mouth every character reaches the document as
3565      // single-byte boxes (tex.web §1034: one char node per byte; pdfTeX's
3566      // subfont encoding turns the run back into a glyph). The text node is
3567      // that run: reassemble it here, once the new byte is on — the font
3568      // decoding step of a byte-mouth run.
3569      if state::lookup_bool("PDFTEX_BYTE_MOUTH")
3570        && text.chars().any(|c| ('\u{80}'..='\u{FF}').contains(&c))
3571      {
3572        // Only the pending tail (an incomplete sequence's bytes) plus the new
3573        // piece is decoded — re-decoding the whole node per byte was O(n²)
3574        // and, given a runaway feeding one node, a 2^32-byte String
3575        // (chinesechess, sweep 70).
3576        let content = self.node.get_content();
3577        let split = crate::mouth::byte_mouth_pending_tail(&content);
3578        let tail = s!("{}{}", &content[split..], text);
3579        let decoded = crate::mouth::decode_byte_mouth_runs(&tail);
3580        if split == content.len() {
3581          self.node.append_text(&decoded)?;
3582        } else {
3583          self
3584            .node
3585            .set_content(&s!("{}{}", &content[..split], decoded))?;
3586        }
3587      } else {
3588        self.node.append_text(text)?;
3589      }
3590    }
3591    // Perl lines 1139-1144: if lastChild is a comment node and its previous sibling is
3592    // a text node, swap them to avoid splitting text runs, then recurse.
3593    // This avoids libxml text-node merging which would bypass ligature processing.
3594    else if self.swap_comment_text_if_needed(text)? {
3595      // Handled by recursive call
3596    } else if HAS_NONSPACE_RE.is_match(text)
3597      || force_whitespace
3598      || can_contain(&self.node, "#PCDATA")
3599    {
3600      // or text allowed here
3601      let mut point = self.find_insertion_point("#PCDATA", None)?;
3602      // Perl L1149-1150: appendNodeBox for autoopened insertion points
3603      if self.box_to_absorb.is_some() && point.get_attribute("_autoopened").is_some() {
3604        let bta = self.box_to_absorb.clone().unwrap();
3605        self.append_node_box(&point, &bta);
3606      }
3607      Debug!(
3608        "document",
3609        "open_text_internal",
3610        s!(
3611          "Inserting text node for {:?} into {:?}",
3612          text,
3613          self.document.node_to_string(&point)
3614        )
3615      );
3616      let mut node = Node::new_text(text, &self.document)?;
3617      point.add_child(&mut node)?;
3618      // libxml2 MERGES adjacent text nodes: when `point`'s last child was
3619      // already a text node, `xmlAddChild` appends our content to it and
3620      // FREES the just-created `node`, leaving its wrapper dangling.
3621      //
3622      // The previous detection — `node.get_type().is_none()` — is a
3623      // use-after-free: it reads the freed node's `type` field. That is
3624      // *benign on glibc* (the freed slot still reads as the old/None type,
3625      // so the merge is detected), but **unsound on macOS libmalloc**, which
3626      // recycles/scribbles the freed slot so `get_type()` returns garbage
3627      // (EntityNode/ElementDecl/…) and the merge goes UNDETECTED — installing
3628      // a freed node as `self.node` and corrupting the current insertion
3629      // point (issue #217; the macOS-only worker-thread crashes).
3630      //
3631      // Detect the merge WITHOUT dereferencing the possibly-freed node:
3632      // after `add_child` our text is `point`'s last child in both cases
3633      // (the appended `node`, or the sibling it merged into). `Node`'s
3634      // `PartialEq` compares the stored `xmlNodePtr` values (no deref), so
3635      // this pointer-identity check is allocator-independent and UAF-safe.
3636      if point.get_last_child().as_ref() == Some(&node) {
3637        // `node` was appended (not merged) — it is live and current.
3638        self.set_node(&node);
3639      } else if let Some(merged) = point.get_last_child()
3640        && merged.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode)
3641      {
3642        // `node` was merged into a text sibling and freed: that sibling holds the text now and is the current
3643        // node, as the appended node would be (Perl `setNode($node)`, Document.pm openText_internal), so its
3644        // close ligates what was inserted. Leaving the parent current kept the rest of the run out of every
3645        // ligature: text after a formula `cleanup_math` turns into spaces (`500$\,$hPa 1989--2008`) merges into
3646        // the spaces' text node (witnesses nucl-ex0511052, 2208.08472; guard
3647        // `perfect_kernel_batch78a::text_after_a_space_only_formula_is_ligatured`).
3648        self.set_node(&merged);
3649      } else {
3650        self.set_node(&point);
3651      }
3652    }
3653    Ok(self.node.clone())
3654  }
3655
3656  /// Perl lines 1139-1144: Avoid splitting text runs across comments.
3657  /// If the current node's lastChild is a comment and the previous sibling is a text node,
3658  /// swap them so the text node is last, set it as current, and recurse to append new text.
3659  /// Returns true if the swap+append was performed, false otherwise.
3660  fn swap_comment_text_if_needed(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<bool> {
3661    if self.node.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
3662      return Ok(false);
3663    }
3664    if let Some(last_child) = self.node.get_last_child()
3665      && last_child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::CommentNode)
3666      && let Some(mut prev_text) = last_child.get_prev_sibling()
3667      && prev_text.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode)
3668    {
3669      // Swap: move text node after comment node
3670      let mut comment_node = last_child;
3671      comment_node.add_next_sibling(&mut prev_text)?;
3672      // Set current node to the moved text node and recurse. Use
3673      // pointer-identity, not the `prev_text` handle directly:
3674      // `add_next_sibling` of a text node can MERGE it into an adjacent
3675      // text sibling and FREE it (the same libxml2 hazard fixed in
3676      // open_text_internal — benign on glibc, a use-after-free on macOS
3677      // libmalloc, issue #217). The moved/merged text is `comment_node`'s
3678      // next sibling either way; if that is still `prev_text` it survived,
3679      // otherwise `prev_text` was freed — fall back to the live sibling.
3680      match comment_node.get_next_sibling() {
3681        Some(moved) => self.set_node(&moved),
3682        None => self.set_node(&prev_text),
3683      }
3684      self.open_text_internal(text)?;
3685      return Ok(true);
3686    }
3687    Ok(false)
3688  }
3689
3690  /// Perl `appendNodeBox` (Core/Document.pm:1685-1700): record `thisbox` as
3691  /// (part of) the box that created `node`, then do the same for each
3692  /// auto-opened ancestor in turn — an auto-opened node's box is the record of
3693  /// everything opened or written inside it, which is what an auto-opened
3694  /// `ltx:picture` or `svg:foreignObject` measures when it closes. Nothing is
3695  /// added where the box is already the node's, or the last of its
3696  /// `unlist` (Perl `eq`).
3697  ///
3698  /// Perl combines with `List($origbox, $box, mode => $origbox->getProperty
3699  /// ('mode'))` (List.pm:31-55): in horizontal mode one flat list, the boxes
3700  /// of any horizontal list among the two taken in its place; in any other
3701  /// mode a nested pair. A flat list this makes is the node's own
3702  /// (`node_box` property): while no one else holds it, the next box is pushed
3703  /// onto it in place (Perl builds a new list each time, O(n²) in a
3704  /// paragraph); while it is shared, a new one is built, as Perl does.
3705  /// OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #319.
3706  fn append_node_box(&mut self, node: &Node, thisbox: &Digested) {
3707    let mut node = node.clone();
3708    loop {
3709      let key = node.to_hashable();
3710      // Whether the node's box is held only here, read before our own clone.
3711      let (orig, owned) = match self.node_boxes.get(&key) {
3712        None => {
3713          self.node_boxes.insert(key, thisbox.clone());
3714          (None, false)
3715        },
3716        Some(orig) => {
3717          let owned = orig.strong_count() == 1;
3718          (Some(orig.clone()), owned)
3719        },
3720      };
3721      if let Some(orig) = orig {
3722        let already_there = same_box(thisbox, &orig)
3723          || unlist_last(&orig).is_some_and(|last| same_box(thisbox, &last));
3724        if !already_there {
3725          let mode = box_mode(&orig);
3726          if flattens(mode) {
3727            if !(owned && push_onto_node_box(&orig, thisbox)) {
3728              let mut boxes = flatten_horizontal(&orig);
3729              boxes.extend(flatten_horizontal(thisbox));
3730              self.node_boxes.insert(key, node_box_list(boxes, mode));
3731            }
3732          } else {
3733            let list = node_box_list(vec![orig, thisbox.clone()], mode);
3734            self.node_boxes.insert(key, list);
3735          }
3736        }
3737      }
3738      match node.get_parent() {
3739        Some(parent) if is_autoopened_element(&parent) => node = parent,
3740        _ => break,
3741      }
3742    }
3743  }
3744
3745  /// Perl `removeNodeBox` (Core/Document.pm:1704-1723): `thisbox`, the box of
3746  /// a node being removed from `node`, leaves the box of `node` and of each
3747  /// auto-opened ancestor in turn — the whole box if it is `thisbox`, else
3748  /// `thisbox` is dropped from its `unlist` (one level: a box nested deeper
3749  /// is not seen, as Perl notes).
3750  fn remove_node_box(&mut self, node: &Node, thisbox: &Digested) {
3751    let mut node = node.clone();
3752    loop {
3753      let key = node.to_hashable();
3754      if let Some(orig) = self.node_boxes.get(&key).cloned() {
3755        if same_box(&orig, thisbox) {
3756          self.node_boxes.remove(&key);
3757        } else {
3758          let members = unlist(&orig);
3759          if members.iter().any(|b| same_box(b, thisbox)) {
3760            let mode = box_mode(&orig);
3761            let rest: Vec<Digested> = members
3762              .into_iter()
3763              .filter(|b| !same_box(b, thisbox))
3764              .collect();
3765            // Perl `List(@rest, mode => $mode)`: one box of that mode is itself.
3766            let list = if rest.len() == 1 && mode.is_none_or(|m| box_mode(&rest[0]) == Some(m)) {
3767              rest.into_iter().next().unwrap()
3768            } else {
3769              node_box_list(rest, mode)
3770            };
3771            self.node_boxes.insert(key, list);
3772          }
3773        }
3774      }
3775      match node.get_parent() {
3776        Some(parent) if is_autoopened_element(&parent) => node = parent,
3777        _ => break,
3778      }
3779    }
3780  }

3782  // Question: Why do I have math ligatures handled within openMathText_internal,
3783  // but text ligatures handled within closeText_internal ???
3784
3785  /// Needed externally only for the binding generation
3786  fn open_math_text_internal(&mut self, text: &str) -> Result<Node> {
3787    // And if there's already text???
3788    let mut node = self.node.clone();
3789    // my $font = $self->getNodeFont($node);
3790    // libxml's append_text uses CString and panics on embedded NULs. NUL is
3791    // forbidden in XML text per spec anyway, so strip it (and the rest of the
3792    // XML-invalid control class — shared policy with `set_attribute`, see
3793    // `xml_sanitize`). Witness: astro-ph0202376 (a paper that produces math
3794    // tokens with \char0 / NUL bytes embedded in their content). Matches
3795    // Perl's libxml behavior which silently drops NULs in text content.
3796    node.append_text(&xml_sanitize(text))?;
3797    // print STDERR "Trying Math Ligatures at \"$string\"\n";
3798    if !state::get_nomathparse_flag() {
3799      self.apply_math_ligatures(&mut node)?;
3800    }
3801    Ok(node)
3802  }
3803
3804  // New strategy (but inefficient): apply ligatures until one succeeds,
3805  // then remove it, and repeat until ALL (remaining) fail.
3806  fn apply_math_ligatures(&mut self, node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
3807    let checked_out_ligatures = state::checkout_value("MATH_LIGATURES");
3808    if let Some(Stored::VecDequeStored(ref stored_ligatures)) = checked_out_ligatures {
3809      let mut ligatures = stored_ligatures.iter().collect::<VecDeque<_>>();
3810      while !ligatures.is_empty() {
3811        let mut matched = false;
3812        let mut next_ligatures = VecDeque::new();
3813        while !ligatures.is_empty() {
3814          let ligature_stored = ligatures.pop_front().unwrap();
3815          if let Stored::Ligature(ligature) = ligature_stored {
3816            if self.apply_math_ligature(node, ligature)? {
3817              next_ligatures.append(&mut ligatures);
3818              matched = true;
3819              break;
3820            }
3821          } else {
3822            next_ligatures.push_back(ligature_stored);
3823          }
3824        }
3825        ligatures = next_ligatures;
3826        if !matched {
3827          if let Some(value) = checked_out_ligatures {
3828            state::checkin_value("MATH_LIGATURES", value);
3829          }
3830          return Ok(());
3831        }
3832      }
3833    }
3834    if let Some(value) = checked_out_ligatures {
3835      state::checkin_value("MATH_LIGATURES", value);
3836    }
3837    Ok(())
3838  }
3839
3840  /// Apply ligature operation to `node`, presumed the last insertion into it's parent(?)
3841  fn apply_math_ligature(&mut self, node: &mut Node, ligature: &Ligature) -> Result<bool> {
3842    if let Some((nmatched, newstring, attr)) = (ligature.matcher.as_ref().unwrap())(self, node)? {
3843      let mut boxes = VecDeque::new();
3844      boxes.push_front(self.get_node_box(node).unwrap());
3845      node.get_first_child().unwrap().set_content(&newstring)?;
3846      // `nmatched - 1` (usize) underflows to usize::MAX if a matcher returns a
3847      // zero-length match, spinning `get_prev_sibling().unwrap()` until it
3848      // panics. Saturate: a 0/1-length match removes no prior siblings.
3849      // Perl Document.pm:1194-1199: a comment the matcher stepped over (and counted) stays.
3850      // Guard: `perfect_kernel_batch56::letters_ligature_joins_across_a_comment`.
3851      let mut prev = node.clone();
3852      for _idx in 0..nmatched.saturating_sub(1) {
3853        // The matcher can OVER-report nmatched past the actual sibling count
3854        // (the mirror of the zero-length underflow above) — stop instead of
3855        // panicking on the unwrap (PR_READINESS must-fix 5).
3856        let Some(remove) = prev.get_prev_sibling() else {
3857          Error!(
3858            "unexpected",
3859            "ligature",
3860            "Math ligature matched more siblings than exist; truncating the merge"
3861          );
3862          break;
3863        };
3864        if let Some(b) = self.get_node_box(&remove) {
3865          boxes.push_front(b);
3866        }
3867        // The merged token's box is taken out of no enclosing box: it lives on
3868        // in `node`'s composite box below. Perl's `removeNode` here
3869        // (Document.pm:1199) runs `removeNodeBox` on the token's parent, which
3870        // takes the `2` and `.` of a `2.414` out of an aligned cell's box
3871        // list, whose reversion is the cell Math's `tex` (Perl:
3872        // `tex="\displaystyle=414\times 0^{-3}"`; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #272).
3873        // Witnesses 2605.02288, 2605.00812; guard
3874        // `node_box_append::math_ligatures_keep_their_boxes`.
3875        if remove.get_type() == Some(NodeType::CommentNode) {
3876          prev = remove;
3877        } else {
3878          self.remove_node_keeping_box(remove);
3879        }
3880      }
3881      // This fragment replaces the node's box by the composite boxes it replaces
3882      // HOWEVER, this gets things out of sync because parent lists of boxes still
3883      // have the old ones.  Unless we could recursively replace all of them, we'd better skip
3884      // it(??)
3885      if boxes.len() > 1 {
3886        // TODO: Cloning boxes is BAD. What is a better model?
3887        let mut list = List::new(boxes.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>());
3888        list.mode = Some(TexMode::Math);
3889        self.set_node_box(node, list.into());
3890      }
3891      for (key, value_opt) in attr.sorted_each() {
3892        if let Some(value) = value_opt {
3893          node.set_attribute(key, value)?;
3894        } else {
3895          node.remove_attribute(key)?;
3896        }
3897      }
3898      Ok(true)
3899    } else {
3900      Ok(false)
3901    }
3902  }

3904  /// Note that a box has been absorbed creating `node`;
3905  /// This does book keeping so that we can return the sequence of nodes
3906  /// that were added by absorbing material.
3907  pub fn record_constructed_node(&mut self, node: &Node) {
3908    // if ((defined $LaTeXML::RECORDING_CONSTRUCTION)    // If we're recording!
3909    let should_push = match self.constructed_nodes.last() {
3910      // and this node isn't already recorded
3911      None => true,
3912      Some(last_node) => last_node != node,
3913    };
3914    if should_push {
3915      self.constructed_nodes.push(node.clone());
3916    }
3917  }

3919  pub fn filter_deletions(&self, nodes: Vec<Node>) -> Vec<Node> {
3920    // This test seems to successfully determine inclusion,
3921    // without requiring the (dangerous? & dubious?) unbindNode to be used.
3922    match self.document.get_root_element() {
3923      Some(root) => nodes
3924        .into_iter()
3925        .filter(|node| xml::is_descendant_or_self(node, &root))
3926        .collect(),
3927      _ => Vec::new(),
3928    }
3929  }

3931  /// Given a list of nodes such as from ->absorb,
3932  /// filter out all the nodes that are children of other nodes in the list.
3933  pub fn filter_children(&self, mut nodes: Vec<Node>) -> Vec<Node> {
3934    if nodes.is_empty() {
3935      Vec::new()
3936    } else {
3937      let mut new = vec![nodes.remove(0)];
3938      for node in nodes {
3939        if new
3940          .iter()
3941          .all(|other| !xml::is_descendant_or_self(&node, other))
3942        {
3943          new.push(node)
3944        }
3945      }
3946      new
3947    }
3948  }

3950  //**********************************************************************
3951  // Low level internal interface
3952
3953  /// Return a string indicating the path to the current insertion point in the document.
3954  /// if $levels is defined, show only that many levels
3955  pub fn get_insertion_context(&self, levels_opt: Option<usize>) -> Result<String> {
3956    let mut levels = match levels_opt {
3957      None => {
3958        // Default depth is based on verbosity
3959        if state::current_verbosity() <= 1 {
3960          Some(5)
3961        } else {
3962          None
3963        }
3964      },
3965      Some(t) => Some(t),
3966    };
3967    let mut node = self.node.clone();
3968    let node_type = node.get_type();
3969    if node_type != Some(NodeType::TextNode)
3970      && node_type != Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
3971      && node_type != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode)
3972    {
3973      let message = s!(
3974        "Insertion point is not an element, document or text: {:?}",
3975        self.document.node_to_string(&node)
3976      );
3977      Error!("internal", "context", message);
3978      return Ok(String::new());
3979    }
3980    // Build a context path like "<ltx:document><ltx:section><ltx:p>" by walking
3981    // ancestors and prepending each element's qname. Mirrors Perl's
3982    // `Stringify($node)` chain with a depth cap from `levels_opt`.
3983    //
3984    // Cap each qname at 80 chars. Pathological inputs (e.g. xy-pic
3985    // emitting unparsed `\fontdimen 17 \cmr10 at NNsp` strings that
3986    // become element names through a sequence of recovery errors)
3987    // can produce multi-MB qnames; walking 5+ ancestors and
3988    // `format!`-ing each yields a 3.25 GB allocation request that
3989    // OOM-kills the worker. Truncating preserves the diagnostic
3990    // signal ("first 80 chars + …") without the unbounded growth.
3991    // Witness papers: math0203082, math0402448 (R35.B, sandbox).
3992    const QNAME_CAP: usize = 80;
3993    let truncate_qname = |qname: &str| -> String {
3994      if qname.len() <= QNAME_CAP {
3995        qname.to_string()
3996      } else {
3997        let mut s: String = qname.chars().take(QNAME_CAP).collect();
3998        s.push('…');
3999        s
4000      }
4001    };
4002    let qn_for = |n: &Node| -> String {
4003      match n.get_type() {
4004        Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => {
4005          with_node_qname(n, |qname| format!("<{}>", truncate_qname(qname)))
4006        },
4007        Some(NodeType::TextNode) => "#text".to_string(),
4008        Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) => "#document".to_string(),
4009        _ => "?".to_string(),
4010      }
4011    };
4012    let mut path = qn_for(&node);
4013    while let Some(parent_node) = node.get_parent() {
4014      node = parent_node;
4015      if let Some(levels_val) = levels {
4016        levels = Some(levels_val - 1);
4017        if levels_val <= 1 {
4018          path = format!("...{path}");
4019          break;
4020        }
4021      }
4022      path = format!("{}{}", qn_for(&node), path);
4023    }
4024    Ok(path)
4025  }
4026
4027  /// Find the node where an element with qualified name `qname` can be inserted.
4028  /// This will move up the tree (closing auto-closable elements),
4029  /// or down (inserting auto-openable elements), as needed.
4030  pub fn find_insertion_point(
4031    &mut self,
4032    qname: &str,
4033    has_opened_opt: Option<SymStr>,
4034  ) -> Result<Node> {
4035    let qsym = arena::pin(qname);
4036    self.find_insertion_point_qsym(qsym, has_opened_opt)
4037  }
4038
4039  pub fn find_insertion_point_qsym(
4040    &mut self,
4041    qsym: SymStr,
4042    has_opened_opt: Option<SymStr>,
4043  ) -> Result<Node> {
4044    self.close_text_internal()?; // Close any current text node.
4045    let cur_qname = get_node_qname(&self.node);
4046    // If `qname` is allowed at the current point, we're done (a display unit at a quote's run-in block goes on to
4047    // close the quote, `holds_in_quote_block`).
4048    if can_contain_qsym(cur_qname, qsym) && holds_in_quote_block(&self.node, qsym) {
4049      return Ok(self.node.clone());
4050    // Else, if we can create an intermediate node that accepts $qname, we'll do
4051    // that.
4052    } else if let Some(inter) = can_contain_indirect(cur_qname, qsym)
4053      && (inter != qsym)
4054      && (inter != cur_qname)
4055    {
4056      // TODO: can we avoid the clone here? there is a mutability conflict...
4057      let node_font = self.get_node_font(&self.node).clone();
4058      // TODO: avoid this clone?
4059      let inter_string = arena::to_string(inter);
4060      self.open_element(
4061        &inter_string,
4062        Some(string_map!("_autoopened" => "true")),
4063        Some(&node_font),
4064      )?;
4065      // And retry insertion (should work now).
4066      return self.find_insertion_point_qsym(qsym, Some(inter));
4067    }
4068    if let Some(has_opened) = has_opened_opt {
4069      // out of options if already inside an auto-open chain
4070      let message: String =
4071        arena::with2(has_opened, cur_qname, |has_opened_str, cur_qname_str| {
4072          Ok::<String, Error>(format!(
4073            "failed auto-open through <{}> at inadmissible <{}>. Currently in {}",
4074            has_opened_str,
4075            cur_qname_str,
4076            self.get_insertion_context(None)?
4077          ))
4078        })?;
4079      Error!("malformed", arena::to_string(qsym), message);
4080      Ok(self.node.clone()) // But we'll do it anyway, unless Error => Fatal.
4081    } else {
4082      // Now we're getting more desparate...
4083      // Check if we can auto close some nodes, and _then_ insert the `qname`.
4084      let mut node = self.node.clone();
4085      let mut close_to = None;
4086      while (node.get_type() != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode)) && can_auto_close(&node) {
4087        let parent_opt = node.get_parent();
4088        let parent_name = match parent_opt {
4089          None => pin!(""),
4090          Some(ref p) => get_node_qname(p),
4091        };
4092        if sym_can_contain_somehow(parent_name, qsym).is_some()
4093          && parent_opt
4094            .as_ref()
4095            .is_none_or(|p| holds_in_quote_block(p, qsym))
4096        {
4097          close_to = Some(node);
4098          break;
4099        }
4100        // A sectioning unit nested in an unlabelled list item (a margin list's `\item[]`, which opens no inline
4101        // sectional block; an error below) is CLOSED by the next sectioning unit, which becomes its sibling inside the
4102        // item — latex.ltx's `\@startsection` ends the previous heading's scope but not the list (2201.06926; Perl
4103        // nests Y inside X with a second error). OD #189. Guard
4104        // `perfect_kernel_batch64::section_in_margin_list_keeps_bibliography`.
4105        if is_lenient_sectioning_unit(qsym)
4106          && is_lenient_sectioning_unit(get_node_qname(&node))
4107          && parent_name == pin!("ltx:item")
4108        {
4109          close_to = Some(node);
4110          break;
4111        }
4112        node = match parent_opt {
4113          Some(p) => p,
4114          None => break,
4115        };
4116      }
4117      if let Some(close_to_node) = close_to {
4118        self.close_node_internal(&close_to_node)?; // Close the auto closeable nodes.
4119        self.find_insertion_point_qsym(qsym, None) // Then retry, possibly w/auto open's
4120      } else if is_quote_closing_unit(qsym) && self.close_quotes_blocking(&[qsym])? {
4121        // A display sectioning unit in a `{quote}`, `{quotation}` or `{verse}` closed it (`close_quotes_blocking`).
4122        self.find_insertion_point_qsym(qsym, None)
4123      } else {
4124        // Cascading-rejection suppression (2026-05-01): when a math leaf
4125        // element (`<ltx:XMTok>`) tries to insert into a text-mode
4126        // container (`<ltx:p>`/`<ltx:text>`), it's almost always a
4127        // cascade from a previously-rejected math wrapper (XMApp /
4128        // XMDual) — Perl emits the wrapper's rejection error but
4129        // doesn't continue to log per-child cascade errors. Mirror
4130        // that to drop the redundant noise. The Δ=2 witnesses are
4131        // hep-th0101146 (`$$ ... \end{equation}` mismatch) and
4132        // nlin0211024 (`${\mbox M}^{...}$$` inside `\begin{center}`).
4133        // We still return self.node.clone() so the caller proceeds
4134        // (the XMTok still gets inserted illegally, but the schema
4135        // validator will reject the whole math construct on
4136        // serialization anyway — the noise was purely diagnostic).
4137        let qsym_str = arena::to_string(qsym);
4138        let cur_str = arena::to_string(cur_qname);
4139        let is_math_leaf = qsym_str == "ltx:XMTok" || qsym_str == "ltx:XMArg";
4140        // `ltx:emph` added 2026-05-01 after math0010241 triage:
4141        // 13 XMTok-in-emph + 1 (Building line) cascade noise drops
4142        // Rust from 33 → 19, exact parity with Perl=19.
4143        let is_text_container =
4144          cur_str == "ltx:p" || cur_str == "ltx:text" || cur_str == "ltx:emph";
4145        if is_math_leaf && is_text_container {
4146          // Cascading rejection — skip the error log (Perl-faithful).
4147          return Ok(self.node.clone());
4148        }
4149        // Sectioning-unit-in-frontmatter leniency (Perl-faithful). A
4150        // `\paragraph{Keywords.}` / `\paragraph{MSC.}` inside an `abstract`
4151        // (a common author idiom) produces `<ltx:paragraph>` inside
4152        // `<ltx:abstract>`. The RNG `abstract_model = Block.model` excludes
4153        // sectioning units, but Perl's builder inserts it WITHOUT erroring
4154        // (Perl 0 / Rust 2 on 2311.06870) — its output literally nests
4155        // `<ltx:paragraph inlist="toc">` in `<ltx:abstract>`. Mirror that
4156        // build-leniency for the narrow sectioning-into-frontmatter case so
4157        // we don't out-strict Perl. Same `return self.node` "insert anyway"
4158        // mechanism as the math-leaf cascade above.
4159        // A sectioning unit inside a list item or a float body is not lenient here: it opens an
4160        // `ltx:inline-sectional-block` (the bridges below; rulings 2026-10-06, 2026-10-09; OD #189).
4161        let is_sectioning_unit = is_lenient_sectioning_unit(qsym);
4162        // Container is either a frontmatter block (abstract/acknowledgements,
4163        // Block.model — no sectioning units) OR another sectioning unit that
4164        // can't hold it (a 2nd `\paragraph` nests inside the 1st when the
4165        // enclosing abstract can't auto-close to a section level). Perl's
4166        // builder produces exactly this nested `<ltx:paragraph><ltx:paragraph>`
4167        // shape inside `<ltx:abstract>` without erroring (2311.06870: Perl 0).
4168        let is_lenient_container = cur_str == "ltx:abstract"
4169          || cur_str == "ltx:acknowledgements"
4170          || cur_str == "ltx:paragraph"
4171          || cur_str == "ltx:subparagraph";
4172        if is_sectioning_unit && is_lenient_container {
4173          return Ok(self.node.clone());
4174        }
4175        // Auto-open bridges — ONE rule, tex.web has none: when a child cannot
4176        // go here, cannot be reached by any autoOpen path of the model
4177        // (Perl Document.pm:974-1010 `computeIndirectModel`) and the current
4178        // element cannot autoClose, open the container chain that the model
4179        // says would hold it, marked `_autoopened`/`_autoclose` so it closes
4180        // with what it wraps. Perl shares every one of these errors (its only
4181        // autoOpen tags are the model's); the bridges are the documented
4182        // surpasses, one table row each, in precedence order:
4183        //
4184        //   Math: a math node arriving in an INLINE-model element opened
4185        //   while in math mode — `\hyperref[l]{b}`/`\glsdisp{k}{k}` whose
4186        //   content is math (glosmathtools.sty:74 `\ensuremath{\glsdisp…}`;
4187        //   `<ltx:XMTok> isn't allowed in <ltx:glossaryref>`,
4188        //   sample_glosmathtools ×2 53 errors; Perl TeX_Math.pool:42 autoOpens
4189        //   only XMText). Wrapper = inline `ltx:Math`/`ltx:XMath`, the shape
4190        //   `\text{$k$}` already has. Guard:
4191        //   `perfect_kernel_batch54::math_content_in_a_ref_gets_an_inline_math`.
4192        //
4193        //   inline-block: block content in an inline container that cannot
4194        //   auto-close — a `{lstlisting}` in an `l`/`c`/`r` tabular cell or a
4195        //   `{tabbing}` field (engtlc, lexref, expex-glossonly: `<ltx:listing>
4196        //   isn't allowed in <ltx:td>`) — takes the shape the `p{}` column
4197        //   already gives cell blocks (`insert_block`). Only when every direct,
4198        //   auto-open and auto-close route above is exhausted, so a display
4199        //   equation in a paragraph still closes the `ltx:p` (Document.pm:1008;
4200        //   making `inline-block` an autoOpen tag globally would wrap
4201        //   equations instead of closing paragraphs). PLANS P37. Guard:
4202        //   `perfect_kernel_batch54::listing_in_a_tabular_cell_gets_an_inline_block`.
4203        //
4204        //   foreignObject: block content inside an SVG group — a TikZ node
4205        //   whose text holds a `\verb` or a paragraph (makeshape 22, optikz
4206        //   46: `<ltx:p> isn't allowed in <svg:g>`) — takes `svg:foreignObject`,
4207        //   whose model is Flow (LaTeXML-misc.rnc `SVG.foreignObject.content`),
4208        //   the same shape `\lxSVG@includegraphics` uses for non-SVG content
4209        //   (pgfsys-latexml.def.ltxml:202 absorbs the node box into the group
4210        //   directly). OXIDIZED_DESIGN #186, PLANS P37 (svg half). Guard:
4211        //   `perfect_kernel_batch54::verbatim_in_a_tikz_node_gets_a_foreign_object`.
4212        //
4213        //   itemize: a list item stranded outside its list — `\item` digested
4214        //   inside a box whose body `insert_block` captures (`\parbox`/
4215        //   `minipage`/`\vbox` inside a list item: tikz-ext-manual's
4216        //   `{arrowtip}` puts `\tipCompat`'s `\item` in a `minipage` inside a
4217        //   `\pgfmanualentryheadline` item; `<ltx:item> isn't allowed in
4218        //   <ltx:_CaptureBlock_>`). The item is still the enclosing list's
4219        //   `\@item` (latex.ltx's `\@parboxrestore` resets no list bindings),
4220        //   and pdflatex typesets it as a labelled paragraph inside the box;
4221        //   only `ltx:item` is autoOpen (latex_constructs.pool.ltxml:1277), so
4222        //   `computeIndirectModel` has no `_CaptureBlock_`→`item` route.
4223        //   Wrapper = the shape LaTeX gives an item outside its list, an
4224        //   `ltx:itemize`; an item in an inline `\fbox` still reports. Guard:
4225        //   `perfect_kernel_batch56::item_in_a_captured_box_gets_an_itemize`.
4226        //
4227        // A row applies when its own predicate holds, the current element can
4228        // hold the chain's first wrapper and the chain's last wrapper can hold
4229        // the child (both by the model, never by name).
4230        struct AutoOpenBridge {
4231          /// The wrapper chain, outermost first.
4232          chain:    &'static [&'static str],
4233          /// The row's own predicate on (current element, arriving child).
4234          applies:  fn(cur: &str, qsym: &str) -> bool,
4235          /// Extra attributes on the outermost wrapper.
4236          attrs:    &'static [(&'static str, &'static str)],
4237          /// The row's predicate on the current node itself.
4238          holder:   fn(node: &Node) -> bool,
4239          /// Whether the auto-closable elements around the current point close first, up to the outermost one whose
4240          /// parent holds the wrapper (the paragraph a `\trivlist` ends, latex.ltx `\@trivlist`'s `\par`).
4241          close_up: bool,
4242        }
4243        const AUTO_OPEN_BRIDGES: &[AutoOpenBridge] = &[
4244          AutoOpenBridge {
4245            chain:    &["ltx:Math", "ltx:XMath"],
4246            applies:  |_cur, qsym| qsym.starts_with("ltx:XM"),
4247            attrs:    &[("mode", "inline")],
4248            holder:   |_| true,
4249            close_up: false,
4250          },
4251          AutoOpenBridge {
4252            chain:    &["ltx:inline-block"],
4253            applies:  |_cur, qsym| qsym != "ltx:inline-block",
4254            attrs:    &[],
4255            holder:   |_| true,
4256            close_up: false,
4257          },
4258          AutoOpenBridge {
4259            chain:    &["svg:foreignObject"],
4260            applies:  |cur, qsym| cur.starts_with("svg:") && qsym != "svg:foreignObject",
4261            attrs:    &[],
4262            holder:   |_| true,
4263            close_up: false,
4264          },
4265          AutoOpenBridge {
4266            chain:    &["ltx:itemize"],
4267            applies:  |_cur, qsym| qsym == "ltx:item",
4268            attrs:    &[],
4269            holder:   |_| true,
4270            close_up: false,
4271          },
4272          // A sectioning unit in a float body (`\section` in a `figure`, `\subsection` in a `table`; 38 2609 papers,
4273          // 117 errors) opens an `ltx:inline-sectional-block` there: the heading keeps its number in the sequence,
4274          // its id and its labels, as the PDF prints it, and the float stays whole (user ruling 2026-10-06,
4275          // OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #189). The float's own id is fixed before the unit steps the counters it is
4276          // made within (`pin_float_id_before_its_sectioning`).
4277          AutoOpenBridge {
4278            chain:    &["ltx:inline-sectional-block"],
4279            applies:  |cur, qsym| {
4280              matches!(cur, "ltx:figure" | "ltx:table" | "ltx:float")
4281                && is_sectioning_unit_name(qsym)
4282            },
4283            attrs:    &[],
4284            holder:   |_| true,
4285            close_up: false,
4286          },
4287          // …and in a list item (an itemize, enumerate or description item, nested or not; 2304.10050, 2312.11556,
4288          // 2406.02069, 2411.15124, 2412.04099, 2501.07868, 2501.07938, 2511.00839; the TeX Live manuals ddphonism,
4289          // phonrule, prerex, pdfmarginpar) the same block, in a paragraph of the
4290          // item, since an item holds paragraphs only (LaTeXML-block.rnc:257 `item_model = tags?, Para.model`): the
4291          // list stays one list, a later `\item` or the list's end closes the block, and a second heading in the item
4292          // is the first's sibling in it (user ruling 2026-10-09, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #189). Only a labelled
4293          // item: an unlabelled `\item[]` is a margin list's (`changemargin`, `\list{}{…}\item[]`, a whole paper in it:
4294          // 2201.06926, 2505.05767), no list but a margin, whose sections nest as Perl's do, its back matter in the last
4295          // of them — the block would leave the appendix, acknowledgements and bibliography no place. An item's id is
4296          // made when it is digested, before the heading steps any counter. Guards
4297          // `perfect_kernel_batch54::{sectioning_unit_inside_item_or_figure_opens_a_block,
4298          // next_sectioning_unit_in_an_item_is_a_sibling}`.
4299          AutoOpenBridge {
4300            chain:    &["ltx:para", "ltx:inline-sectional-block"],
4301            applies:  |cur, qsym| cur == "ltx:item" && is_sectioning_unit_name(qsym),
4302            attrs:    &[],
4303            holder:   item_has_label,
4304            close_up: false,
4305          },
4306          // …and a run-in `\paragraph` or `\subparagraph` in a `{quote}`, `{quotation}` or `{verse}`: pdflatex sets
4307          // the heading and the text after it, up to the environment's end, inside the quote's `\list` margins
4308          // (article.cls:389-408, `quote` = `\list{}{\rightmargin\leftmargin}\item\relax`), and the quote holds the
4309          // block directly (LaTeXML-block.rnc `quote_model` takes `Misc.class`); the quote's end closes it, and a later
4310          // display unit in the same quote closes the quote (`close_quotes_blocking` above). The display units
4311          // `\part`..`\subsubsection` open no block (`is_quote_closing_unit`; `\begin{quotation}\section*{}` around a
4312          // title page's abstract, 0712.1985). Main-session ruling 2026-10-17, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #678;
4313          // witnesses 2607.27159 2505.18677 2305.11603 1809.03802 2208.14587. Guards `perfect_kernel_batch69a::{
4314          // paragraph_in_a_quote_stays_in_it, section_after_a_paragraph_in_a_quote_closes_it}`.
4315          AutoOpenBridge {
4316            chain:    &["ltx:inline-sectional-block"],
4317            applies:  |cur, qsym| cur == "ltx:quote" && is_run_in_unit_name(qsym),
4318            attrs:    &[],
4319            holder:   |_| true,
4320            close_up: false,
4321          },
4322          AutoOpenBridge {
4323            chain:    &["ltx:item", "ltx:para"],
4324            applies:  |cur, qsym| cur == qsym,
4325            attrs:    &[],
4326            holder:   |_| true,
4327            close_up: false,
4328          },
4329          // A theorem, a proof or a table of contents written inside a container whose model holds no Para.class (a
4330          // `{quote}`, a `\footnote`'s `ltx:note`, a `{wrapfigure}`, a font or color group's `ltx:text`, a tabular
4331          // cell): pdflatex sets it there, inside the container's own box, so it opens an `ltx:inline-logical-block`
4332          // (Misc.class, model Para.model: LaTeXML-para.rnc:77-90), the wrapper `\marginpar` already gives its note
4333          // body (sect09.rs `\lx@marginpar`) — the content stays in place and the schema is unchanged (main-session
4334          // ruling P1 2026-10-17; OXIDIZED_DESIGN #271 keeps the quote model as it is). The `\trivlist` that starts a
4335          // theorem ends the paragraph it meets (latex.ltx `\@trivlist`'s `\par`), so the auto-closable elements around
4336          // the point (the `ltx:p`, a font switch's `ltx:text`) close first, up to the outermost whose parent holds
4337          // the wrapper; a container that cannot auto-close (the note, a constructor's `ltx:text`) keeps it inside.
4338          // Perl shares every one of these errors (same schema, no such autoOpen). Not inside a frontmatter
4339          // container (`ltx:abstract`, `ltx:acknowledgements`, `ltx:keywords`, `ltx:classification`, `ltx:creator`, or
4340          // anything in one): there the "isn't allowed" Error stands, as in Perl, until the frontmatter study is ruled
4341          // on (main-session ruling 2026-10-17; guard `perfect_kernel_batch69c::theorem_in_abstract_is_not_bridged`); a
4342          // kernel table of contents there goes after the container instead (`float_out_of_frontmatter`, OD #753).
4343          // Witnesses 2406.11811, 2103.03402, 0806.0214, 2602.15784, 2301.10544, 1410.7242 (theorem in a quote),
4344          // 1412.2039, math0603642 (TOC in a quote), 2507.09788, 2307.10959, 2308.06338, 2410.15097, 0804.3724,
4345          // math0612590 (theorem in a footnote), 1310.0491 (an ltx:text). Guards
4346          // `perfect_kernel_batch69c::{para_level_block_in_quote_opens_an_inline_logical_block,
4347          // para_level_block_in_note_and_wrapfigure_opens_an_inline_logical_block}`; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #689.
4348          AutoOpenBridge {
4349            chain:    &["ltx:inline-logical-block"],
4350            applies:  |_cur, qsym| matches!(qsym, "ltx:theorem" | "ltx:proof" | "ltx:TOC"),
4351            attrs:    &[],
4352            holder:   outside_frontmatter_container,
4353            close_up: true,
4354          },
4355        ];
4356        for bridge in AUTO_OPEN_BRIDGES {
4357          let first = arena::pin(bridge.chain[0]);
4358          let last = arena::pin(bridge.chain[bridge.chain.len() - 1]);
4359          let applies = arena::with2(cur_qname, qsym, |cur, q| (bridge.applies)(cur, q))
4360            && (bridge.holder)(&self.node);
4361          if applies && bridge.close_up && can_contain_qsym(last, qsym) {
4362            let mut node = self.node.clone();
4363            let mut close_to = None;
4364            while node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) && can_auto_close(&node) {
4365              let Some(parent) = node.get_parent() else {
4366                break;
4367              };
4368              if parent.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
4369                && can_contain_qsym(get_node_qname(&parent), first)
4370              {
4371                close_to = Some(node);
4372              }
4373              node = parent;
4374            }
4375            if let Some(close_to_node) = close_to {
4376              self.close_node_internal(&close_to_node)?;
4377            }
4378          }
4379          let cur_qname = get_node_qname(&self.node);
4380          if applies && can_contain_qsym(cur_qname, first) && can_contain_qsym(last, qsym) {
4381            let node_font = self.get_node_font(&self.node).clone();
4382            for (i, wrapper) in bridge.chain.iter().enumerate() {
4383              let mut attrs = string_map!("_autoopened" => "true", "_autoclose" => "true");
4384              if i == 0 {
4385                for (k, v) in bridge.attrs {
4386                  attrs.insert((*k).to_string(), (*v).to_string());
4387                }
4388              }
4389              self.open_element(wrapper, Some(attrs), Some(&node_font))?;
4390            }
4391            return self.find_insertion_point_qsym(qsym, Some(last));
4392          }
4393        }
4394        // Didn't find a legit place.
4395        // Perl Document.pm:1008-1010: "<qname> isn't allowed in <cur_qname>"
4396        // (a bare qname for #PCDATA), with "Currently in <insertion
4397        // context>" as a SEPARATE Error detail — NOT a Rust backtrace
4398        // (`disabled backtrace`) merged into the user-facing message.
4399        let message = arena::with2(cur_qname, qsym, |cur_qname_str, qname| {
4400          let qname_disp = if qname == "#PCDATA" {
4401            qname.to_string()
4402          } else {
4403            s!("<{}>", qname)
4404          };
4405          s!("{} isn't allowed in <{}>", qname_disp, cur_qname_str)
4406        });
4407        let context = s!("Currently in {}", self.get_insertion_context(None)?);
4408        Error!("malformed", arena::to_string(qsym), message, context);
4409
4410        // But we'll do it anyway, unless Error => Fatal.
4411        Ok(self.node.clone())
4412      }
4413    }
4414  }
4415
4416  fn get_insertion_candidates(&self, node: &Node) -> Vec<Node> {
4417    let mut nodes: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
4418    // Check the current element FIRST, then build list of candidates.
4419    let first = if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
4420      Cow::Owned(node.get_parent().unwrap())
4421    } else {
4422      Cow::Borrowed(node)
4423    };
4424    let is_capture = first.get_name() == "_Capture_";
4425
4426    if first.get_type() != Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) && !is_capture {
4427      nodes.push(first.clone().into_owned());
4428    }
4429
4430    // Collect previous siblings, if node is a text node.
4431    let mut element_node_opt: Option<Cow<Node>> = if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
4432      let mut current_opt = Some(Cow::Borrowed(node));
4433      while let Some(current) = current_opt {
4434        current_opt = current.get_prev_sibling().map(Cow::Owned);
4435        if current.get_name() == "_Capture_" {
4436          nodes.extend(xml::element_nodes(&current));
4437        } else {
4438          nodes.push(current.into_owned());
4439        }
4440      }
4441      node.get_parent().map(Cow::Owned)
4442    } else {
4443      Some(Cow::Borrowed(node))
4444    };
4445    // Now collect (element) node & ancestors
4446    while let Some(element_node) = element_node_opt {
4447      element_node_opt = element_node.get_parent().map(Cow::Owned);
4448      let node_type = element_node.get_type();
4449      if node_type.is_none() || node_type == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
4450        break;
4451      }
4452      if element_node.get_name() == "_Capture_" {
4453        nodes.extend(xml::element_nodes(&element_node));
4454      } else {
4455        nodes.push(element_node.into_owned());
4456      }
4457    }
4458    if is_capture {
4459      nodes.push(first.into_owned());
4460    }
4461
4462    nodes
4463  }

4472

4481      //   .unwrap_or_else(|| {

4483      //       .get_namespace_declarations()

4486      //       .unwrap_or_else(|| {

4491      //         ).unwrap_or_else(|_| {

4494      //             self.document.node_to_string(node),
