4524  //%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
4525  // Document surgery (?)
4526  // %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
4527  // The following carry out DOM modification but NOT relative to any current
4528  // insertion point (eg self.node), but rather relative to nodes specified
4529  // in the arguments.
4530
4531  /// Set any allowed attribute on a node, decoding the prefix, if any.
4532  /// Also records, and checks, any id attributes.
4533  /// \[xml:id and namespaced attributes are always allowed\]
4534  ///
4535  /// "Allowed" is the document model's call, so this is not a plain libxml
4536  /// write: an attribute the schema does not permit on `node` is dropped rather
4537  /// than emitted, which is what keeps a binding from producing a document that
4538  /// fails validation.
4539  pub fn set_attribute(&mut self, node: &mut Node, key: &str, value: &str) -> Result<()> {
4540    // Sanitize BEFORE the empty check: a value of only invalid chars (e.g. a
4541    // lone NUL) must degrade to the skip path, not reach libxml. Without this
4542    // an interior NUL panics in libxml's `CString::new(value).unwrap()`
4543    // (node.rs:639) and aborts the whole conversion — witness `$a^^@b$`-class
4544    // stray NULs (BibTeX `\"u`-mangling) reaching the `tex=` reversion
4545    // attribute now that NUL's catcode is 12/OTHER like Perl. The text sinks
4546    // (`open_text_internal`/`open_math_text_internal`) already stripped NUL;
4547    // this attribute sink did not. PR #249 review P0-1.
4548    let value_sanitized = xml_sanitize(value);
4549    // `class` is a list of NMTOKENs (LaTeXML-common.rng:94) and `xml:id` an
4550    // XML Name (:120); the ONE emitter every writer funnels through
4551    // (`add_ss_values` too) makes them so — user ruling 2026-09-18, beyond
4552    // Perl, which emits listings' `ltx_lst_language_{TeX}_LaTeX` / `C++` /
4553    // an unexpanded `\lexer@cs`, raw `\lx@add@class` `@` names, fontawesome's
4554    // `fa-*`, and csvsimple-legacy's `\par` leaking into a class and an id
4555    // (33 manuals, 3,488 jing lines; 2 manuals, 1,231). A value that is
4556    // already valid is untouched.
4557    let value_sanitized: Cow<'_, str> = match key {
4558      "class" => Cow::Owned(nmtokens_clean(&value_sanitized)),
4559      "xml:id" if !is_xml_name(&value_sanitized) => {
4560        Cow::Owned(crate::common::cleaners::clean_id(&value_sanitized))
4561      },
4562      _ => value_sanitized,
4563    };
4564    let value: &str = &value_sanitized;
4565    if value.is_empty() {
4566      return Ok(()); // skip if empty
4567    }
4568    // Normalise the key first, then run Perl's plain `setAttribute`
4569    // (`Core/Document.pm:1370-1386`): schema-check, then the LITERAL `xml:id`
4570    // test. The normalisation is needed because this port spells `xml:id` as a
4571    // bare `id` throughout its property/attribute maps -- the math parser,
4572    // `base_xmath`, alignment rows and `RefStepID`'s `#id` all do it, where
4573    // Perl's constructors always write `xml:id` out in full -- so a bare `id`
4574    // arriving here normally MEANS `xml:id`. The exception is that `id` is ALSO
4575    // a real attribute in the model: `LaTeXML-bib.rnc:335,353` declare
4576    // `attribute id { text }?` on `ltx:bib-identifier` and `ltx:bib-review`,
4577    // carrying the ISSN/DOI/MR identifier itself. Letting the alias apply
4578    // unconditionally rewrote those into invalid-NCName ids
4579    // (`xml:id="0010-3640,1097-0312"`) -- witness arXiv 2508.17585.
4580    let key = if key == "id" && !model::can_have_attribute(get_node_qname(node), arena::pin("id")) {
4581      "xml:id"
4582    } else {
4583      key
4584    };
4585    // Accept internal attributes (starting with _), namespaced (containing :), and model-allowed.
4586    if !key.starts_with('_') && !key.contains(':') {
4587      let qname = get_node_qname(node);
4588      if !model::can_have_attribute(qname, arena::pin(key)) {
4589        return Ok(()); // silently skip attributes not allowed by schema
4590      }
4591    }
4592    if key == "xml:id" {
4593      // record_id_with_node detects duplicates and returns a
4594      // deduplicated id when a DIFFERENT node already claims the
4595      // same id. Previously we discarded that return value and
4596      // wrote the original `value`, which meant libxml2 saw two
4597      // nodes with the same xml:id. The post-processing scan's
4598      // libxml2 idHash lookups then ran O(n²) on any document
4599      // with enough duplicates (see 1106.1389 / KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
4600      // #13: 14 duplicate-id sites from \addtocounter{equation}{-1}
4601      // + \subequations inside a \newtheorem[equation] theorem).
4602      let deduped = self.record_id_with_node(value, node);
4603      node.set_attribute("xml:id", &deduped)?;
4604    } else if !key.contains(':') {
4605      // No colon; no namespace (the common case!)
4606      // Note: Full model validation (can_have_attribute) is done in node_set_attribute.
4607      // Here we just set the attribute, since the caller is responsible for filtering.
4608      node.set_attribute(key, value)?;
4609    } else {
4610      // Namespaced attribute (`prefix:local`). Mirror Perl
4611      // `Core/Document.pm::setAttribute`, whose `getDocumentNamespacePrefix($ns, 1)`
4612      // *promotes* the prefix's namespace to a document namespace on first use.
4613      // That lets finalize's `apply_document_namespace_declarations` declare
4614      // `xmlns:prefix` on the root, so the prefixed attribute resolves into its
4615      // namespace on serialization and the post XSLT can copy it (e.g.
4616      // `data:sourcepos` → `data-sourcepos`). Without the promotion a code-only
4617      // namespace (like `data`, used by `--source-map`) is emitted unbound and
4618      // dropped. General over any registered prefix — implements the decodeQName
4619      // TODO. (`aria`/schema namespaces are already document namespaces, so the
4620      // re-registration is an idempotent no-op for them.)
4621      if let Ok((Some(ns_uri), _local)) = model::decode_qname(key) {
4622        let prefix = key.split(':').next().unwrap_or("");
4623        model::register_document_namespace(prefix, Some(&ns_uri));
4624      }
4625      node.set_attribute(key, value)?;
4626    }
4627    // ... TODO: continue (see Perl)
4628    Ok(())
4629  }
4630
4631  pub fn add_ss_values(&mut self, node: &mut Node, key: &str, values_str: &str) -> Result<()> {
4632    // $values = $values->toAttribute if ref $values;
4633    if !values_str.is_empty() {
4634      // Skip if `empty'; but 0 is OK!
4635      let mut values: Vec<&str> = values_str.split_whitespace().collect();
4636      if let Some(oldvalues) = node.get_attribute(key) {
4637        // previous values?
4638        let mut old: Vec<&str> = oldvalues.split_whitespace().collect();
4639        for new in values {
4640          if old.iter().all(|v| *v != new) {
4641            old.push(new);
4642          }
4643        }
4644        old.sort_unstable();
4645        self.set_attribute(node, key, &old.join(" "))?;
4646      } else {
4647        values.sort_unstable();
4648        self.set_attribute(node, key, &values.join(" "))?;
4649      }
4650    }
4651    Ok(())
4652  }

4654  /// Add one or more CSS classes to a node, without disturbing the ones it
4655  /// already carries.
4656  ///
4657  /// `class` is treated as the space-separated set it is
4658  /// ([`add_ss_values`](Self::add_ss_values)), so several bindings can each
4659  /// contribute a class to the same element — which is why this exists rather
4660  /// than a plain `setAttribute("class", …)`, and what
4661  /// [`remove_ss_values`](Self::remove_ss_values) undoes.
4662  pub fn add_class(&mut self, node: &mut Node, class: &str) -> Result<()> {
4663    self.add_ss_values(node, "class", class)
4664  }
4665
4666  /// Remove space-separated values from an attribute.
4667  /// Perl: sub removeSSValues (Document.pm lines 1423-1437)
4668  pub fn remove_ss_values(&mut self, node: &mut Node, key: &str, values: &str) {
4669    let to_remove: Vec<&str> = values.split_whitespace().collect();
4670    if to_remove.is_empty() {
4671      return;
4672    }
4673    if let Some(current) = node.get_attribute(key) {
4674      let updated: Vec<&str> = current
4675        .split_whitespace()
4676        .filter(|v| !to_remove.contains(v))
4677        .collect();
4678      if updated.is_empty() {
4679        let _ = node.remove_attribute(key);
4680      } else {
4681        let mut sorted = updated;
4682        sorted.sort_unstable();
4683        node
4684          .set_attribute(key, &sorted.join(" "))
4685          .unwrap_or_default();
4686      }
4687    }
4688  }
4689
4690  /// Remove CSS class from element.
4691  /// Perl: sub removeClass (Document.pm lines 1439-1442)
4692  pub fn remove_class(&mut self, node: &mut Node, class: &str) {
4693    self.remove_ss_values(node, "class", class);
4694  }

4696  /// Float to a node that can accept the given attribute.
4697  /// Returns the previous node so it can be restored after setting the attribute.
4698  /// Perl: sub floatToAttribute (Document.pm lines 1080-1092)
4699  pub fn float_to_attribute(&mut self, key: &str) -> Option<Node> {
4700    let candidates = self.get_insertion_candidates(&self.node);
4701    for candidate in candidates {
4702      let qname_sym = get_node_qname(&candidate);
4703      if sym_can_have_attribute(qname_sym, arena::pin(key)) {
4704        let savenode = self.node.clone();
4705        self.set_node(&candidate);
4706        return Some(savenode);
4707      }
4708    }
4709    Warn!(
4710      "malformed",
4711      key,
4712      s!("No open node can get attribute '{}'", key)
4713    );
4714    None
4715  }

4717  /// Check if a node is currently open (i.e., is or contains the current node).
4718  /// Perl: sub isOpen (Document.pm lines 1998-2006)
4719  pub fn is_open(&self, node: &Node) -> bool {
4720    if *node == self.node {
4721      return true;
4722    }
4723    for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
4724      if self.is_open(&child) {
4725        return true;
4726      }
4727    }
4728    false
4729  }
4730
4731  //**********************************************************************
4732  // Association of nodes and ids (xml:id)
4733
4734  /// Records the association of the current Document `node` with the `id`,
4735  /// which should be the `xml:id` attribute of the `node`.
4736  /// Usually this association will be maintained by the methods
4737  /// that create nodes or set attributes.
4738  fn record_id(&mut self, id: &str) -> String {
4739    let needs_modify = if let Some(prev) = self.idstore.get(id) {
4740      // Whoops! Already assigned!!!
4741      // Can we recover?
4742      self.node != *prev
4743    } else {
4744      false
4745    };
4746    let final_id = if needs_modify {
4747      let badid = id.to_string();
4748      let new_id = self.modify_id(badid);
4749      Info!(
4750        "malformed",
4751        "id",
4752        s!("Duplicated attribute xml:id. Using id='{}'", new_id)
4753      );
4754      new_id
4755    } else {
4756      id.to_string()
4757    };
4758    self.idstore.insert(final_id.clone(), self.node.clone());
4759    final_id
4760  }
4761
4762  /// Records the association of the given `node` with the `id`,
4763  /// which should be the `xml:id` attribute of the `node`.
4764  /// Usually this association will be maintained by the methods
4765  /// that create nodes or set attributes.
4766  fn record_id_with_node(&mut self, id: &str, node: &Node) -> String {
4767    let prev_opt = if let Some(prev) = self.idstore.get(id) {
4768      // Whoops! Already assigned!!!
4769      // Can we recover? Only conflict if a DIFFERENT node already has this id.
4770      if node != prev {
4771        Some(prev.clone())
4772      } else {
4773        None
4774      }
4775    } else {
4776      None
4777    };
4778    // The spilled half: an id that left the idstore with a spilled fragment
4779    // is just as taken (its node is on disk, not in the tree).
4780    let spilled_collision = prev_opt.is_none() && self.spilled_ids.contains(id);
4781    let final_id = if spilled_collision {
4782      let new_id = self.modify_id(id.to_owned());
4783      Debug!(
4784        "malformed",
4785        "id",
4786        s!(
4787          "Duplicated attribute xml:id. Using id='{}' on <{}> id='{}' already set on a disk-staged fragment",
4788          new_id,
4789          arena::to_string(get_node_qname(node)),
4790          id
4791        )
4792      );
4793      new_id
4794    } else if let Some(prev) = prev_opt {
4795      let badid = id;
4796      let new_id = self.modify_id(id.to_owned());
4797      // Concise node descriptions, mirroring Perl `Stringify($node)`
4798      // (Common/Object.pm L40-49: `<tag attrs…>` with no child
4799      // serialization). Rust previously dumped the FULL node via
4800      // `node_to_string`, which (a) diverged from Perl's concise form and
4801      // (b) spilled child TEXT into the log — e.g. a figure caption
4802      // beginning "Error bars are the standard deviations…" then appears as
4803      // a line starting "Error" and is mis-counted as an error by
4804      // text-grep error sweeps (false positive on 2009.01426, which has
4805      // ZERO real errors). Use just the qname (+ the relevant id), which is
4806      // what an id-dedup diagnostic actually needs.
4807      let message = s!(
4808        "Duplicated attribute xml:id. Using id='{}' on <{}> id='{}' already set on <{}>",
4809        new_id,
4810        arena::to_string(get_node_qname(node)),
4811        badid,
4812        arena::to_string(get_node_qname(&prev))
4813      );
4814      // Perl-faithful (Document.pm L1454): Info-level. The id-counter
4815      // collision is the dedup-recovery path (`modify_id` appends
4816      // suffix), not silent corruption. The earlier Error-level
4817      // promotion was motivated by 1410.8171 (Sárkány PRA), but root-
4818      // cause investigation showed the empty-S3+ rendering there was
4819      // the siunitx ExplodeText! tokenization bug (fixed by
4820      // fc2aae7266), not the dedup recovery. After that fix, the
4821      // residual dedup events on the canvas are SHARED with Perl —
4822      // the in-tree test fixture tests/math/declare.xml itself bakes
4823      // in the `xml:id="S1.Ex1.m1.2a"` dedup result, confirming
4824      // Perl produces the same behavior. Downstream broken XMRefs
4825      // (post-dedup) emit Warning:expected:node "No node found with
4826      // id=…" which already surfaces the consequence at the appro-
4827      // priate severity. Math-parser hygiene fix (preventing the
4828      // collision in the first place) is tracked separately.
4829      Debug!("malformed", "id", message);
4830      new_id
4831    } else {
4832      id.to_string()
4833    };
4834    self.idstore.insert(final_id.clone(), node.clone());
4835    final_id
4836  }
4837
4838  pub fn unrecord_id(&mut self, id: &str) { self.idstore.remove(id); }
4839
4840  /// Guardian-safe unlink: walk `node`'s subtree invalidating every `xml:id`
4841  /// idstore entry, then detach it from its parent. Use this in preference
4842  /// to a raw `node.unlink()` anywhere the node *might* carry an `xml:id`
4843  /// (subtree reshuffles in math-parser, post-processing cleanup, etc.),
4844  /// to prevent the dangling-Node class of bug that produced the 1605.08055
4845  /// Finalizing-phase SIGSEGV (see SYNC_STATUS.md D3b).
4846  ///
4847  /// This is the unlink-only half of `remove_node` — it does **not** adjust
4848  /// `self.node` / the insertion point, which is correct for callers that
4849  /// intend to re-parent the unlinked subtree elsewhere (the common case).
4850  /// Callers that want the insertion-point bookkeeping should use
4851  /// `remove_node` instead.
4852  pub fn safe_unlink(&mut self, mut node: Node) {
4853    if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
4854      if let Some(id) = node.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
4855        self.unrecord_id(&id);
4856      }
4857      for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
4858        self.remove_node_aux(child);
4859      }
4860    }
4861    node.unlink();
4862  }
4863
4864  /// These are used to record or unrecord, in bulk, all the ids within a node (tree).
4865  ///
4866  /// When `record_id_with_node` detects a duplicate it renames the id (e.g.
4867  /// `X.1.mf` → `X.1.mfa`). Any sibling `<ltx:XMRef idref="X.1.mf"/>` in the
4868  /// same subtree would otherwise become a dangling reference for the post-
4869  /// processor. After re-recording IDs, sweep the subtree once and update any
4870  /// XMRef whose `idref` matches an entry in the rename map.
4871  ///
4872  /// Perl `Core::Document::recordNodeIDs` (Document.pm L1466-1472) has the
4873  /// same latent bug — recording renames but XMRefs aren't touched. The bug
4874  /// surfaces in our port because the math-parser path
4875  /// (`parser.rs::install_replacements`-style `unrecord+record` round-trips)
4876  /// is denser than Perl's; both end up needing this remap to keep XMRef
4877  /// chains intact. Intentional surpass-Perl divergence; tracked in
4878  /// SYNC_STATUS Task #10.
4879  pub fn record_node_ids(&mut self, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
4880    use rustc_hash::FxHashMap;
4881    let mut rename: FxHashMap<String, String> = FxHashMap::default();
4882    for mut idnode in self.findnodes("descendant-or-self::*[@xml:id]", Some(node)) {
4883      if let Some(id) = idnode.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
4884        let newid = self.record_id_with_node(&id, &idnode);
4885        if newid != id {
4886          idnode.set_attribute("xml:id", &newid)?;
4887          rename.insert(id, newid);
4888        }
4889      }
4890    }
4891    if !rename.is_empty() {
4892      for mut xmref in self.findnodes("descendant-or-self::*[@idref]", Some(node)) {
4893        if let Some(idref) = xmref.get_attribute("idref")
4894          && let Some(new) = rename.get(&idref)
4895        {
4896          xmref.set_attribute("idref", new)?;
4897        }
4898      }
4899    }
4900    Ok(())
4901  }
4902
4903  /// Makes the SVG ids under `root` unique in the document, as the svg schema types them
4904  /// (svg-core-attrib.rng:26-28). A picture TeX copies — `\copy`, `\usebox`, expl3's `\box_use:N`
4905  /// (tex.web:20952 copies a node list with its whatsits verbatim) — writes the ids the pgf driver
4906  /// fixed at digestion (pgfsys-latexml.def.ltxml:346-352, :678-714) once per copy; PDF has no ids,
4907  /// XML must not repeat them (suanpan-l3: 9,480 jing lines; thuaslogos: copies nested in one
4908  /// picture). Walks `root` in document order: an SVG element's `id` already handed out (or held by
4909  /// an `xml:id`) is renamed with the next free suffix, and every reference — `url(#X)` in any
4910  /// attribute, `href`/`xlink:href` `#X` — binds to the latest preceding definition of X under
4911  /// `root`; a reference to a definition elsewhere is left alone.
4912  ///
4913  /// A walked element is marked (`_svgid`, a bookkeeping attribute finalize strips): the math
4914  /// parser re-creates a picture where it moves it (`append_tree`), each re-creation closing a new
4915  /// `svg:svg` — the mark travels with the copied attributes, so a moved picture keeps its ids and
4916  /// references, where an unmarked one is a new copy. `append_clone` (the alignment split's MathFork,
4917  /// the frontmatter writer's contacts and notes) instead makes a second copy beside the original: it
4918  /// copies the svg `id` as Perl does and drops the mark, so the copy's own walk renames the ids it
4919  /// repeats (guard `perfect_kernel_batchne7::tikz_badges_in_frontmatter_contacts_keep_svg_ids`). A picture keeps Perl's
4920  /// ids unless an earlier element already holds them (a relocated footnote copy can). Perl writes
4921  /// the duplicates (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #391); the id map follows its `appendClone`
4922  /// (Document.pm:1920-1956). Guards: `perfect_kernel_batch57::copied_pictures_keep_unique_svg_ids`,
4923  /// `perfect_kernel_batch57::rebuilt_math_pictures_keep_their_svg_ids`.
4924  pub fn record_svg_ids(&mut self, root: &Node) -> Result<()> {
4925    use rustc_hash::FxHashMap;
4926    if root.get_attribute("_svgid").is_some() {
4927      return Ok(());
4928    }
4929    let mut in_effect: FxHashMap<String, String> = FxHashMap::default();
4930    for mut node in self.findnodes("descendant-or-self::*", Some(root)) {
4931      let is_svg = with_node_qname(&node, |qname| qname.starts_with("svg:"));
4932      if !is_svg {
4933        continue;
4934      }
4935      let walked = node.get_attribute("_svgid").is_some();
4936      if !walked {
4937        node.set_attribute("_svgid", "1")?;
4938      }
4939      if let Some(id) = node.get_attribute_no_ns("id") {
4940        let taken = !walked
4941          && (self.svg_ids.contains(&id)
4942            || self.idstore.contains_key(&id)
4943            || self.spilled_ids.contains(&id));
4944        let effective = if taken {
4945          let candidate = self.next_svg_id(&id);
4946          node.set_attribute("id", &candidate)?;
4947          candidate
4948        } else {
4949          id.clone()
4950        };
4951        self.svg_ids.insert(effective.clone());
4952        in_effect.insert(id, effective);
4953      }
4954      if in_effect.is_empty() {
4955        continue;
4956      }
4957      // `xlink:href` is set as a literal prefixed name until finalize declares the namespace
4958      // (`Document::set_attribute`), so the local name is the part after the prefix.
4959      for ((name, ns), value) in node.get_properties_ns() {
4960        let rebound = if value.contains("url(#") {
4961          let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len());
4962          let mut rest = value.as_str();
4963          while let Some(at) = rest.find("url(#") {
4964            out.push_str(&rest[..at + 5]);
4965            rest = &rest[at + 5..];
4966            let end = rest.find(')').unwrap_or(rest.len());
4967            let target = &rest[..end];
4968            out.push_str(in_effect.get(target).map_or(target, String::as_str));
4969            rest = &rest[end..];
4970          }
4971          out.push_str(rest);
4972          out
4973        } else if name.rsplit(':').next() == Some("href")
4974          && let Some(target) = value.strip_prefix('#')
4975          && let Some(new) = in_effect.get(target)
4976        {
4977          s!("#{}", new)
4978        } else {
4979          continue;
4980        };
4981        if rebound != value {
4982          match ns {
4983            Some(ns) => node.set_attribute_ns(&name, &rebound, &ns)?,
4984            None => node.set_attribute(&name, &rebound)?,
4985          }
4986        }
4987      }
4988    }
4989    Ok(())
4990  }
4991
4992  /// The next free SVG id for a repeat of `id`: `id` with a `radix_alpha` suffix, as `modify_id`
4993  /// makes them, free of every SVG id, `xml:id` and spilled id.
4994  fn next_svg_id(&mut self, id: &str) -> String {
4995    let mut n = self.svg_id_suffixes.get(id).copied().unwrap_or(1);
4996    loop {
4997      let candidate = s!("{}{}", id, radix_alpha(n));
4998      n += 1;
4999      if !self.svg_ids.contains(&candidate)
5000        && !self.idstore.contains_key(&candidate)
5001        && !self.spilled_ids.contains(&candidate)
5002      {
5003        self.svg_id_suffixes.insert(id.to_string(), n);
5004        return candidate;
5005      }
5006    }
5007  }
5008
5009  pub fn unrecord_node_ids(&mut self, node: &Node) {
5010    for idnode in self.findnodes("descendant-or-self::*[@xml:id]", Some(node)) {
5011      if let Some(id) = idnode.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
5012        self.unrecord_id(&id);
5013      }
5014    }
5015  }
5016
5017  //**********************************************************************
5018  // Streaming (fragmented) conversion: spill closed subtrees to disk.
5019
5020  /// Spill closed subtrees to the segment store, freeing their DOM memory
5021  /// (streaming pass 1).
5022  ///
5023  /// Walks the SPINE — root element down to the current insertion element —
5024  /// and, at every level, spills the runs of closed element children that
5025  /// precede the open (spine) child: serialize in the pre-finalize form with
5026  /// the exact `(depth, noindent)` the eager serializer would use, write to
5027  /// `store`, record every spilled `xml:id`/label in `index`, purge the
5028  /// pointer-keyed registries (`idstore` via `unrecord_id`, `node_boxes` by
5029  /// key — freed nodes' pointers can be REUSED, so a stale entry is not just
5030  /// dangling but can mis-associate a box with a future node), replace the
5031  /// run with one `<_spilled_ ref="N"/>` placeholder, and unlink+free the
5032  /// nodes. Serialization at assembly time splices the processed segment
5033  /// where the placeholder sits, so document order, nesting and
5034  /// spine-attribute finality are preserved by construction.
5035  ///
5036  /// Two deliberate exclusions:
5037  /// * ROOT-level children spill only when sectional (`ROOT_SPILLABLE`):
5038  ///   the frontmatter fallback and `maybe_promote_leading_title` operate on
5039  ///   the leading non-sectional root children at end-of-build.
5040  /// * An open element's heading parts (`ltx:tags`, `ltx:title`, `ltx:toctitle`) never spill: its close-time
5041  ///   hooks read them (a bibliography taking the place of the unit that heads it, latexml_engine sect11.rs
5042  ///   `absorb_bibliography_heading`). One title per open element, so the memory cost is negligible.
5043  ///
5044  /// Returns the number of runs spilled.
5045  pub fn spill_closed_subtrees(&mut self, index: &mut crate::sxml::FragmentIndex) -> Result<usize> {
5046    debug_assert!(
5047      self.spill_store.is_some(),
5048      "spill_closed_subtrees needs the store attached (set_spill_store)"
5049    );
5050    let Some(root) = self.document.get_root_element() else {
5051      return Ok(0);
5052    };
5053    // The spine, root-first. The insertion point may be a text node; start
5054    // from its nearest element.
5055    let mut spine: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
5056    let mut cursor = if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
5057      Some(self.node.clone())
5058    } else {
5059      self.node.get_parent()
5060    };
5061    while let Some(n) = cursor {
5062      if n.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
5063        break;
5064      }
5065      cursor = n.get_parent();
5066      spine.push(n);
5067    }
5068    spine.reverse();
5069    if spine.is_empty() && self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
5070      // The ROOT itself has closed (`\end{document}` absorbed): everything
5071      // under it is a closed subtree now, so the spine is just the root and
5072      // every eligible child may spill. Without this case the FINAL spill of
5073      // a streaming conversion silently no-ops — the witness kept 27,400
5074      // formulae live into the spine tail this way and died there.
5075      spine.push(root.clone());
5076    }
5077    if spine.first() != Some(&root) {
5078      // The insertion point is outside the tree under the root: nothing is
5079      // safely classifiable as closed.
5080      return Ok(0);
5081    }
5082    let namespaces: Vec<(String, String)> = root
5083      .get_namespace_declarations()
5084      .iter()
5085      .map(|ns| (ns.get_prefix(), ns.get_href()))
5086      .collect();
5087    let aligning = Self::pending_aligning_context();
5088
5089    let mut runs_spilled = 0usize;
5090    // Every spine level INCLUDING the insertion element itself: at a legal
5091    // yield seam the insertion point routinely IS the root (between
5092    // top-level constructs), where a levels-above-only walk sees an empty
5093    // spine range and spills NOTHING — the witness leaked two thirds of its
5094    // chapters into the spine tail exactly this way. The insertion element's
5095    // children are complete, closed subtrees at a seam (the constructed-node
5096    // stacks expire between absorbs); its level simply has no barrier child.
5097    for level in 0..spine.len() {
5098      let parent = spine[level].clone();
5099      let barrier = spine.get(level + 1).cloned();
5100      // The serializer's recursion contract for children of `parent`
5101      // (`serialize_into`: depth+1, parent's schema-driven noindent).
5102      let noindent = {
5103        let parent_qname = get_node_qname(&parent);
5104        model::can_contain_sym(parent_qname, pin!("#PCDATA"))
5105      };
5106      // Do NOT spill the sole `ltx:text` child of an open `ltx:text` frame: that
5107      // is exactly the `auto_collapse_children` pattern (a redundant font/frame
5108      // wrapper merged into its parent at close). Spilling the child first leaves
5109      // the still-open frame with a `<_spilled_/>` placeholder, so the close-time
5110      // collapse sees a non-`ltx:text` child and skips the merge the EAGER path
5111      // performs — the streamed output then nests where eager collapses, breaking
5112      // the byte-identity invariant (witness: a `breaklines=true` framed
5113      // `Verbatim` whose parbox layer crosses a fragment seam, issue #702). The
5114      // protected node is a small wrapper; keeping it resident until the frame
5115      // closes costs negligible memory. Conservative on purpose: it also spares a
5116      // few wrappers `auto_collapse` would NOT merge (`_force_font` /
5117      // non-mergeable attr), which stay nested in BOTH paths anyway.
5118      let parent_is_collapse_frame = get_node_qname(&parent) == pin!("ltx:text") && {
5119        let elem_kids: Vec<Node> = parent
5120          .get_child_nodes()
5121          .into_iter()
5122          .filter(|c| {
5123            c.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) && c.get_name() != SPILL_PLACEHOLDER
5124          })
5125          .collect();
5126        elem_kids.len() == 1 && get_node_qname(&elem_kids[0]) == pin!("ltx:text")
5127      };
5128      let mut run: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
5129      let pending_from = Self::pending_alignment_from(&parent, &aligning);
5130      let mut pending = matches!(pending_from, Some(None));
5131      for child in parent.get_child_nodes() {
5132        if Some(&child) == barrier.as_ref() {
5133          break;
5134        }
5135        // `prev` itself predates the declaration and may spill; its
5136        // followers may not.
5137        let is_pending_anchor = pending_from
5138          .as_ref()
5139          .is_some_and(|prev| prev.as_ref() == Some(&child));
5140        let eligible = child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
5141          && child.get_name() != SPILL_PLACEHOLDER
5142          && !pending
5143          && !parent_is_collapse_frame
5144          && (level > 0 || ROOT_SPILLABLE.contains(&child.get_name().as_str()))
5145          // A bibliography pins its subtree in RAM: a LATER `\bibstyle`
5146          // writes attributes onto it through a doc-wide search (sweep
5147          // witness tests/structure/bibsect.tex). Rare and small.
5148          && self
5149            .findnodes("descendant-or-self::ltx:bibliography", Some(&child))
5150            .is_empty()
5151          // (`parent` is open: its heading stays until it closes)
5152          && !matches!(
5153            get_node_qname(&child),
5154            q if q == pin!("ltx:tags") || q == pin!("ltx:title") || q == pin!("ltx:toctitle")
5155          )
5156          // The unit right before the bibliography still open (the barrier) stays too: closing, the
5157          // bibliography may take its place (latexml_engine sect11.rs `absorb_bibliography_heading`).
5158          && !barrier.as_ref().is_some_and(|open| {
5159            get_node_qname(open) == pin!("ltx:bibliography")
5160              && child.get_next_element_sibling().as_ref() == Some(open)
5161          });
5162        if eligible {
5163          run.push(child);
5164        } else {
5165          if !run.is_empty() {
5166            // A non-eligible node interrupts the run: flush what precedes it so
5167            // each placeholder replaces exactly the contiguous nodes it stands
5168            // for, and document order is preserved around the interloper.
5169            runs_spilled += self.spill_run(&mut run, level + 1, noindent, &namespaces, index)?;
5170          }
5171          // A closed NON-sectional root child stays resident for the
5172          // frontmatter heuristics, but only its prose is read: spill the
5173          // rest of it (`spill_prose_free_children`).
5174          let resident_root_child = level == 0
5175            && child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
5176            && child.get_name() != SPILL_PLACEHOLDER
5177            && !ROOT_SPILLABLE.contains(&child.get_name().as_str())
5178            && !ROOT_FRONTMATTER.contains(&child.get_name().as_str());
5179          if resident_root_child {
5180            runs_spilled +=
5181              self.spill_prose_free_children(&child, level + 2, &namespaces, &aligning, index)?;
5182          }
5183        }
5184        if is_pending_anchor {
5185          pending = true;
5186        }
5187      }
5188      if !run.is_empty() {
5189        runs_spilled += self.spill_run(&mut run, level + 1, noindent, &namespaces, index)?;
5190      }
5191    }
5192    Ok(runs_spilled)
5193  }
5194
5195  /// `ROOT_SPILLABLE` keeps a non-sectional root-level child resident for the
5196  /// end-of-build frontmatter heuristics (`maybe_promote_leading_title`,
5197  /// `maybe_dedup_leading_title_ink` in `base_utilities.rs`), which read the
5198  /// text and font of the leading `ltx:p` paragraphs and nothing else. So its
5199  /// closed element children that hold no prose paragraph spill like any other
5200  /// closed subtree — a paragraph inside drawn content (an `svg:foreignObject`
5201  /// label under `ltx:picture`) is not document prose. A child that does hold
5202  /// prose stays resident and is walked the same way, so a wrapper
5203  /// (`ltx:quote`, `ltx:logical-block`) keeps its paragraphs and sheds its
5204  /// pictures, tables and equations; an `ltx:p` itself is kept whole.
5205  ///
5206  /// Witness: pgf-PeriodicTable's eight sectionless `\pgfPT` tables (one
5207  /// `ltx:para > ltx:picture` each) climbed ~106 MB per table under
5208  /// `--streaming` with every picture-end seam honored, because nothing under
5209  /// a root-level `ltx:para` ever spilled and the sweep of `node_boxes` found
5210  /// every table's boxes still live.
5211  fn spill_prose_free_children(
5212    &mut self,
5213    parent: &Node,
5214    depth: usize,
5215    namespaces: &[(String, String)],
5216    aligning: &Option<(Node, Option<Node>)>,
5217    index: &mut crate::sxml::FragmentIndex,
5218  ) -> Result<usize> {
5219    let noindent = model::can_contain_sym(get_node_qname(parent), pin!("#PCDATA"));
5220    let mut runs_spilled = 0usize;
5221    let mut run: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
5222    let mut resident: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
5223    let pending_from = Self::pending_alignment_from(parent, aligning);
5224    let mut pending = matches!(pending_from, Some(None));
5225    for child in parent.get_child_nodes() {
5226      if pending_from
5227        .as_ref()
5228        .is_some_and(|prev| prev.as_ref() == Some(&child))
5229      {
5230        // `prev` itself predates the declaration and may spill; its followers
5231        // may not.
5232        pending = true;
5233      }
5234      // Only content the schema admits directly in a paragraph block
5235      // (`ltx:para` = Block/Misc/Meta: pictures, tabulars, equations, nested
5236      // blocks) may become a segment root: pass 2 re-parses a segment under
5237      // the `_lxfragment` wrapper, whose schema decisions cannot host inline
5238      // content (a spilled `ltx:sup` from a root-level `ltx:note` failed
5239      // there: tests/cluster_regressions/frontmatter_spconf_name).
5240      let is_element = child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
5241        && child.get_name() != SPILL_PLACEHOLDER
5242        && model::can_contain_sym(pin!("ltx:para"), get_node_qname(&child));
5243      // Prose = an `ltx:p` outside any picture that holds non-space text
5244      // outside any picture. A text-less `ltx:p` — an inline centered picture
5245      // closing under `ltx:para > ltx:p > ltx:text > ltx:picture` (no `\par`
5246      // inside the paragraph; pgf-spectra LSE emits 141 spectra that way) —
5247      // is never a leading-title candidate (`maybe_dedup_leading_title_ink`
5248      // needs alphabetic text) and spills whole like a bare picture would.
5249      // Matching the `ltx:p` itself kept every such paragraph resident and
5250      // pinned its digested boxes in `node_boxes` (163,636 entries, ~4.4 GB
5251      // of the 4.8 GB fuse on LSE); guard
5252      // `inline_pictures_in_paragraphs_stay_memory_bounded`.
5253      let holds_prose = is_element && subtree_holds_prose(&child);
5254      let eligible = is_element
5255        && !holds_prose
5256        && !pending
5257        && self
5258          .findnodes("descendant-or-self::ltx:bibliography", Some(&child))
5259          .is_empty();
5260      if eligible {
5261        if std::env::var_os("LXML_TRACE_NODE_BOXES").is_some() {
5262          eprintln!(
5263            "streaming: prose-free spill of {} under {}",
5264            child.get_name(),
5265            parent.get_name()
5266          );
5267        }
5268        run.push(child);
5269        continue;
5270      }
5271      if !run.is_empty() {
5272        runs_spilled += self.spill_run(&mut run, depth, noindent, namespaces, index)?;
5273      }
5274      if holds_prose && !pending && get_node_qname(&child) != pin!("ltx:p") {
5275        resident.push(child);
5276      }
5277    }
5278    if !run.is_empty() {
5279      runs_spilled += self.spill_run(&mut run, depth, noindent, namespaces, index)?;
5280    }
5281    for wrapper in resident {
5282      runs_spilled +=
5283        self.spill_prose_free_children(&wrapper, depth + 1, namespaces, aligning, index)?;
5284    }
5285    if runs_spilled > 0 {
5286      self.release_wrapper_boxes(parent);
5287    }
5288    Ok(runs_spilled)
5289  }
5290
5291  /// The pending aligning context, if any: `\centering`/`\raggedright`/
5292  /// `\raggedleft` record the current element and its last child
5293  /// (`setup_aligning_context`, latex_constructs/mod.rs) and stamp the class
5294  /// on that element's LATER children when the group ends
5295  /// (`apply_aligning_context`). Those children are not closed yet.
5296  fn pending_aligning_context() -> Option<(Node, Option<Node>)> {
5297    let node = state::with_value("ALIGNING_NODE", |v| match v {
5298      Some(Stored::Node(n)) => Some(n.clone()),
5299      _ => None,
5300    })?;
5301    let prev = state::with_value("ALIGNING_PREV_CHILD", |v| match v {
5302      Some(Stored::Node(p)) => Some(p.clone()),
5303      _ => None,
5304    });
5305    Some((node, prev))
5306  }
5307
5308  /// For `parent` under a pending aligning context: `Some(prev)` when the
5309  /// context's children after `prev` (all of them for `Some(None)`) are still
5310  /// to be stamped and must stay resident. Spilling them frees the anchor, and
5311  /// a later node allocated at the same address matched it instead
5312  /// (tikz-network under tufte-book: `ltx_align_left` moved from the title
5313  /// block and the first chapter to a later chapter and an appendix).
5314  fn pending_alignment_from(
5315    parent: &Node,
5316    aligning: &Option<(Node, Option<Node>)>,
5317  ) -> Option<Option<Node>> {
5318    aligning
5319      .as_ref()
5320      .filter(|(node, _)| node == parent)
5321      .map(|(_, prev)| prev.clone())
5322  }
5323
5324  /// A resident wrapper's recorded box owns what was just spilled beneath it:
5325  /// every element a constructor opens records the SAME whatsit
5326  /// (`set_node_box` on `ltx:para`, `ltx:p`, `ltx:picture`, `svg:svg` alike),
5327  /// so dropping the spilled nodes' entries frees nothing while the wrapper's
5328  /// entry still holds the picture whatsit and, through it, the whole box tree
5329  /// (the n8 witness kept every table alive this way: the sweep found the
5330  /// wrappers live, and their box was the table). Drop the entries of the
5331  /// wrapper and its ancestors below the root; the root's own box (the
5332  /// `\begin{document}` whatsit) owns no body content. A wrapper's box is
5333  /// consulted only while it is the insertion point's ancestor, which a closed
5334  /// root-level child never is again.
5335  fn release_wrapper_boxes(&mut self, wrapper: &Node) {
5336    let mut cursor = Some(wrapper.clone());
5337    while let Some(n) = cursor {
5338      if n.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) || get_node_qname(&n) == pin!("ltx:document") {
5339        break;
5340      }
5341      self.node_boxes.remove(&n.to_hashable());
5342      cursor = n.get_parent();
5343    }
5344  }
5345
5346  /// Spill one contiguous run of closed sibling elements as a single segment.
5347  /// Consumes (drains) `run`; on success the nodes are unlinked and freed.
5348  /// Serialized-bytes ceiling per SEGMENT. A spill run is chunked so no
5349  /// segment exceeds it (approximately — a single oversized subtree still
5350  /// becomes one segment): pass 2 re-materializes a segment WHOLE, so the
5351  /// segment size bounds pass-2 peak memory the way the yield budget bounds
5352  /// pass 1. The witness's first RSS-triggered yield once spilled half the
5353  /// document as ONE 512 MB segment, and pass 2 died re-parsing it.
5354  fn segment_chunk_bytes() -> usize {
5355    // Calibration override (`LATEXML_SEGMENT_CHUNK_MIB`), deliberately env-only
5356    // and NOT a CLI flag — the same reasoning as `LATEXML_SPILL_AT_MIB`, and
5357    // for the same reason: MAX below is an ARGUED constant, not a measured one.
5358    //
5359    // Its stated basis is a TIME claim ("the point past which a single
5360    // segment's re-parse dominates pass 2"), but the pass-2 tail is linear in
5361    // fragment size — `prune_dangling_split_xmrefs`, `prune_xmduals`,
5362    // `mark_xmnode_visibility` and `cleanup_unreferenced_xmtok_ids` are each
5363    // one `findnodes` plus an O(1)-per-node loop, `finalize_subtree` is a
5364    // recursive walk, and the rewrite rule set is fixed. Larger segments
5365    // should also SUIT the allocator, which is the largest single profile
5366    // category (~16.5%): fewer, bigger alloc/free cycles.
5367    //
5368    // Note what the derivation below wants: at --max-memory 48000 it computes
5369    // watermark/72 = 166 MB and MAX then clamps it to 32 MB. This knob exists
5370    // so that ceiling can be swept rather than argued.
5371    if let Some(mib) = std::env::var("LATEXML_SEGMENT_CHUNK_MIB")
5372      .ok()
5373      .and_then(|v| v.parse::<usize>().ok())
5374      .filter(|mib| *mib > 0)
5375    {
5376      return mib.saturating_mul(1024 * 1024);
5377    }
5378    /// Validated on the 131 MB witness. The accompanying claim that a single
5379    /// segment's re-parse dominates pass 2 past this point is NOT substantiated
5380    /// by the pass-2 tail, which is linear — see the override above.
5381    const MAX: usize = 32 * 1024 * 1024;
5382    /// Below this, per-segment overhead (parse, index merge, reserialize)
5383    /// outweighs the memory saved.
5384    const MIN: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
5385    /// Serialized bytes → live DOM, measured: 18.6 MB of core XML
5386    /// materialized as ~1,346 MB of libxml2 DOM on a witness slice.
5387    const DOM_EXPANSION: u64 = 72;
5388    match crate::stomach::spill_watermark_bytes() {
5389      // Pass 2 re-materializes ONE segment whole, so a chunk must fit the
5390      // same watermark pass 1 respects — otherwise the phase that exists to
5391      // bound memory becomes the phase that blows it on a small machine.
5392      Some(watermark) => ((watermark / DOM_EXPANSION) as usize).clamp(MIN, MAX),
5393      None => MAX,
5394    }
5395  }
5396
5397  fn spill_run(
5398    &mut self,
5399    run: &mut Vec<Node>,
5400    depth: usize,
5401    noindent: bool,
5402    namespaces: &[(String, String)],
5403    index: &mut crate::sxml::FragmentIndex,
5404  ) -> Result<usize> {
5405    use crate::sxml::SegmentMeta;
5406    // An element whose children are exclusively EMPTY text nodes serializes
5407    // as `<p></p>` — indistinguishable, after a parse round-trip, from a
5408    // childless `<p/>`. Mark such elements before serializing so pass 2 can
5409    // restore the empty text child and keep the round-trip exact (sweep
5410    // witness tests/fonts/abxtest.tex).
5411    fn mark_empty_text_elements(node: &Node) {
5412      if node.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
5413        return;
5414      }
5415      let children = node.get_child_nodes();
5416      if !children.is_empty()
5417        && children
5418          .iter()
5419          .all(|c| c.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) && c.get_content().is_empty())
5420      {
5421        let mut n = node.clone();
5422        let _ = n.set_attribute("_lx_empty_text", "1");
5423      }
5424      for child in children {
5425        mark_empty_text_elements(&child);
5426      }
5427    }
5428    for node in run.iter() {
5429      mark_empty_text_elements(node);
5430    }
5431    if let Some(observe) = self.spill_observer {
5432      for node in run.iter() {
5433        observe(self, node);
5434      }
5435    }
5436    // Stamp the DIGESTED BOX's math-font verdict on XMArg elements before
5437    // their boxes are purged: the FLOATSUPERSCRIPT rewrite (tex_math.rs)
5438    // decides `<text font="italic">` wrapping from the box font's family,
5439    // and a fragment re-materialized in pass 2 has no boxes. An attr carries
5440    // the EXACT verdict (an ancestor-`_font` approximation mis-wrapped
5441    // text-mode superscripts — sweep witness tests/math/niceunits.tex).
5442    for node in run.iter() {
5443      for mut xmarg in self.findnodes("descendant-or-self::ltx:XMArg", Some(node)) {
5444        if let Some(tbox) = self.get_node_box(&xmarg)
5445          && let Ok(Some(font)) = tbox.get_font()
5446          && font
5447            .get_family()
5448            .map(|f| f.as_ref() == "math")
5449            .unwrap_or(false)
5450        {
5451          let _ = xmarg.set_attribute("_boxfont_math", "1");
5452        }
5453      }
5454    }
5455
5456    // What eager finalize reads above the run, for pass 2: the font it declares there, and the element it mints the
5457    // run's id-less top nodes under (2507.13358).
5458    let spill_parent = run.first().and_then(|n| n.get_parent());
5459    let context_font = spill_parent.as_ref().map(|parent| {
5460      let font = self.finalize_context_font(parent);
5461      let key = font.to_hashable();
5462      self.node_fonts.entry(key).or_insert(font);
5463      key.to_string()
5464    });
5465    let anchor = spill_parent.as_ref().and_then(Self::spill_anchor);
5466    if let Some(anchor) = &anchor {
5467      self.spill_anchors.insert(anchor.clone());
5468    }
5469    // Chunk the run so each segment stays under `segment_chunk_bytes()` of
5470    // serialized text; every chunk gets its own segment + placeholder, so
5471    // document order is preserved chunk-by-chunk.
5472    let chunk_ceiling = Self::segment_chunk_bytes();
5473    let mut runs_spilled = 0usize;
5474    let mut chunk: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
5475    let mut xml = String::new();
5476    let all: Vec<Node> = std::mem::take(run);
5477    let total = all.len();
5478    for (i, node) in all.into_iter().enumerate() {
5479      // A spilled subtree can CONTAIN placeholders from earlier, deeper
5480      // spills (a closing section swallows its paragraphs' placeholders).
5481      // They serialize LITERALLY (`literal_placeholders` is set for all of
5482      // pass 1) and the final assembly's splice resolves them recursively —
5483      // inlining them here instead once rebuilt an 841 MB and a 1.85 GB
5484      // segment out of chapter shells on the 131 MB witness, and pass 2
5485      // died re-materializing them.
5486      debug_assert!(
5487        self.literal_placeholders,
5488        "spill_run must serialize placeholders literally (set for all of pass 1)"
5489      );
5490      self.serialize_into(&mut xml, &node, depth, noindent, false);
5491      chunk.push(node);
5492      let last = i + 1 == total;
5493      if xml.len() >= chunk_ceiling || last {
5494        let meta = SegmentMeta {
5495          depth,
5496          noindent,
5497          font: context_font.clone(),
5498          anchor: anchor.clone(),
5499          namespaces: namespaces.to_vec(),
5500          parent: chunk
5501            .first()
5502            .and_then(|n| n.get_parent())
5503            .map(|p| arena::to_string(get_node_qname(&p))),
5504          ancestors: {
5505            // Every ancestor xml:id: a scope rooted at one of these covers
5506            // the whole fragment (see SegmentMeta::ancestors).
5507            let mut ids = Vec::new();
5508            let mut cur = chunk.first().and_then(|n| n.get_parent());
5509            while let Some(n) = cur {
5510              // Both attribute forms — constructed ancestors carry the plain
5511              // one (see `node_xml_id_any_form`); a namespace-only read left
5512              // these lists near-empty, so label/id-scoped rules could not
5513              // cover their fragments.
5514              if let Some(id) = Self::node_xml_id_any_form(&n) {
5515                ids.push(id);
5516              }
5517              cur = n.get_parent();
5518            }
5519            ids
5520          },
5521        };
5522        let store = self
5523          .spill_store
5524          .as_mut()
5525          .expect("checked at spill_closed_subtrees entry");
5526        let seg = store.write_segment(&xml, meta)?;
5527        xml.clear();
5528        // Index + purge while the nodes are still alive, then placeholder +
5529        // free.
5530        for node in chunk.iter() {
5531          self.index_and_purge_spilled(node, seg, index);
5532        }
5533        let spill_error = |details: String| {
5534          Error::from(ErrorData {
5535            target:   ErrorTarget::Document,
5536            category: ErrorCategory::Libxml,
5537            message:  s!("segment staging: {}", details),
5538          })
5539        };
5540        let mut placeholder = Node::new(SPILL_PLACEHOLDER, None, &self.document)
5541          .map_err(|()| spill_error(s!("cannot create the placeholder node")))?;
5542        placeholder
5543          .set_attribute("ref", &seg.to_string())
5544          .map_err(|e| spill_error(s!("cannot mark the placeholder: {e}")))?;
5545        // Record the LAST spilled sibling's qname: build-time hooks that
5546        // consult a previous element sibling (prune_empty_para's
5547        // was-I-first test — sweep witness tests/alignment/colortbls.tex)
5548        // would otherwise see the placeholder where eager sees that node.
5549        // Never serialized — assembly splices the segment text instead.
5550        if let Some(last) = chunk.last() {
5551          placeholder
5552            .set_attribute("last", &arena::to_string(get_node_qname(last)))
5553            .map_err(|e| spill_error(s!("cannot mark the placeholder: {e}")))?;
5554        }
5555        chunk
5556          .first_mut()
5557          .expect("a flushed chunk is non-empty")
5558          .add_prev_sibling(&mut placeholder)
5559          .map_err(|e| spill_error(s!("cannot insert the placeholder: {e}")))?;
5560        for node in chunk.drain(..) {
5561          // Actually FREE the spilled subtree (unlink alone leaks — see
5562          // Node::free_subtree). Its ids were unrecorded by
5563          // index_and_purge_spilled above; discard_subtree re-purges
5564          // node_boxes (cheap) and reclaims the C memory, which is the whole
5565          // point of the spill.
5566          self.discard_subtree(node);
5567        }
5568        SPILLED_SEGMENTS.set(SPILLED_SEGMENTS.get() + 1);
5569        runs_spilled += 1;
5570      }
5571    }
5572    Ok(runs_spilled)
5573  }
5574
5575  /// The nearest `xml:id` on `node` or an ancestor below the root ([`SegmentMeta::anchor`](crate::sxml::SegmentMeta)).
5576  fn spill_anchor(node: &Node) -> Option<String> {
5577    let mut cur = Some(node.clone());
5578    while let Some(n) = cur {
5579      let parent = n
5580        .get_parent()
5581        .filter(|p| p.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode));
5582      parent.as_ref()?;
5583      if let Some(id) = Self::node_xml_id_any_form(&n) {
5584        return Some(id);
5585      }
5586      cur = parent;
5587    }
5588    None
5589  }
5590
5591  /// The font `finalize_rec` declares for `parent`'s children: from the text default, each ancestor's font
5592  /// attributes its element can carry, root first ([`SegmentMeta::font`](crate::sxml::SegmentMeta)).
5593  fn finalize_context_font(&self, parent: &Node) -> Font {
5594    let mut chain = Vec::new();
5595    let mut cur = Some(parent.clone());
5596    while let Some(n) = cur.filter(|n| n.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)) {
5597      cur = n.get_parent();
5598      chain.push(n);
5599    }
5600    let mut declared = Font::text_default();
5601    for node in chain.iter().rev() {
5602      if node.has_attribute("_standalone_font") {
5603        declared = Font::text_default();
5604      }
5605      if self.has_node_font(node) {
5606        let qname = get_node_qname(node);
5607        for (key, (_, properties)) in self.get_node_font(node).relative_to(&declared) {
5608          if model::can_have_attribute(qname, arena::pin(&key)) {
5609            declared = declared.merge_ref(&properties);
5610          }
5611        }
5612      }
5613      if let Some(anchor) = node.get_attribute("_font_anchor") {
5614        declared = declared.merge_ref(&Font {
5615          size: Some(anchor.parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(10.0)),
5616          ..Font::default()
5617        });
5618      }
5619    }
5620    declared
5621  }
5622
5623  /// Streaming, after pass 1: every spill anchor's `_ID_counter_*` attributes as construction left them — recorded
5624  /// when it spilled, else read from the spine. Pass 2 continues them; [`Self::set_id_counters`] hands them back.
5625  pub fn take_spill_anchor_counters(
5626    &mut self,
5627  ) -> rustc_hash::FxHashMap<String, Vec<(String, String)>> {
5628    let mut counters = std::mem::take(&mut self.spilled_anchor_counters);
5629    for id in std::mem::take(&mut self.spill_anchors) {
5630      if let Some(node) = self.lookup_id(&id) {
5631        counters.insert(id, id_counters(node));
5632      }
5633    }
5634    counters
5635  }
5636
5637  /// Set the `_ID_counter_*` attributes of the element `id` names, if it is in this document.
5638  pub fn set_id_counters(&mut self, id: &str, counters: &[(String, String)]) {
5639    if let Some(node) = self.idstore.get_mut(id) {
5640      for (key, value) in counters {
5641        let _ = node.set_attribute(key, value);
5642      }
5643    }
5644  }
5645
5646  /// A node's `xml:id`, namespace-aware with a defensive plain-name fallback.
5647  ///
5648  /// MECHANISM CORRECTION (2026-08-04, empirically probed against libxml
5649  /// 0.3.21): `set_attribute("xml:id", …)` DOES namespace the attribute
5650  /// (`xmlSetProp` resolves the predefined `xml` prefix), so builder-
5651  /// CONSTRUCTED nodes and PARSED nodes both store the namespaced form and
5652  /// `get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS)` reads both; no code path in this
5653  /// workspace produces a literal-named "xml:id" attribute. The earlier
5654  /// claim here that constructed nodes carry the plain form does not
5655  /// reproduce. The 131 MB-book witness (2026-08-01: spill-time indexing
5656  /// registered 865 of 23,654 labels) was fixed by the commit that added
5657  /// this helper, but the missing-id mechanism was misattributed; the bare
5658  /// fallback is kept as belt (it is dead under the probed model, and
5659  /// harmless).
5660  pub(crate) fn node_xml_id_any_form(node: &Node) -> Option<String> {
5661    node
5662      .get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS)
5663      .or_else(|| node.get_attribute("xml:id"))
5664  }
5665
5666  /// Record a spilled subtree's ids and labels in the fragment index, and
5667  /// purge every registry holding a handle or pointer into it.
5668  fn index_and_purge_spilled(
5669    &mut self,
5670    node: &Node,
5671    seg: crate::sxml::SegmentId,
5672    index: &mut crate::sxml::FragmentIndex,
5673  ) {
5674    // Box entries exist for TEXT nodes too (see purge_node_boxes_rec) —
5675    // purge before the element gate or a prose-heavy document leaks a
5676    // pinned `Digested` per spilled text node.
5677    self.node_boxes.remove(&node.to_hashable());
5678    if node.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
5679      return;
5680    }
5681    // Namespace prefixes this subtree uses leave the resident DOM with it;
5682    // the root declaration pass consults `spilled_ns_prefixes` for them.
5683    if let Some(ns) = node.get_namespace() {
5684      let prefix = ns.get_prefix();
5685      if !prefix.is_empty() {
5686        self.spilled_ns_prefixes.insert(prefix);
5687      }
5688    }
5689    for (key, _) in node.get_attributes() {
5690      if let Some(colon) = key.find(':') {
5691        let prefix = &key[..colon];
5692        if !self.spilled_ns_prefixes.contains(prefix) {
5693          self.spilled_ns_prefixes.insert(prefix.to_string());
5694        }
5695      }
5696    }
5697    for attr in [
5698      "about", "resource", "property", "typeof", "rel", "rev", "datatype",
5699    ] {
5700      if let Some(value) = node.get_attribute(attr) {
5701        for term in value.split_whitespace() {
5702          if let Some(colon) = term.find(':') {
5703            index.record_rdfa_prefix(&term[..colon], "");
5704          }
5705        }
5706      }
5707    }
5708    let id_opt = Self::node_xml_id_any_form(node);
5709    if let Some(id) = &id_opt {
5710      index.record_id(id, seg);
5711      self.unrecord_id(id);
5712      self.spilled_ids.insert(id.clone());
5713      if self.spill_anchors.remove(id) {
5714        self
5715          .spilled_anchor_counters
5716          .insert(id.clone(), id_counters(node));
5717      }
5718      if let Some(labels) = node.get_attribute("labels") {
5719        for label in labels.split_whitespace() {
5720          index.record_label(label, id);
5721        }
5722      }
5723    }
5724    for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
5725      self.index_and_purge_spilled(&child, seg, index);
5726    }
5727  }
5728
5729  // `strip_indentation_whitespace` lived here until `spill_flat` (its only
5730  // caller was streaming pass 2): it deleted the whitespace-only text nodes
5731  // our own pretty-printer had added to spill segments, via the same
5732  // `model::can_contain_sym(#PCDATA)` query the serializer indents by. Flat
5733  // spill serialization means those nodes are never created, so the
5734  // generate-then-undo pair is gone. It also `unlink_node`d rather than
5735  // freed — the orphan-leak trap — so do not resurrect it as-is.
5736
5737  /// Remove the pointer-keyed `node_boxes` entries for `node` and its whole
5738  /// subtree. MANDATORY before freeing nodes mid-conversion: a freed node's
5739  /// address is REUSED by later allocations, and a stale entry then
5740  /// mis-associates the old box (and its font) with an unrelated new node —
5741  /// observed as spurious `<text font="italic">` wrappers the moment the
5742  /// math parser started freeing replaced trees promptly.
5743  pub fn purge_node_boxes_rec(&mut self, node: &Node) {
5744    // EVERY node type can carry an entry: absorbing text records the box
5745    // against the TEXT node (`openText_internal`), and `get_node_box` never
5746    // reads those — but an unpurged one pins its whole `Digested` forever.
5747    // Measured: the dominant pass-1 creep on a 131 MB prose-heavy book
5748    // (~11 GB of orphaned text-node boxes; every probed collection flat).
5749    self.node_boxes.remove(&node.to_hashable());
5750    if node.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
5751      return; // only elements have children to descend into
5752    }
5753    for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
5754      self.purge_node_boxes_rec(&child);
5755    }
5756  }
5757
5758  /// Discard a garbage subtree for good: purge the pointer-keyed
5759  /// `node_boxes` entries, then free the C memory NOW via the fork's
5760  /// `Node::free_subtree` — the missing half of every unlink-to-discard
5761  /// site (rust-libxml Linkage: a doc-created node that is unlinked but
5762  /// never re-attached is freed by NOBODY; math parsing discards thousands
5763  /// of replaced subtrees per document, measured ~1.4 MB/formula, ~1.8 GB
5764  /// retained per 32 MB streaming segment). `free_subtree` also
5765  /// neutralizes every live wrapper into the subtree, so stray clones in
5766  /// long-lived collections (`constructed_nodes`, an idstore epoch) go
5767  /// inert instead of firing a deferred `xmlFreeNode` after the document
5768  /// itself is gone.
5769  ///
5770  /// PRECONDITIONS (the caller's contract, satisfied at current sites):
5771  /// * every `xml:id` in the subtree is already unrecorded or transferred —
5772  ///   this deliberately does NOT `unrecord_node_ids`, because discard
5773  ///   always follows a copy (`append_tree`) that re-recorded the SAME id
5774  ///   strings for the copies, and unrecording here would kill those fresh
5775  ///   entries;
5776  /// * no live handle into the subtree is used afterwards.
5777  pub fn discard_subtree(&mut self, node: Node) {
5778    self.purge_node_boxes_rec(&node);
5779    // The last ligated text node may be in the freed subtree, and libxml may hand its address to the next node
5780    // created: forget it (the next close then ligates from the start, as Perl's).
5781    self.ligated_text = None;
5782    node.free_subtree();
5783  }
5784
5785  /// Drop every `node_boxes` entry whose node is no longer IN this document
5786  /// tree (streaming pass 1's self-healing sweep). Entries are written for
5787  /// every constructed node and purged at the spill/discard chokepoints —
5788  /// but dozens of build-time discard paths (alignment rearrangement above
5789  /// all: 105k `align` environments on the 131 MB witness) detach nodes
5790  /// without purging, and each stale entry pins a whole `Digested` box tree.
5791  /// Measured: ~518k stale entries before the FIRST spill, growing past
5792  /// 1.75M — the dominant residual pass-1 creep after the C-side frees.
5793  /// A mark-and-retain against the live tree is immune to every such path,
5794  /// including future ones. The mark phase walks the whole live DOM, so the
5795  /// streaming driver gates it on `node_boxes` growth (core_interface.rs).
5796  pub fn sweep_stale_node_boxes(&mut self) {
5797    let t_start = std::time::Instant::now();
5798    fn mark(node: &Node, live: &mut rustc_hash::FxHashSet<usize>) {
5799      live.insert(node.to_hashable());
5800      if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
5801        for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
5802          mark(&child, live);
5803        }
5804      }
5805    }
5806    let mut live: rustc_hash::FxHashSet<usize> = rustc_hash::FxHashSet::default();
5807    if let Some(root) = self.document.get_root_element() {
5808      mark(&root, &mut live);
5809    }
5810    let t_mark = t_start.elapsed();
5811    let before = self.node_boxes.len();
5812    let t_retain_start = std::time::Instant::now();
5813    self.node_boxes.retain(|k, _| live.contains(k));
5814    let t_retain = t_retain_start.elapsed();
5815    let after = self.node_boxes.len();
5816    self.last_swept_node_boxes_len = after;
5817    let total = t_start.elapsed();
5818    if std::env::var_os("LXML_TRACE_NODE_BOXES").is_some() {
5819      eprintln!(
5820        "streaming: node_boxes sweep {before} -> {after} (live: {}, dropped: {}) | mark: {t_mark:?}, retain: {t_retain:?}, total: {total:?}",
5821        live.len(),
5822        before - after
5823      );
5824    }
5825  }

5827  /// Attach the processed-segment store for serialization: from here on,
5828  /// `serialize_into` splices each segment's output text where its
5829  /// placeholder sits (streaming assembly).
5830  pub fn set_spill_store(&mut self, store: crate::sxml::SegmentStore) {
5831    self.spill_store = Some(store);
5832  }
5833
5834  /// Streaming pass 1 switch: defer (true) or restore (false) the ROOT
5835  /// element's `after_open` hook dispatch. See the field docs.
5836  pub fn set_defer_root_after_open(&mut self, defer: bool) { self.defer_root_after_open = defer; }
5837
5838  /// Is the root's late-hook dispatch currently deferred (streaming pass 1)?
5839  /// Engine bindings consult this to defer digestion-state-dependent
5840  /// insertions (frontmatter) to end-of-digestion.
5841  pub fn root_after_open_deferred(&self) -> bool { self.defer_root_after_open }
5842
5843  /// Open a `ltx:_Capture_` wrapper at the TOP of the root — after the last
5844  /// existing `ltx:resource` child (resources lead the document in the eager
5845  /// output), else as the first child. Shared insertion context for the
5846  /// streaming-mode operations that must place content where an
5847  /// empty-just-opened root would have put it.
5848  fn open_root_top_capture(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
5849    let Some(mut root) = self.document.get_root_element() else {
5850      return Ok(None);
5851    };
5852    let mut last_resource: Option<Node> = None;
5853    for child in root.get_child_nodes() {
5854      if child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) && child.get_name() == "resource" {
5855        last_resource = Some(child);
5856      }
5857    }
5858    let wrapper = match last_resource {
5859      Some(r) => match r.get_next_sibling() {
5860        Some(next) => self.insert_element_before(&next, "ltx:_Capture_", None)?,
5861        None => self.open_element_at(&mut root, "ltx:_Capture_", None, None)?,
5862      },
5863      None => match root.get_first_child() {
5864        Some(first) => self.insert_element_before(&first, "ltx:_Capture_", None)?,
5865        None => self.open_element_at(&mut root, "ltx:_Capture_", None, None)?,
5866      },
5867    };
5868    Ok(Some(wrapper))
5869  }
5870
5871  /// Streaming pass 1: fold freshly queued resources into the live document
5872  /// as they arrive, at the top of the root. Perl's own contract
5873  /// (`Package.pm:RequireResource`): with a live document, `addResource`
5874  /// inserts DIRECTLY; only a document-less preamble queues. The eager path
5875  /// keeps the queue until the root's `after_open` because its build starts
5876  /// post-digestion; under streaming that drain is deferred to
5877  /// end-of-digestion, and mid-digestion consumers — the frontmatter
5878  /// fallback's `/ltx:document/ltx:resource[last()]` anchor — need the
5879  /// resources already placed.
5880  pub fn process_pending_resources_at_top(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
5881    let resources: Vec<Resource> = state::take_pending_resources();
5882    if resources.is_empty() {
5883      state::reset_pending_resources();
5884      return Ok(());
5885    }
5886    let Some(wrapper) = self.open_root_top_capture()? else {
5887      // No root yet: re-queue for the next absorb (or the deferred drain).
5888      for resource in resources {
5889        state::push_pending_resource(resource);
5890      }
5891      return Ok(());
5892    };
5893    let savenode = self.node.clone();
5894    self.set_node(&wrapper);
5895    for resource in resources {
5896      self.add_resource(resource)?;
5897    }
5898    state::reset_pending_resources();
5899    self.unwrap_nodes(wrapper)?;
5900    self.set_node(&savenode);
5901    Ok(())
5902  }
5903
5904  /// Streaming: dispatch the ROOT's deferred after-open hooks at
5905  /// end-of-digestion — the eager timing (build starts only after digestion
5906  /// ends) — with the insertion point at the TOP of the root, as if it had
5907  /// just opened empty. `after_open` itself cannot be used here: it pins the
5908  /// current node to the dispatched element, so everything the hooks insert
5909  /// (resources, frontmatter) would APPEND after the built content instead
5910  /// of leading it. A `ltx:_Capture_` wrapper as first child recreates the
5911  /// empty-root insertion context (the frontmatter fallback's own
5912  /// technique), and is unwrapped afterwards.
5913  pub fn dispatch_deferred_root_hooks(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
5914    debug_assert!(
5915      !self.defer_root_after_open,
5916      "clear the deferral before dispatching"
5917    );
5918    let Some(mut root) = self.document.get_root_element() else {
5919      return Ok(());
5920    };
5921    let savenode = self.node.clone();
5922    let Some(wrapper) = self.open_root_top_capture()? else {
5923      return Ok(());
5924    };
5925    self.set_node(&wrapper);
5926    let qname = get_node_qname(&root);
5927    let box_opt = self.get_node_box(&root);
5928    let (_prompt, late) = self.get_tag_action_list_parts(qname, TagOptionName::AfterOpen);
5929    for action in late {
5930      action(self, &mut root, box_opt.as_ref())?;
5931    }
5932    self.unwrap_nodes(wrapper)?;
5933    self.set_node(&savenode);
5934    Ok(())
5935  }
5936
5937  /// Merge RDFa prefixes recorded from spilled content, so the root's
5938  /// `prefix=` attribute covers usages the live-DOM scan can no longer see.
5939  pub fn add_extra_rdfa_prefixes<'a>(&mut self, prefixes: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>) {
5940    self.extra_rdfa_prefixes.extend(prefixes.map(String::from));

5944  /// which mutates segments while fragment documents exist independently —
5945  /// and re-attaches it for assembly).
5946  pub fn take_spill_store(&mut self) -> Option<crate::sxml::SegmentStore> {
5947    self.spill_store.take()

5949
5950  /// Discard the in-memory `idstore` cache and rebuild it from the
5951  /// current DOM state. Historically guarded the 1605.08055 SIGSEGV
5952  /// where `mark_xmnode_visibility` dereferenced dangling lookup_id
5953  /// entries while recursing through XMRef targets.
5954  ///
5955  /// As of cycle 72, the 5 call sites that previously dropped nodes
5956  /// without unrecord_id — math-parser `replace_tree` at
5957  /// parser.rs:456/690 (cascades via remove_node) and `unbind_node`
5958  /// loops at parser.rs:639/856 + rewrite.rs:522 (all have
5959  /// preceding unrecord_node_ids guards) — are ID-safe. This rebuild
5960  /// is retained as a belt-and-suspenders probe until the
5961  /// 1605.08055 verification per SYNC_STATUS.md D3b lands.
5962  ///
5963  /// The rebuild is a DOM walk, so live id uniqueness is restored
5964  /// alongside — duplicates already in DOM are resolved with
5965  /// `modify_id`, matching `record_node_ids` semantics.
5966  pub fn rebuild_idstore_from_dom(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
5967    self.idstore.clear();
5968    if let Some(root) = self.document.get_root_element() {
5969      self.record_node_ids(&root)?;
5970    }
5971    Ok(())
5972  }
5973
5974  /// Get a new, related, but unique id.
5975  /// Sneaky option: try "ID_SUFFIX" as a suffix for id, first.
5976  /// Perl: sub modifyID (Document.pm lines 1483-1494)
5977  pub fn modify_id(&mut self, id: String) -> String {
5978    if self.idstore.contains_key(&id) || self.spilled_ids.contains(&id) {
5979      // Whoops! Already assigned!!!
5980      // Can we recover?
5981      let badid = id;
5982      // First try ID_SUFFIX if set
5983      if let Some(Stored::String(suffix)) = state::lookup_value("ID_SUFFIX") {
5984        let suffixed = s!("{}{}", badid, arena::to_string(suffix));
5985        if !self.idstore.contains_key(&suffixed) && !self.spilled_ids.contains(&suffixed) {
5986          return suffixed;
5987        }
5988      }
5989      // Try radix_alpha(1) through radix_alpha(26^3)
5990      // Gotta give up, eventually; is 3 letters enough?
5991      for s1 in 1_i64..=(26 * 26 * 26) {
5992        let candidate = s!("{}{}", badid, radix_alpha(s1));
5993        if !self.idstore.contains_key(&candidate) && !self.spilled_ids.contains(&candidate) {
5994          return candidate;
5995        }
5996      }
5997      emit_error(
5998        "malformed",
5999        "id",
6000        &format!("Automatic incrementing of ID counters failed for '{badid}'"),
6001      );
6002      badid
6003    } else {
6004      id
6005    }
6006  }
6007
6008  pub fn lookup_id(&self, id: &str) -> Option<&Node> { self.idstore.get(id) }
6009
6010  /// Clone the idstore for use in thread-local contexts (math parsing).
6011  pub fn get_idstore_clone(&self) -> HashMap<String, Node> { self.idstore.clone() }
6012
6013  // ======================================================================
6014  //  Odd bit:
6015  //  In an XMDual, in each branch (content, presentation) there will be atoms
6016  //  that correspond to the input (one will be real, the other an XMRef to the first).
6017  //  But also there will be additional "decoration" (delimiters, punctuation, etc on the
6018  // presentation  side; other symbols, bindings, whatever, on the content side).
6019  //  These decorations should NOT be subject to rewrite rules,
6020  //  and in cross-linked parallel markup, they should be attributed to the
6021  //  upper containing object's ID, rather than left dangling.
6022  //
6023  //  To determine this, we mark all math nodes as to whether they are "visible" from
6024  //  presentation, content or both (the default top-level being both).
6025  //  Decorations are the nodes that are visible to only one mode.
6026  //  Note that nodes that are not visible at all CAN occur (& do currently when the parser
6027  //  creates XMDuals), pruneXMDuals (below) gets rid of them.
6028
6029  // NOTE: This should ultimately be in a base Document class,
6030  // since it is also needed before conversion to parallel markup!
6031  pub fn mark_xmnode_visibility(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
6032    let xmath = self.findnodes("//ltx:XMath/*", None);
6033    for math in xmath.iter() {
6034      for mut node in self.findnodes("descendant-or-self::*[@_pvis or @_cvis]", Some(math)) {
6035        node.remove_attribute("_pvis")?;
6036        node.remove_attribute("_cvis")?;
6037      }
6038    }
6039    for math in xmath {
6040      self.mark_xmnode_visibility_aux(math, true, true)?;
6041    }
6042    Ok(())
6043  }
6044
6045  fn mark_xmnode_visibility_aux(&self, node: Node, cvis: bool, pvis: bool) -> Result<()> {
6046    // Recurses to math-tree depth via XMDual/XMRef-following + element-
6047    // child fan-out. Deep grammar-ambiguous papers (sandbox 0711.4787
6048    // et al, #17) hit Rust's 8 MB main-thread stack here during the
6049    // `Finalizing...` phase (via prune_xmduals → mark_xmnode_visibility).
6050    // Grow the stack on demand instead of overflowing (guard params are
6051    // configurable in `crate::stack_guard`).
6052    crate::stack_guard::maybe_grow(move || self.mark_xmnode_visibility_aux_inner(node, cvis, pvis))
6053  }
6054
6055  fn mark_xmnode_visibility_aux_inner(
6056    &self,
6057    mut node: Node,
6058    cvis: bool,
6059    mut pvis: bool,
6060  ) -> Result<()> {
6061    if (!cvis || node.has_attribute("_cvis")) && (!pvis || node.has_attribute("_pvis")) {
6062      return Ok(());
6063    }
6064    let qname = get_node_qname(&node);
6065    // Special case: for XMArg used to wrap "formal" arguments on the content side,
6066    // mark them as visible as presentation as well.
6067    if cvis && (qname == pin!("ltx:XMArg")) {
6068      pvis = true;
6069    }
6070    if cvis {
6071      node.set_attribute("_cvis", "1")?;
6072    }
6073    if pvis {
6074      node.set_attribute("_pvis", "1")?;
6075    }
6076    if qname == pin!("ltx:XMDual") {
6077      let mut children = xml::element_nodes(&node);
6078      // XMDual should have exactly 2 element children (content + presentation),
6079      // but a malformed math parse (e.g. semantic action producing empty pair
6080      // during deep ambiguity collapse) can leave an empty XMDual. Skip
6081      // visibility-marking rather than panicking on `children.remove(0)` —
6082      // see wp5 sandbox 2110.10033 and 4 sibling papers.
6083      if children.len() >= 2 {
6084        let c = children.remove(0);
6085        let p = children.remove(0);
6086        if cvis {
6087          self.mark_xmnode_visibility_aux(c, true, false)?;
6088        }
6089        if pvis {
6090          self.mark_xmnode_visibility_aux(p, false, true)?;
6091        }
6092      }
6093    } else if qname == pin!("ltx:XMRef") {
6094      match node.get_attribute("idref") {
6095        None => {
6096          let key = node.get_attribute("_xmkey");
6097          Warn!(
6098            "expected",
6099            "id",
6100            "Missing idref on ltx:XMRef",
6101            s!("_xmkey is `{}`", key.unwrap_or_default())
6102          );
6103        },
6104        Some(id) => match self.lookup_id(&id) {
6105          None => {
6106            Warn!(
6107              "expected",
6108              "node",
6109              s!("No node found with id='{id}' (referred to from ltx:XMRef)")
6110            );
6111          },
6112          Some(reffed) => {
6113            self.mark_xmnode_visibility_aux(reffed.clone(), cvis, pvis)?;
6114          },
6115        },
6116      }
6117    } else {
6118      for child in xml::element_nodes(&node) {
6119        self.mark_xmnode_visibility_aux(child, cvis, pvis)?;
6120      }
6121    }
6122    Ok(())
6123  }
6124
6125  /// Remove `ltx:XMRef[@_split_ref="1"]` whose `idref` no longer
6126  /// resolves. These are the XMRefs minted by
6127  /// `amsmath::rearrange_ams_split` to mirror the flattened cell
6128  /// sequence inside an `XMDual(XMWrap(refs), XMArray(cells))`. The
6129  /// math parser can later absorb some cells (typically inserted
6130  /// MULOP times-ops on `\mathcal{L}\rho` chains) into wrapping
6131  /// XMApps, dropping their xml:id from the live DOM and leaving
6132  /// the sibling XMRefs dangling. Left in place, each dangling
6133  /// XMRef trips three separate diagnostics later — math parser's
6134  /// read_xmref Warn, finalize's mark_xmnode_visibility Warn, and
6135  /// post-process's mark_xm_node_visibility Error.
6136  ///
6137  /// We restrict the sweep to the `_split_ref` marker so refs from
6138  /// other provenance (base_xmath `\lx@dual`, renamed-id cases like
6139  /// declare_test's `S1.Ex1.m1.1` → `.1a` rename) stay untouched.
6140  ///
6141  /// Content-preserving: XMRefs are structural cross-references,
6142  /// not author body, and the math parser has already absorbed the
6143  /// referenced cell into the visible XMArray branch — no glyph or
6144  /// formula material is lost.
6145  pub fn prune_dangling_split_xmrefs(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
6146    let xmrefs = self.findnodes("//ltx:XMRef[@_split_ref or @_mf_ref]", None);
6147    for xmref in xmrefs {
6148      let idref = match xmref.get_attribute("idref") {
6149        Some(id) => id,
6150        None => continue,
6151      };
6152      if self.lookup_id(&idref).is_none() && xmref.get_parent().is_some() {
6153        self.remove_node(xmref);
6154      }
6155    }
6156    // Broader sweep: any XMRef pointing to a canonical math node id
6157    // `S<N>.E<M>.m1.<K>...` that no longer resolves. These are minted
6158    // by base_xmath::add_column_to_math_fork during rearrange_ams_*
