6159    // (align/gather/multline), but unlike `_split_ref` they aren't
6160    // marked. The math parser absorbs cells later, leaving the refs
6161    // dangling and triggering the `Error:expected:id` cascade in
6162    // post-processing.
6163    //
6164    // We restrict the regex to the equation-numbered form (E<digit>,
6165    // not Ex<digit>) so declare_test's renamed-id case
6166    // (`S1.Ex1.m1.1` → `.1a`) stays untouched. canvas papers using
6167    // `\begin{equation}` produce `E1`/`E2`/... ids.
6168    static RE_MATH_ID: Lazy<Regex> = Lazy::new(|| Regex::new(r"^S\d+\.E\d+\.m\d+\.").unwrap());
6169    let xmrefs2 = self.findnodes("//ltx:XMRef[@idref]", None);
6170    for xmref in xmrefs2 {
6171      // Skip if already pruned via _split_ref sweep above.
6172      if xmref.get_parent().is_none() {
6173        continue;
6174      }
6175      let idref = match xmref.get_attribute("idref") {
6176        Some(id) => id,
6177        None => continue,
6178      };
6179      if RE_MATH_ID.is_match(&idref) && self.lookup_id(&idref).is_none() {
6180        // Safety guard: NEVER drop a ref that is an OPERAND of an XMApp.
6181        // Removing it would corrupt the application — e.g. an `\lx@dual`
6182        // content arm `XMApp(probability, XMRef)` would lose its argument,
6183        // emitting a malformed `apply(probability)` with no operand (silent
6184        // content-MathML corruption; witnessed on `aligned`+`\Pr(a,b|c)`,
6185        // docs/reproducers/class_b_aligned_pr_xmref.tex). Such content-arm
6186        // refs are essential shared links — they are NEVER the redundant
6187        // MathFork/`_split_ref` mirrors this sweep targets (those live in
6188        // XMWrap/XMArray, not as XMApp operands). Leave it dangling so the
6189        // faithful "No node found" Warn (`mark_xmnode_visibility`) fires
6190        // rather than silently corrupting the content tree.
6191        if let Some(parent) = xmref.get_parent()
6192          && get_node_qname(&parent) == pin!("ltx:XMApp")
6193        {
6194          let kids = parent.get_child_elements();
6195          let is_operand = kids
6196            .iter()
6197            .position(|k| *k == xmref)
6198            .is_some_and(|pos| pos > 0);
6199          if is_operand {
6200            continue;
6201          }
6202        }
6203        self.remove_node(xmref);
6204      }
6205    }
6206    Ok(())
6207  }
6208
6209  /// Reduce any ltx:XMDual's to just the visible branch, if the other is not visible
6210  /// (according to markXMNodeVisibility)
6211  /// If we could be 100% sure that the marking had stayed consistent (after various doc surgery)
6212  /// we could avoid re-marking, but we'd better be sure before removing nodes!
6213  pub fn prune_xmduals(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
6214    // RE-mark visibility!
6215    self.mark_xmnode_visibility()?;
6216    // will reversing keep from problems removing nodes from trees that already have been removed?
6217    for dual in self
6218      .findnodes("descendant-or-self::ltx:XMDual", None)
6219      .into_iter()
6220      .rev()
6221    {
6222      let mut dual_children = xml::element_nodes(&dual);
6223      // Defensive: an XMDual should always have presentation +
6224      // content children, but a malformed math parse (post-ambiguity
6225      // collapse) can yield <2. Skip rather than panic.
6226      // Witness 2110.10033 (panicked at document.rs:3120, post-fix
6227      // continuation of earlier guard at document.rs:2993).
6228      let Some(presentation) = dual_children.pop() else {
6229        continue;
6230      };
6231      let Some(content) = dual_children.pop() else {
6232        continue;
6233      };
6234      if self
6235        .findnode("descendant-or-self::*[@_pvis or @_cvis]", Some(&content))
6236        .is_none()
6237      {
6238        // content never seen
6239        self.collapse_xmdual(dual, presentation)?;
6240      } else if self
6241        .findnode(
6242          "descendant-or-self::*[@_pvis or @_cvis]",
6243          Some(&presentation),
6244        )
6245        .is_none()
6246      {
6247        // pres.
6248        self.collapse_xmdual(dual, content)?;
6249      } else {
6250        // compact aligned structures, where possible
6251        self.compact_xmdual(dual, content, Some(presentation))?;
6252      }
6253    }
6254    Ok(())
6255  }
6256
6257  fn compact_xmdual(
6258    &mut self,
6259    dual: Node,
6260    content: Node,
6261    presentation: Option<Node>,
6262  ) -> Result<()> {
6263    // Perl: our $content_transfer_overrides = { decl_id, meaning, name, omcd };
6264    // Perl: our $dual_transfer_overrides = { decl_id, meaning, name, omcd, xml:id, role };
6265    static CONTENT_TRANSFER: Lazy<HashSet<&'static str>> =
6266      Lazy::new(|| HashSet::from_iter(["decl_id", "meaning", "name", "omcd"]));
6267    static DUAL_TRANSFER: Lazy<HashSet<&'static str>> =
6268      Lazy::new(|| HashSet::from_iter(["decl_id", "meaning", "name", "omcd", "xml:id", "role"]));
6269
6270    let presentation = match presentation {
6271      Some(p) => p,
6272      None => return Ok(()),
6273    };
6274    let c_name = with_node_qname(&content, |n| n.to_string());
6275    let p_name = with_node_qname(&presentation, |n| n.to_string());
6276
6277    // Case 1: Quick fix — merge two tokens (Perl compactXMDual L1588-1593).
6278    // Perl has NO id cleanup here: mergeAttributes deliberately TRANSFERS the
6279    // content/dual xml:id onto the surviving presentation token (unRecordID +
6280    // recordID, L1308-1313), keeping refs to that id resolvable. A former
6281    // Rust-only "remove the leaked content id" block contradicted that — and
6282    // was dead anyway (its bare has/get/remove_attribute("xml:id") calls
6283    // always missed the namespaced attribute).
6284    if c_name == "ltx:XMTok" && p_name == "ltx:XMTok" {
6285      let mut pres = presentation;
6286      self.merge_attributes(&content, &mut pres, Some(&CONTENT_TRANSFER))?;
6287      self.merge_attributes(&dual, &mut pres, Some(&DUAL_TRANSFER))?;
6288      // Unlink presentation from dual before replacing, since presentation is a child of dual
6289      pres.unlink();
6290      self.replace_node(dual, vec![pres])?;
6291      return Ok(());
6292    }
6293
6294    // Case 2: Compact mirror XMApp nodes
6295    if c_name != "ltx:XMApp" || p_name != "ltx:XMApp" {
6296      return Ok(());
6297    }
6298    let content_args = xml::element_nodes(&content);
6299    let pres_args = xml::element_nodes(&presentation);
6300    if content_args.len() != pres_args.len() {
6301      return Ok(());
6302    }
6303    let n_args = content_args.len();
6304
6305    // Walk the corresponding children, double-check they are referenced in the same order
6306    enum NewArg {
6307      Single(Node),
6308      Pair(Node, Node), // (content_arg, pres_arg) — to be merged
6309    }
6310    let mut new_args: Vec<NewArg> = Vec::with_capacity(n_args);
6311    for (c_arg, p_arg) in content_args.into_iter().zip(pres_args) {
6312      if let Some(c_idref) = c_arg.get_attribute("idref")
6313        && c_idref == p_arg.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS).unwrap_or_default()
6314      {
6315        new_args.push(NewArg::Single(p_arg));
6316        continue;
6317      }
6318      if let Some(p_idref) = p_arg.get_attribute("idref")
6319        && p_idref == c_arg.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS).unwrap_or_default()
6320      {
6321        new_args.push(NewArg::Single(c_arg));
6322        continue;
6323      }
6324      // We can handle content-side XMToks to any XM* presentation subtree
6325      let c_arg_name = with_node_qname(&c_arg, |n| n.to_string());
6326      if c_arg_name != "ltx:XMTok" {
6327        return Ok(()); // Can't compact this structure
6328      }
6329      new_args.push(NewArg::Pair(c_arg, p_arg));
6330    }
6331
6332    // If we made it here, this dual has two mirrored applications — compact it.
6333    let mut parent = match dual.get_parent() {
6334      Some(p) => p,
6335      None => return Ok(()),
6336    };
6337    let mut compact_apply = self.open_element_at(&mut parent, "ltx:XMApp", None, None)?;
6338    for n_arg in new_args {
6339      let mut node = match n_arg {
6340        NewArg::Single(n) => n,
6341        NewArg::Pair(c_arg, mut p_arg) => {
6342          self.merge_attributes(&c_arg, &mut p_arg, Some(&CONTENT_TRANSFER))?;
6343          p_arg
6344        },
6345      };
6346      node.unlink();
6347      compact_apply.add_child(&mut node)?;
6348    }
6349    // Migrate dual attributes to the new XMApp
6350    self.merge_attributes(&dual, &mut compact_apply, Some(&DUAL_TRANSFER))?;
6351    // Direct DOM swap: replace dual with compact_apply without re-creating nodes.
6352    // Perl uses replaceChild which is a direct swap; replace_tree calls append_tree
6353    // which re-creates elements and fires afterOpen/afterClose hooks a second time.
6354    compact_apply.unlink();
6355    let mut dual_mut = dual;
6356    dual_mut.add_prev_sibling(&mut compact_apply).ok();
6357    self.remove_node(dual_mut);
6358    Ok(())
6359  }
6360
6361  /// Replace an XMDual with one of its branches
6362  fn collapse_xmdual(&mut self, dual: Node, mut branch: Node) -> Result<()> {
6363    // The other branch is not visible, nor referenced,
6364    // but the dual may have an id and be referenced
6365    if let Some(dualid) = dual.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
6366      self.unrecord_id(&dualid); // We'll move or remove the ID from the dual
6367      if let Some(branchid) = branch.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
6368        // branch has id too!
6369        for mut tref in self.findnodes(&s!("//*[@idref='{}']", dualid), None) {
6370          tref.set_attribute("idref", &branchid)?;
6371        } // Change dualid refs to branchid
6372      } else {
6373        // Assign the dual's id to the branch. Record first so we
6374        // receive a deduplicated id if something else claimed it
6375        // between the `unrecord_id` above and now — write the
6376        // deduped value, not the original.
6377        let deduped = self.record_id_with_node(&dualid, &branch);
6378        branch.set_attribute("xml:id", &deduped)?;
6379      }
6380    }
6381    // Direct DOM swap: Perl uses replaceChild (no re-creation, no hooks fired twice)
6382    let mut dual_mut = dual;
6383    dual_mut.add_prev_sibling(&mut branch).ok();
6384    self.remove_node(dual_mut);
6385    Ok(())
6386  }
6387
6388  //**********************************************************************
6389  /// Record the Box that created this node.
6390  pub fn set_node_box(&mut self, node: &Node, digested: Digested) {
6391    let nodeid = node.to_hashable();
6392    self.node_boxes.insert(nodeid, digested);
6393  }
6394
6395  pub fn get_node_box(&self, node: &Node) -> Option<Digested> {
6396    if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
6397      let nodeid = node.to_hashable();
6398      self.node_boxes.get(&nodeid).cloned()
6399    } else {
6400      None
6401    }
6402  }
6403
6404  //**********************************************************************
6405  /// Record the Font of a node
6406  pub fn set_node_font(&mut self, node: &mut Node, font: &Font) -> Result<()> {
6407    let fontid = font.to_hashable();
6408    node.set_attribute("_font", &fontid.to_string())?;
6409    // try to avoid aggressive clones, when unnecessary
6410    match self.node_fonts.get(&fontid) {
6411      None => {
6412        self.node_fonts.insert(fontid, font.clone());
6413      },
6414      Some(v) => {
6415        if v != font {
6416          self.node_fonts.insert(fontid, font.clone());
6417        }
6418      },
6419    }
6420    Ok(())
6421  }
6422
6423  pub fn copy_node_font(&mut self, from: &Node, to: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
6424    if let Some(fontid) = from.get_attribute("_font") {
6425      to.set_attribute("_font", &fontid)?;
6426    }
6427    Ok(())
6428  }
6429
6430  /// Possibly a sign of a design flaw; Set the node's font & all children that HAD the same font.
6431  pub fn merge_node_font_rec(&mut self, node: &Node, font: &Font) -> Result<()> {
6432    let oldfont = self.get_node_font(node);
6433    let props = oldfont.purestyle_changes(font);
6434    let mut nodes = VecDeque::new();
6435    nodes.push_front(node.clone());
6436    while let Some(mut n) = nodes.pop_front() {
6437      if n.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
6438        let font = &self.get_node_font(&n).merge_ref(&props);
6439        self.set_node_font(&mut n, font)?;
6440        for child in n.get_child_nodes() {
6441          nodes.push_back(child);
6442        }
6443      }
6444    }
6445    Ok(())
6446  }
6447
6448  pub fn set_box_font(&mut self, node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
6449    if let Some(ref thisbox) = self.box_to_absorb
6450      && let Some(font) = thisbox.get_font()?
6451    {
6452      let todo_font_clone = (*font).clone();
6453      self.set_node_font(node, &todo_font_clone)?;
6454    }
6455    Ok(())
6456  }
6457
6458  pub fn get_node_font(&self, node: &Node) -> &Font {
6459    if let Some(element) = xml::closest_element(node) {
6460      // Use the closest element (for text nodes, this is the parent element); the id is read in place, not copied
6461      // (`_font` is read on every text chunk: docs/performance/PERFORMANCE.md P11).
6462      // Tolerate non-numeric `_font` attributes — they can occur when
6463      // a corrupted property propagates across reversion (driver:
6464      // 2304.07380 panicked at parse::<u64>().unwrap()). Fall through
6465      // to the default font instead of aborting the run.
6466      if let Some(Ok(id)) = element.with_attribute(c"_font", str::parse::<u64>)
6467        && let Some(fnt) = self.node_fonts.get(&id)
6468      {
6469        return fnt;
6470      }
6471    }
6472    &FONT_TEXT_DEFAULT
6473  }
6474
6475  /// Decode a _font hash string to a Font object
6476  pub fn decode_font(&self, font_hash: &str) -> Option<&Font> {
6477    font_hash
6478      .parse::<u64>()
6479      .ok()
6480      .and_then(|id| self.node_fonts.get(&id))
6481  }
6482
6483  pub fn has_node_font(&self, node: &Node) -> bool {
6484    match xml::closest_element(node) {
6485      Some(element) => element.has_attribute("_font"),
6486      _ => false,
6487    }
6488  }
6489
6490  pub fn get_node_language(&self, node: &Node) -> String {
6491    let mut node_ref = node;
6492    let mut current;
6493    loop {
6494      if node_ref.get_type() != Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
6495        break;
6496      }
6497      // `xml:lang` is stored namespaced (local name "lang"); the string
6498      // accessor `get_attribute("xml:lang")` always returns None — read it via
6499      // the XML namespace. (Same libxml footgun as xml:id; see
6500      // docs/archive/XMLID_ACCESSOR_AUDIT_2026-06-08.md.)
6501      if let Some(lang) = node_ref.get_attribute_ns("lang", XML_NS) {
6502        return lang;
6503      }
6504      // Perl `getNodeLanguage` reads `_font` off the SAME (walked) ancestor,
6505      // not the original node — use `node_ref`, not `node`. Be robust against a
6506      // missing/foreign _font property (Perl PR #2767): never panic on a
6507      // non-numeric font id.
6508      if let Some(Ok(id)) = node_ref.with_attribute(c"_font", str::parse::<u64>)
6509        && let Some(font) = self.node_fonts.get(&id)
6510        && let Some(lang) = font.get_language()
6511      {
6512        return lang.to_string();
6513      }
6514      match node_ref.get_parent() {
6515        Some(parent) => {
6516          current = parent;
6517          node_ref = &current;
6518        },
6519        _ => {
6520          break;
6521        },
6522      }
6523    }
6524    String::from("en")
6525  }
6526
6527  // sub decodeFont {
6528  //   my ($self, $fontid) = @_;
6529  //   return $$self{node_fonts}{$fontid} || LaTeXML::Common::Font->textDefault(); }
6530
6531  /// Remove a node from the document (from it's parent).
6532  ///
6533  /// Two pieces of bookkeeping come with it: the `xml:id` of the node and of
6534  /// every descendant is un-recorded, so the ids are free for reuse and no
6535  /// dangling reference is left behind; and if the insertion point was inside
6536  /// what is being removed, it is rescued up to the parent — otherwise the
6537  /// document would go on building into a detached subtree.
6538  ///
6539  /// The node's box leaves the boxes of its parent and of the parent's
6540  /// auto-opened ancestors (Perl `removeNode` → `removeNodeBox`,
6541  /// Document.pm:1788-1789): what the node contributed to them is gone.
6542  pub fn remove_node(&mut self, node: Node) {
6543    self.remove_node_with_box_action(node, NodeBoxAction::Unlink)
6544  }
6545
6546  /// [`remove_node`](Self::remove_node) for a node whose content lives on in
6547  /// another node, so its box stays in the boxes it is part of: a copy
6548  /// (`append_tree`; Perl's `appendChild` moves the node itself — `\sideset`'s
6549  /// nucleus, amsmath), a renamed node, a token a math ligature merged, a node
6550  /// its replacements stand for (Perl's `replaceChild` has moved it into a
6551  /// document fragment, where `removeNodeBox` finds no element to update).
6552  /// Unlinking these boxes took pieces out of the reversions that `tex=` is
6553  /// read from (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #272).
6554  pub fn remove_node_keeping_box(&mut self, node: Node) {
6555    self.remove_node_with_box_action(node, NodeBoxAction::Keep)
6556  }
6557
6558  /// The shared body of [`remove_node`](Self::remove_node) and
6559  /// [`remove_node_keeping_box`](Self::remove_node_keeping_box): `box_action`
6560  /// says whether the node's box is unlinked from its enclosing boxes.
6561  fn remove_node_with_box_action(&mut self, node: Node, box_action: NodeBoxAction) {
6562    let mut chopped: bool = self.node == node; // Note if we're removing insertion point
6563    if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
6564      // If an element, do ID bookkeeping.
6565      if let Some(id) = node.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
6566        self.unrecord_id(&id);
6567      }
6568      if box_action == NodeBoxAction::Unlink
6569        && let Some(nodebox) = self.get_node_box(&node)
6570        && let Some(parent) = node.get_parent()
6571      {
6572        self.remove_node_box(&parent, &nodebox);
6573      }
6574      for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
6575        chopped = chopped || self.remove_node_aux(child);
6576      }
6577    }
6578    if let Some(parent) = node.get_parent() {
6579      if chopped {
6580        // Don't remove insertion point!
6581        self.set_node(&parent);
6582      }
6583      // Perl's `removeChild` hands the node to XML::LibXML's proxy GC, which
6584      // frees it with the last reference. Here an unlinked node whose
6585      // `node->doc` is still set is freed by NOBODY (the fork's `Drop` frees
6586      // only doc-less nodes, and `xmlFreeDoc` never reaches an orphan), so a
6587      // bare `unlink` leaked every removed subtree for the process lifetime:
6588      // ~5-6 MB per tikz picture of pgfsys transient `svg:g` groups dropped
6589      // by `collapse_svg_group`, eager and streaming alike (pgf-PeriodicTable
6590      // n8: the glibc heap climbed 11 → 47 MB across eight spilled tables and
6591      // the manual reached 742 MB of orphans by fragment 256). The ids are
6592      // unrecorded above, so `discard_subtree`'s contract holds.
6593      self.discard_subtree(node);
6594    }
6595  }
6596
6597  fn remove_node_aux(&mut self, node: Node) -> bool {
6598    let mut chopped = self.node == node;
6599    if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
6600      // If an element, do ID bookkeeping.
6601      if let Some(id) = node.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
6602        self.unrecord_id(&id);
6603      }
6604      for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
6605        chopped = chopped || self.remove_node_aux(child);
6606      }
6607    }
6608    chopped
6609  }
6610
6611  //**********************************************************************
6612  // Inserting new nodes at random points into the document,
6613  // typically, later in the process or during some kind of rearrangement.
6614
6615  // This is a somewhat strange situation; There are commands and environments
6616  // that do some interesting thing to their contents. This include things like
6617  // center, flushleft, or rotate, or ...
6618  // Naively one is tempted to create a containing block with appropriate type &
6619  // attributes. However, since these things can be allowed in so many places
6620  // by LaTeX, that one has a difficult time creating a sensible document model.
6621  // The purpose of transformingBlock is to set the contents (possibly creating a
6622  // consistent <p> around them, if called for), and returning the list of newly
6623  // created nodes. These nodes can then have appropriate attributes added as
6624  // needed for each specific case.
6625
6626  // Since this situation can occur in both LaTeX and AmSTeX type documents,
6627  // we'll put it in the TeX pool so it can be reused.
6628
6629  // Tricky bit for creating nodes late in the game,
6630
6631  ////// See createElementAt
6632  /// This opens a new element at the _specified_ point, rather than the current insertion point.
6633  /// This is useful during document rearrangement or augmentation that may be needed later
6634  /// in the process.
6635  pub fn open_element_at(
6636    &mut self,
6637    point: &mut Node,
6638    qname: &str,
6639    attributes: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
6640    font_opt: Option<Font>,
6641  ) -> Result<Node> {
6642    self.open_element_at_with_box(point, qname, attributes, font_opt, None)
6643  }
6644
6645  /// [`open_element_at`](Self::open_element_at) with Perl's `_box` attribute:
6646  /// `requested_box` is the box the new node records, ahead of the insertion
6647  /// point's box and the box being absorbed (Document.pm:1861).
6648  fn open_element_at_with_box(
6649    &mut self,
6650    point: &mut Node,
6651    qname: &str,
6652    attributes: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
6653    mut font_opt: Option<Font>,
6654    requested_box: Option<Digested>,
6655  ) -> Result<Node> {
6656    // Font resolution priority (matching Perl's openElement/openElementAt):
6657    // 1. Explicit font_opt parameter
6658    // 2. _font attribute in attributes hash
6659    // 3. box_to_absorb.get_font() — the font of the current box being absorbed (Perl:
6660    //    $attributes{_box} = $LaTeXML::BOX; $font = $attributes{_box}->getFont)
6661    // 4. Insertion point's font (final fallback, handled later)
6662    if font_opt.is_none()
6663      && let Some(ref attrs) = attributes
6664      && let Some(fontid) = attrs.get("_font")
6665    {
6666      // Tolerate non-numeric `_font` attributes — see get_node_font
6667      // for the same defensive read; same panic site, different
6668      // call. Driver: 2406.14188.
6669      if let Ok(id) = fontid.parse::<u64>() {
6670        font_opt = self.node_fonts.get(&id).cloned();
6671      }
6672    }
6673    if font_opt.is_none()
6674      && let Some(ref digested) = self.box_to_absorb
6675      && let Ok(Some(font)) = digested.get_font()
6676    {
6677      font_opt = Some((*font).clone());
6678    }
6679    let (decoded_ns, tag) = model::decode_qname(qname)?;
6680    let mut newnode;
6681    // box = self.node_boxes.get(box);    // may already be the string key
6682    // If this will be the document root node, things are slightly more involved.
6683    if point.get_type() == Some(NodeType::DocumentNode) {
6684      // First node! (?)
6685      Debug!("adding schema declaration, new node will be : {}", tag);
6686      model::add_schema_declaration(self);
6687      newnode = Node::new(&tag, None, &self.document).unwrap();
6688      self.record_constructed_node(&newnode);
6689      self.document.set_root_element(&newnode);
6690      for node in &mut self.pending {
6691        newnode.add_prev_sibling(node)?; // Add saved comments, PI's
6692      }
6693
6694      if let Some(ns) = decoded_ns {
6695        // Here, we're creating the initial, document element, which will hold ALL of
6696        // the namespace declarations. If there is a default namespace (no
6697        // prefix), that will also be declared, and applied here. However, if
6698        // there is ALSO a prefix associated with that namespace, we have to declare it
6699        // FIRST due to the (apparently) buggy way that XML::LibXML works with
6700        // namespaces in setAttributeNS.
6701        let prefix_opt = model::get_document_namespace_prefix(&ns, false, false);
6702        let attprefix_opt = model::get_document_namespace_prefix(&ns, true, true);
6703        if prefix_opt.is_none()
6704          && let Some(attprefix_sym) = attprefix_opt
6705        {
6706          let attr_ns_node = arena::with(attprefix_sym, |attprefix| {
6707            Namespace::new(attprefix, &ns, &mut newnode)
6708          })
6709          .unwrap();
6710          newnode.set_namespace(&attr_ns_node)?;
6711        }
6712        // TODO: Figure out a better way to achieve the "activate" effect in
6713        // XML:LibXML::Element it seems just creating the namespace without
6714        // setting it is equivalent ??
6715        let ns_node = Namespace::new("", &ns, &mut newnode).unwrap();
6716        newnode.set_namespace(&ns_node)?;
6717      }
6718    } else {
6719      if font_opt.is_none() {
6720        font_opt = Some(self.get_node_font(point).clone());
6721      }
6722      newnode = self.open_element_internal(point, decoded_ns, &tag)?;
6723    }
6724
6725    // Source-locator stamping (`--source-map`, issues #47/#92). `open_element_at`
6726    // is the shared element-creation primitive (plain `open_element`, math, and
6727    // alignment all route here), so stamping here covers them uniformly —
6728    // including the `ltx:Math` wrapper that bypasses `open_element`. Off by
6729    // default; the cheap gate keeps the normal path free.
6730    if state::source_map_enabled() {
6731      self.stamp_source_locator(&newnode, qname);
6732    }
6733
6734    if let Some(attrs) = attributes {
6735      let mut sorted_keys = attrs.keys().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>();
6736      sorted_keys.sort_unstable();
6737      for key in sorted_keys {
6738        if key == "font" || key == "locator" {
6739          continue;
6740        }
6741        self.set_attribute(&mut newnode, key, &attrs[key])?;
6742      }
6743    }
6744    if let Some(font) = font_opt {
6745      self.set_node_font(&mut newnode, &font)?;
6746    }
6747
6748    // Perl Document.pm:1861-1862: the new node's box is the requested `_box`
6749    // (`openElement` passes `$LaTeXML::BOX`), else the insertion point's box,
6750    // else `$LaTeXML::BOX`; and `appendNodeBox` records it on the new node AND
6751    // extends the box of every auto-opened ancestor with it, so an auto-opened
6752    // `ltx:picture` or `svg:foreignObject` measures everything opened inside it,
6753    // not just the box that opened it (batch 56iy's residual). Guard:
6754    // `node_box_append::*`. (A `Digested` clone is an `Rc` clone.)
6755    let node_box = requested_box
6756      .or_else(|| self.get_node_box(point))
6757      .or_else(|| self.box_to_absorb.clone());
6758    // A fresh node holds only this box (its pointer key may be a freed node's
6759    // stale entry, which must not combine with it); the walk then goes on
6760    // from the parent, as Perl's `appendNodeBox` finds the new node holding it.
6761    if let Some(node_box) = node_box {
6762      self
6763        .node_boxes
6764        .insert(newnode.to_hashable(), node_box.clone());
6765      if let Some(parent) = newnode.get_parent()
6766        && is_autoopened_element(&parent)
6767      {
6768        self.append_node_box(&parent, &node_box);
6769      }
6770    }
6771
6772    // Debug!(
6773    //   s!("Inserting {:?} into {:?}", get_node_qname(&newnode), get_node_qname(point))
6774    // );
6775
6776    // Run afterOpen operations
6777    self.after_open(&mut newnode)?;
6778
6779    Ok(newnode)
6780  }
6781
6782  fn open_element_internal(
6783    &mut self,
6784    point: &mut Node,
6785    ns_opt: Option<String>,
6786    tag: &str,
6787  ) -> Result<Node> {
6788    // TODO:
6789    //
6790    // I am seriously irritated by the XML namespace and the confusion of the "default#"
6791    // tricks and libxml2's custom decisions about namespace interactions
6792    //
6793    // I have "hacked together" a working flow for now, but I expect to
6794    // encounter bugs related to the shortcuts taken here. I would welcome a
6795    // redesign       that simplifies the namespace logic dramatically.
6796    let new_ns = match ns_opt {
6797      Some(ns_uri) => {
6798        match point.lookup_namespace_prefix(&ns_uri) {
6799          // namespace not already declared?
6800          None => {
6801            if let Some(prefix) = model::get_document_namespace_prefix(&ns_uri, false, false) {
6802              if prefix != pin!("") {
6803                let mut root = self.document.get_root_element().unwrap();
6804                match arena::with(prefix, |prefix_str| {
6805                  Namespace::new(prefix_str, &ns_uri, &mut root)
6806                }) {
6807                  Ok(ns) => Some(ns),
6808                  Err(_) => {
6809                    // The namespace already exists on root (declared by an
6810                    // earlier element of the same namespace — e.g. a prior
6811                    // tikz/SVG picture) but `lookup_namespace_prefix` did not
6812                    // find it from this deeply-nested insertion point. Recover
6813                    // by reusing the root declaration (or creating it on the
6814                    // insertion point), exactly as the already-declared branch
6815                    // below — do NOT drop the namespace. Witness 1802.00756:
6816                    // a `tikzpicture` inside a nested `gather*`/`minipage`/
6817                    // `figure*` emitted 14× "failed to create namespace: svg"
6818                    // and the `<svg:svg>`/`<svg:g>` lost their namespace.
6819                    arena::with(prefix, |prefix_str| {
6820                      let found = root
6821                        .get_namespace_declarations()
6822                        .into_iter()
6823                        .find(|ns| ns.get_prefix() == prefix_str);
6824                      if found.is_none() {
6825                        Namespace::new(prefix_str, &ns_uri, point).ok()
6826                      } else {
6827                        found
6828                      }
6829                    })
6830                  },
6831                }
6832              } else {
6833                // default namespace?
6834                None
6835              }
6836            } else {
6837              // default namespace?
6838              None
6839            }
6840          },
6841          Some(prefix) => {
6842            if !prefix.is_empty() {
6843              let mut root = self.document.get_root_element().unwrap();
6844              match Namespace::new(&prefix, &ns_uri, &mut root) {
6845                Ok(ns) => Some(ns),
6846                Err(_) => {
6847                  // Namespace already exists on root — find and reuse it.
6848                  // We search declarations then fall back to creating on the
6849                  // insertion point (which inherits from root).
6850                  let found = root
6851                    .get_namespace_declarations()
6852                    .into_iter()
6853                    .find(|ns| ns.get_prefix() == prefix);
6854                  if found.is_none() {
6855                    // Try creating on the insertion point instead
6856                    Namespace::new(&prefix, &ns_uri, point).ok()
6857                  } else {
6858                    found
6859                  }
6860                },
6861              }
6862            } else {
6863              // default namespace?
6864              None
6865            }
6866          },
6867        }
6868      },
6869      None => None,
6870    };
6871
6872    let no_ns = new_ns.is_none();
6873    let mut newnode = match Node::new(tag, new_ns.clone(), &self.document) {
6874      Ok(n) => n,
6875      Err(_) => {
6876        // libxml2 rejected the tag (e.g. NUL byte, malformed name).
6877        // Bail out of element creation rather than aborting; caller
6878        // can recover. Driver: 2304.07380 panic at Node::new unwrap.
6879        let message = s!("failed to create element {:?}", tag);
6880        Error!("document", "open_element_internal", message);
6881        return Err(message.into());
6882      },
6883    };
6884    point.add_child(&mut newnode)?;
6885    if no_ns {
6886      // When no explicit namespace was determined (default namespace element),
6887      // try to find the root's default namespace first. This prevents inheriting
6888      // the parent's namespace when inside a different namespace context (e.g.,
6889      // SVG elements getting svg: prefix on LaTeXML elements like Math/XMath).
6890      let root_ns = self
6891        .document
6892        .get_root_element()
6893        .and_then(|r| r.get_namespace());
6894      let parent_ns = point.get_namespace();
6895      if let Some(ref rns) = root_ns {
6896        // Use root's namespace for default-namespace elements
6897        let _ = newnode.set_namespace(rns);
6898      } else if let Some(ns) = parent_ns {
6899        // Fallback: inherit from parent (original behavior)
6900        newnode.set_namespace(&ns)?;
6901      }
6902    } else if let Some(ref ns) = new_ns {
6903      // For explicitly namespaced elements (e.g., svg:svg), ensure the namespace
6904      // is set after add_child — Node::new may not properly bind the namespace
6905      // when the Namespace was retrieved from get_namespace_declarations().
6906      let _ = newnode.set_namespace(ns);
6907    }
6908
6909    self.record_constructed_node(&newnode);
6910    Ok(newnode)
6911  }
6912
6913  /// Whenever a node has been created using openElementAt,
6914  /// closeElementAt ought to be used to close it, when you're finished inserting into $node.
6915  /// Basically, this just runs any afterClose operations.
6916  pub fn close_element_at(&mut self, node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> { self.after_close(node) }
6917
6918  pub fn after_open(&mut self, node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
6919    // Streaming pass 1: the root's LATE hooks are deferred to
6920    // end-of-digestion (their eager semantics are "digestion complete") but
6921    // its early/normal hooks — structural work like the pending-resource
6922    // drain, which mid-digestion consumers depend on — still run at open.
6923    // See the `defer_root_after_open` field docs.
6924    if self.defer_root_after_open && self.document.get_root_element().as_ref() == Some(node) {
6925      let savenode = self.node.clone();
6926      self.set_node(node);
6927      let node_qname = get_node_qname(node);
6928      let box_opt = self.get_node_box(node);
6929      let (prompt, _late) = self.get_tag_action_list_parts(node_qname, TagOptionName::AfterOpen);
6930      for action in prompt {
6931        action(self, node, box_opt.as_ref())?;
6932      }
6933      self.set_node(&savenode);
6934      return Ok(());
6935    }
6936    // Set current point to this node, just in case the afterOpen's use it.
6937    let savenode = self.node.clone();
6938    self.set_node(node);
6939    let node_qname = get_node_qname(node);
6940    // Perl: my $box = getNodeBox($self, $node);
6941    let box_opt = self.get_node_box(node);
6942    for action in self.get_tag_action_list(node_qname, TagOptionName::AfterOpen) {
6943      action(self, node, box_opt.as_ref())?;
6944    }
6945    self.set_node(&savenode);
6946    Ok(())
6947  }
6948
6949  pub fn after_close(&mut self, node: &mut Node) -> Result<()> {
6950    // Should we set point to this node? (or to last child, or something ??
6951    let savenode = self.node.clone();
6952    let node_qname = get_node_qname(node);
6953    // Perl: my $box = getNodeBox($self, $node);
6954    let box_opt = self.get_node_box(node);
6955    for action in self.get_tag_action_list(node_qname, TagOptionName::AfterClose) {
6956      action(self, node, box_opt.as_ref())?;
6957    }
6958    // (unless a hook removed the node it stood on — algorithm2e's listing drops an empty line the close walk began
6959    // in — where `remove_node` already moved the point)
6960    if !savenode.is_null() {
6961      self.set_node(&savenode);
6962    }
6963    Ok(())
6964  }
6965
6966  //**********************************************************************
6967  // Appending clones of nodes
6968
6969  // Inserting clones of nodes into the document.
6970  // Nodes that exist in some other part of the document (or some other document)
6971  /// Append COPIES of `new_children` under `node`.
6972  ///
6973  /// Cloning rather than moving is what makes this usable on nodes that belong
6974  /// to another document — moving them would remove them from it. Three things
6975  /// are repaired on the way in: document fragments are expanded to their
6976  /// children, the namespace structure is rebuilt clean (libxml2 otherwise has
6977  /// a tendency to introduce annoying "default" namespace prefix
6978  /// declarations), and every `xml:id` in the copy is rewritten to a fresh id,
6979  /// with internal references remapped to match — otherwise the copy would
6980  /// duplicate the original's ids.
6981  // # Should have variants here for prepend, insert before, insert after.... ???
6982  pub fn append_clone(&mut self, node: &mut Node, new_children: Vec<Node>) -> Result<()> {
6983    // Expand any document fragments
6984    let new_children = new_children
6985      .into_iter()
6986      .flat_map(|child| {
6987        if child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::DocumentFragNode) {
6988          child.get_child_nodes()
6989        } else {
6990          vec![child]
6991        }
6992      })
6993      .collect::<Vec<Node>>();
6994    // Now find all xml:id's in the new_children and record replacement id's for them
6995    let mut id_map = HashMap::default();
6996    // Find all id's defined in the copy and change the id.
6997    // Note: XPath ".//@xml:id" can fail to find namespace-qualified attributes.
6998    // Use DOM walking as fallback to ensure all ids are found.
6999    for child in new_children.iter() {
7000      let mut xpath_ids: Vec<String> = self.findvalues(".//@xml:id", Some(child));
7001      if xpath_ids.is_empty() {
7002        // Fallback: walk DOM to find xml:id attributes
7003        Self::collect_xml_ids_from(child, &mut xpath_ids);
7004      }
7005      for id in xpath_ids {
7006        id_map.insert(id.clone(), self.modify_id(id));
7007      }
7008    }
7009    // Now do the cloning (actually copying) and insertion.
7010    self.append_clone_aux(node, new_children, &mut id_map)
7011  }
7012
7013  /// Walk DOM to collect xml:id attribute values (fallback when XPath fails).
7014  fn collect_xml_ids_from(node: &Node, ids: &mut Vec<String>) {
7015    if let Some(id) = node.get_attribute("xml:id") {
7016      ids.push(id);
7017    } else if let Some(id) = node.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
7018      ids.push(id);
7019    }
7020    for child in node.get_child_nodes() {
7021      if child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
7022        Self::collect_xml_ids_from(&child, ids);
7023      }
7024    }
7025  }
7026
7027  fn append_clone_aux(
7028    &mut self,
7029    node: &mut Node,
7030    new_children: Vec<Node>,
7031    id_map: &mut HashMap<String, String>,
7032  ) -> Result<()> {
7033    for child in new_children.into_iter() {
7034      match child.get_type() {
7035        Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => {
7036          let mut new = self.open_element_internal(
7037            node,
7038            child.get_namespace().map(|ns| ns.get_href()),
7039            &child.get_name(),
7040          )?;
7041          // Key order: `get_attributes` is a HashMap, libxml appends on set —
7042          // sort so a cloned subtree serializes deterministically
7043          // (`open_element_at` emits sorted; Perl's native clone keeps it).
7044          let mut attrs: Vec<(String, String)> = child.get_attributes().into_iter().collect();
7045          attrs.sort();
7046          // `get_attributes` names both an `xml:id` and an SVG element's plain `id` (the svg
7047          // schema's ID attribute) "id". Perl remaps only `xml:id` and copies every other
7048          // attribute as it is (Document.pm:1943-1954), so an SVG element's own `id` is copied
7049          // verbatim: remapped into an `xml:id`, the copy was schema-invalid (tikz-shields-doc,
7050          // a TikZ badge in a frontmatter contact). Only on SVG elements: elsewhere a bare `id`
7051          // stays the `xml:id` whose namespace a cloneNode stripped (1410.8508, below).
7052          let svg_id = if with_node_qname(&child, |qname| qname.starts_with("svg:")) {
7053            child.get_attribute_no_ns("id")
7054          } else {
7055            None
7056          };
7057          for (key, val) in attrs {
7058            match key.as_str() {
7059              // The walked mark of `record_svg_ids` stays on the original: the clone is a second
7060              // copy, so its own `svg:svg` close renames the ids it repeats, with their references.
7061              "_svgid" => {},
7062              "xml:id" | "id" if svg_id.is_some() => {
7063                new.set_attribute("id", svg_id.as_deref().unwrap_or_default())?;
7064              },
7065              "xml:id" | "id" => {
7066                // Use the replacement id. The pre-walk
7067                // (findvalues/collect_xml_ids_from) normally populates
7068                // id_map with every `xml:id` it can see, but the
7069                // namespace/prefix of the attribute key returned by
7070                // libxml2's `get_attributes()` can differ from what the
7071                // XPath / DOM walk picked up (e.g. when the incoming
7072                // node's tree came through a cloneNode that stripped
7073                // the xml namespace). Fall back to minting a fresh
7074                // replacement id on-the-fly rather than panicking —
7075                // 1410.8508 hit this when the pre-walk found zero ids
7076                // but attributes on a child node did carry xml:id.
7077                let fresh;
7078                let mapped_id = match id_map.get(&val) {
7079                  Some(id) => id,
7080                  None => {
7081                    fresh = self.modify_id(val.clone());
7082                    id_map.insert(val.clone(), fresh.clone());
7083                    id_map.get(&val).unwrap()
7084                  },
7085                };
7086                let newid = self.record_id_with_node(mapped_id, &new);
7087                // Write the literal "xml:id" key (not the bare "id" local-
7088                // name returned by libxml's get_attributes). Otherwise the
7089                // cloned node only gets a plain `id` attribute, and the
7090                // subsequent `after_open` chain's `has_attribute_ns("id",
7091                // XML_NS)` check returns false, causing `generate_id` to
7092                // mint a fresh `.<parent>.N` xml:id that doesn't match the
7093                // sibling XMRef idrefs (which were rewritten from id_map).
7094                // Witness: arXiv:2509.07628 — MathFork mainfork emitted
7095                // 154 XMRefs with `.mf` idrefs while the cloned target
7096                // nodes received parent-scoped `.m2.N` xml:ids, leaving
7097                // every XMRef dangling and triggering 4
7098                // `Error:expected:id` per equation during post-processing
7099                // visibility marking. Same shape applies anywhere a
7100                // cloned subtree carries xml:id attributes — MathFork,
7101                // tabular-cell clone, _Capture_ flush.
7102                new.set_attribute("xml:id", &newid)?;
7103                // Update id_map so subsequent idref lookups use the ACTUAL recorded id.
7104                // record_id_with_node may change the id (e.g., if there are conflicts),
7105                // so the mapped_id and newid may differ.
7106                if *mapped_id != newid {
7107                  id_map.insert(val.clone(), newid);
7108                }
7109              },
7110              "idref" => {
7111                // Refer to the replacement id if it was replaced
7112                let id = id_map.get(&val).unwrap_or(&val);
7113                new.set_attribute(&key, id)?;
7114              },
7115              other_key =>
7116              // TODO: Are namespaced attributes successfully handled here? Check.
7117              {
7118                new.set_attribute(other_key, &val)?
7119              },
7120            };
7121          }
7122          // Carry the source node's box onto the clone, matching Perl: its
7123          // `cloneNode` copies the internal `_box` attribute, so `getNodeBox`
7124          // still resolves on the clone. Our node box is a side map keyed by
7125          // node identity, so a fresh clone is box-less unless carried
7126          // explicitly — the same invariant repaired in `rename_node_internal`
7127          // for arXiv/html_feedback#6873. This completes node-box carrying
7128          // across all four node-creating ops (open / wrap / rename / clone).
7129          // Latent today — the current `append_clone` sites (MathFork, contacts)
7130          // don't re-read a clone's box for size, and box-derived outputs
7131          // (`tex=`, ids) ride across as copied attributes — but it keeps a
7132          // future size-dependent afterClose on cloned SVG content from
7133          // silently misfiring the way the foreignObject y-flip transform did.
7134          if let Some(childbox) = self.get_node_box(&child) {
7135            self.set_node_box(&new, childbox);
7136          }
7137          self.after_open(&mut new)?;
7138          self.append_clone_aux(&mut new, child.get_child_nodes(), id_map)?;
7139          self.after_close(&mut new)?;
7140        },
7141        Some(NodeType::TextNode) => node.append_text(&child.get_content())?,
7142        Some(NodeType::CommentNode) => {
7143          // Skip XML comments during cloning (Perl also skips them in most contexts)
7144        },
7145        other => {
7146          emit_warn(
7147            "internal",
7148            "document",
7149            &format!("append_clone_aux: skipping unsupported {other:?} node type"),
7150          );
7151        },
7152      };
7153    }
7154    Ok(())
7155  }
7156
7157  //**********************************************************************
7158  // Wrapping & Unwrapping nodes by another element.
7159
7160  /// Wrap `nodes` with an element named `qname`, making the new element replace
7161  /// the first `node`, and all `nodes` becomes the child of the new node.
7162  /// \[this makes most sense if `nodes` are a sequence of siblings\]
7163  ///
7164  /// Returns `None` if `qname` isn't allowed in the parent, or if `nodes`
7165  /// aren't allowed in `qname`, otherwise the newly created `qname` — so a
7166  /// caller must treat "wrapped" as a request the model may decline, not as a
7167  /// guarantee. `None` also covers a first node with no parent (already
7168  /// detached, or the root): there is nothing to wrap it in place of. Witness
7169  /// 1804.09736.
7170  ///
7171  /// The wrapper inherits the parent's font and box, so wrapping does not
7172  /// change how the enclosed material renders. [`unwrap_nodes`](Self::unwrap_nodes)
7173  /// is the inverse.
7174  pub fn wrap_nodes(&mut self, qname: &str, nodes: Vec<Node>) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
7175    self.wrap_nodes_as(qname, nodes, &[])
7176  }
7177
7178  /// [`wrap_nodes`](Self::wrap_nodes), the wrapper carrying `attributes` from its opening, so its
7179  /// `after_open`/`after_close` hooks see them: an `xml:id` given here is the one `generate_id`
7180  /// keeps.
7181  pub fn wrap_nodes_as(
7182    &mut self,
7183    qname: &str,
7184    nodes: Vec<Node>,
7185    attributes: &[(String, String)],
7186  ) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
7187    if nodes.is_empty() {
7188      return Ok(None);
7189    }
7190    let first_node = &nodes[0];
7191    // Can't wrap a node that has no parent (already detached / is the root) —
7192    // return None like the other "can't wrap here" paths. Witness: 1804.09736.
7193    let Some(mut parent) = first_node.get_parent() else {
7194      return Ok(None);
7195    };
7196    let (ns, tag) = model::decode_qname(qname)?;
7197    let mut new = self.open_element_internal(&mut parent, ns, &tag)?;
7198    for (name, value) in attributes {
7199      self.set_attribute(&mut new, name, value)?;
7200    }
7201    self.after_open(&mut new)?;
7202    parent.replace_child_node(new.clone(), first_node.clone())?;
7203
7204    self.copy_node_font(&parent, &mut new)?;
7205
7206    if let Some(tbox) = self.get_node_box(&parent) {
7207      self.set_node_box(&new, tbox);
7208    }
7209    for mut node in nodes.into_iter() {
7210      node.unlink();
7211      new.add_child(&mut node)?;
7212    }
7213    self.after_close(&mut new)?;
7214    Ok(Some(new))
7215  }
7216
7217  /// Unwrap the children of $node, by replacing $node by its children.
7218  pub fn unwrap_nodes(&mut self, node: Node) -> Result<()> {
7219    let children = node.get_child_nodes();
7220    self.replace_node(node, children)
7221  }
7222
7223  /// Replace `node` by `nodes` (presumably descendants of some kind?)
7224  // DG: Don't return the replaced `node`, as it is groudns for memory management trouble
7225  //     with the low-level libxml layer. I've encountered segfaults here.
7226  ///
7227  /// No box changes hands (Perl Document.pm:2011-2025): Perl's first
7228  /// `replaceChild` moves `node` into a document fragment, so its `removeNode`
7229  /// finds no parent element whose box to update, and its closing
7230  /// `appendNodeBox` map runs over the `@nodes` its `while (shift)` loop has
7231  /// emptied. Only a `node` replaced by nothing leaves its parent's box, as
7232  /// `removeNode` does. The `\@framebox` unwrap inside an auto-opened picture
7233  /// keeps the frame's size (`x \put(0,0){A} \fbox{…} y`). Guard:
7234  /// `node_box_append::replacing_a_node_keeps_the_boxes`.
7235  pub fn replace_node(&mut self, mut node: Node, with: Vec<Node>) -> Result<()> {
7236    if node.get_parent().is_some() {
7237      let replaced = !with.is_empty();
7238      // libxml2's xmlAddNextSibling merges consecutive text nodes: when both
7239      // the reference sibling and the new node are TextNode, it appends the
7240      // new node's content to the reference node and frees the new node. The
7241      // Rust wrapper doesn't surface the merged result, so naively advancing
7242      // `c0_opt` to `with_node` would capture a pointer to freed memory,
7243      // producing silent data loss for the third+ insertion and eventually
7244      // a libxml2 SIGSEGV when the dangling pointer is re-traversed (e.g.
7245      // during a later XPath evaluation). Detect the text-text case and
7246      // coalesce in-place instead.
7247      let mut c0_opt: Option<Node> = None;
7248      for mut with_node in with.into_iter() {
7249        with_node.unlink();
7250        let is_text = with_node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode);
7251        if let Some(mut c0) = c0_opt {
7252          let c0_is_text = c0.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode);
7253          if is_text && c0_is_text {
7254            let existing = c0.get_content();
7255            let added = with_node.get_content();
7256            c0.set_content(&format!("{existing}{added}"))?;
7257            // with_node is a standalone (unlinked) text node whose content
7258            // now lives in c0: free it (see `remove_node`).
7259            self.discard_subtree(with_node);
7260            c0_opt = Some(c0);
7261            continue;
7262          }
7263          c0.add_next_sibling(&mut with_node)?;
7264        } else {
7265          // first node, swap in
7266          node.add_next_sibling(&mut with_node)?;
7267        }
7268        c0_opt = Some(with_node);
7269      }
7270      if replaced {
7271        self.remove_node_keeping_box(node);
7272      } else {
7273        self.remove_node(node);
7274      }
7275    }
7276    Ok(())
7277  }
7278
7279  /// Replace `node` by `with` as Perl's `replaceTree` (Document.pm:2079-2091)
7280  /// does with their boxes: `node`'s box leaves its parent's (`removeNode`
7281  /// while `node` is still in place), then each element of `with` is recorded
7282  /// as `appendTree` → `openElementAt` records a node it re-creates — its own
7283  /// box, else the parent's, else the box being absorbed — which extends an
7284  /// auto-opened parent's box (`appendNodeBox`). `cleanup_math` unwraps a
7285  /// Math that holds only text this way (TeX_Math.pool.ltxml:219): the
7286  /// auto-opened `svg:foreignObject` around an `\hbox` in an xymatrix cell
7287  /// measures the `\hbox` in place of the Math (tests/graphics/xytest).
7288  pub fn replace_node_as_tree(&mut self, node: Node, with: Vec<Node>) -> Result<()> {
7289    let Some(parent) = node.get_parent() else {
7290      return Ok(());
7291    };
7292    if with.is_empty() {
7293      self.remove_node(node);
7294      return Ok(());
7295    }
7296    if let Some(nodebox) = self.get_node_box(&node) {
7297      self.remove_node_box(&parent, &nodebox);
7298    }
7299    let elements: Vec<Node> = with
7300      .iter()
7301      .filter(|n| n.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode))
7302      .cloned()
7303      .collect();
7304    let has_text = elements.len() < with.len();
7305    self.replace_node(node, with)?;
7306    for element in elements {
7307      let element_box = self
7308        .get_node_box(&element)
7309        .or_else(|| self.get_node_box(&parent))
7310        .or_else(|| self.box_to_absorb.clone());
7311      if let Some(element_box) = element_box {
7312        self.append_node_box(&element, &element_box);
7313      }
7314    }
7315    // Text pieces (an `XMHint`'s spaces) Perl's `appendTree` adds raw, with no
7316    // box. An auto-opened `svg:foreignObject` left with no box at all (the
7317    // `$\phantom{H}$` of a quantikz cell) Perl then turns into `svg:text`
7318    // (TeX_Box.pool.ltxml:386-389), which needs no size; the Rust
7319    // foreignObject stays and must be sized, so it records the box being
7320    // absorbed, as text arriving at an auto-opened node does
7321    // (`openText_internal`, Document.pm:1149-1150). OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES
7322    // #319; guard `cluster_schema::empty_node_foreign_object_is_sized`.
7323    if has_text
7324      && is_autoopened_element(&parent)
7325      && get_node_qname(&parent) == pin!("svg:foreignObject")
7326      && self.get_node_box(&parent).is_none()
7327      && let Some(absorbed) = self.box_to_absorb.clone()
7328    {
7329      self.append_node_box(&parent, &absorbed);
7330    }
7331    Ok(())
7332  }
7333
7334  /// Rename an element to `newname`, returning the new node.
7335  ///
7336  /// Not an in-place rename: a fresh element is opened next to the original,
7337  /// the attributes and (when `reinsert`) the children are carried over, and
7338  /// the original is removed. Perl went this way "initially since
7339  /// `$node->setNodeName` was broken in XML::LibXML 1.58", and kept it because
7340  /// building the replacement through the normal open path is what runs the
7341  /// model's checks and `afterOpen` hooks for the new tag — a raw rename would
7342  /// leave an element the schema never vetted.
7343  ///
7344  /// [`rename_node_qsym`](Self::rename_node_qsym) is the same for an already
7345  /// interned name.
7346  pub fn rename_node(&mut self, node: Node, newname: &str, reinsert: bool) -> Result<Node> {
7347    let (ns, tag) = model::decode_qname(newname)?;
7348    let newsym = arena::pin(newname);
7349    self.rename_node_internal(node, newsym, ns, tag, reinsert)
7350  }
7351  pub fn rename_node_qsym(&mut self, node: Node, newsym: SymStr, reinsert: bool) -> Result<Node> {
7352    let (ns, tag) = model::decode_qname_sym(newsym)?;
7353    self.rename_node_internal(node, newsym, ns, tag, reinsert)
7354  }
7355  fn rename_node_internal(
7356    &mut self,
7357    mut node: Node,
7358    newname: SymStr,
7359    ns: Option<String>,
7360    tag: String,
7361    reinsert: bool,
7362  ) -> Result<Node> {
7363    let mut parent = node
7364      .get_parent()
7365      .expect("rename should never be called on an orphan or root node.");
7366    let mut new = self.open_element_internal(&mut parent, ns, &tag)?;
7367    // Move to the position AFTER node
7368    node.add_next_sibling(&mut new)?;
7369    // Copy ALL attributes from `node` to `newnode`, in key order (HashMap
7370    // iteration would serialize the renamed element's attributes in a
7371    // per-process random order; the original was emitted sorted).
7372    let mut id = None;
7373    let mut attrs: Vec<(String, String)> = node.get_attributes().into_iter().collect();
7374    attrs.sort();
7375    for (key, value) in attrs {
7376      // `get_attributes()` returns the `xml:id` attribute under its LOCAL name
7377      // `"id"` (it lives in the XML namespace), NOT the prefixed `"xml:id"`.
7378      // Capture it here so it can be re-registered on `new` AFTER `remove_node`
7379      // unrecords it below — and re-set it through `Document::set_attribute`
7380      // (which routes "id"/"xml:id" through `record_id_with_node` + the XML
7381      // namespace), rather than the raw `Node::set_attribute` copy used for
7382      // ordinary attributes (that would drop the namespace AND the idstore
7383      // registration). Missing this stranded the equation refnum id across
7384      // `rearrange_lone_ams_aligned`'s equation→equationgroup rename, leaving
7385      // the group with a generic paragraph id and dangling intra-math XMRefs
7386      // (witness 2311.01600; see docs/archive/EXPECTED_ID_XMREF_DESIGN_2026-06-08.md).
7387      if key == "xml:id" || key == "id" {
7388        id = Some(value);
7389        continue;
7390      }
7391      let can_have = model::can_have_attribute(newname, arena::pin(&key));
7392      if can_have {
7393        new.set_attribute(&key, &value)?;
7394      }
7395    }
7396    // AND move all content from `node` to `newnode`
7397    if !reinsert {
7398      for mut child in node.get_child_nodes() {
7399        child.unbind();
7400        new.add_child(&mut child)?;
7401      }
7402    } else {
7403      std::mem::swap(&mut self.node, &mut new);
7404      for mut child in node.get_child_nodes() {
7405        child.unbind();
7406        if child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
7407          self.open_text_internal(&child.get_content())?;
7408          self.close_text_internal()?;
7409        } else {
7410          let child_qname = get_node_qname(&child);
7411          let mut point = self.find_insertion_point_qsym(child_qname, None)?;
7412          point.add_child(&mut child)?;
7413        }
7414      }
7415      std::mem::swap(&mut self.node, &mut new);
7416    }
7417    // Carry the node box across the rename. Perl's `renameNode` copies ALL of
7418    // `$node`'s attributes to `$new`, and the box is recorded as the internal
7419    // `_box` attribute, so `afterClose`'s `getNodeBox($new)` still finds it. Our
7420    // node box lives in a side map keyed by node identity — the fresh `new` node
7421    // would otherwise be box-less, so a size-dependent afterClose handler
7422    // misfires. Concretely: `insert_block` renames a `_CaptureBlock_` (which
7423    // carries the block's box) to `svg:foreignObject`; without the box, the fo's
7424    // afterClose (`tex_box.rs`, Perl `TeX_Box.pool.ltxml` L407-423) can't read a
7425    // size and skips the y-flip `transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 h)"`, so a
7426    // `tabular` inside a `tcolorbox` `enhanced` skin renders upside down in the
7427    // TeX-y-up SVG group (arXiv/html_feedback#6873, paper 2601.13118 Table 2).
7428    if let Some(nodebox) = self.get_node_box(&node) {
7429      self.set_node_box(&new, nodebox);
7430    }
7431    // THEN call afterOpen... ?
7432    //   It would normally be called before children added,
7433    //   but how can we know if we're duplicated auto-added stuff?
7434    self.after_open(&mut new)?;
7435    self.after_close(&mut new)?;
7436    // Finally, remove the old node — its box stays where it is: `new` holds it
7437    // and lives on in its place. Perl's `removeNode` here (Document.pm:2064)
7438    // takes the box out of the parent's, so an XMText renamed to XMWrap by
7439    // `cleanup_XMText` drops a `\mbox`/`\raisebox`/`\hbox`/`\resizebox` from an
7440    // aligned cell's `tex` (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #272; witnesses 2605.07372,
7441    // 2605.17816, 2605.23113; guard `node_box_append::aligned_cells_keep_their_boxed_pieces`).
7442    self.remove_node_keeping_box(node);
7443
7444    // and FINALLY, we can register the new node under the id.
7445    // `Document::set_attribute("xml:id", …)` routes through
7446    // `record_id_with_node` (idstore registration + dedup) and sets the
7447    // correctly-namespaced `xml:id` attribute. Only set it when the new qname
7448    // can carry an id (mirrors the per-attribute `can_have_attribute` gate).
7449    if let Some(id) = id
7450      && model::can_have_attribute(newname, arena::pin("xml:id"))
7451    {
7452      self.set_attribute(&mut new, "xml:id", &id)?;
7453    }
7454
7455    Ok(new)
7456  }
7457
7458  /// Whitespace inside an explicit TYPEWRITER text wrapper is verbatim
7459  /// CONTENT (code indentation, measured by the sizing pass) — the p-edge
7460  /// trim recursion must not descend into it. During construction the
7461  /// public `font` attribute may not be written yet, so also decode the
7462  /// internal `_font`. `ltx:verbatim` itself is EXEMPT: Perl's edge trim
7463  /// descends into an inline `\verb` at a paragraph edge and trims its
7464  /// leading space (tokenize/verb.t), and we keep that parity.
7465  fn is_typewriter_wrapper(&self, node: &Node) -> bool {
7466    if node.get_name() == "verbatim" {
7467      return false;
7468    }
7469    if node
7470      .get_attribute("font")
7471      .is_some_and(|f| f.contains("typewriter"))
7472    {
7473      return true;
7474    }
7475    node
7476      .get_attribute("_font")
7477      .and_then(|id| self.decode_font(&id))
7478      .is_some_and(|f| f.family.as_deref() == Some("typewriter"))
7479  }
7480
7481  pub fn trim_node_whitespace(&mut self, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
7482    // A paragraph in a typewriter CONTEXT keeps its whitespace: verbatim
7483    // content is line-mapped into ltx:p's (fancyvrb et al.), where leading
7484    // spaces ARE the code indentation (2605.00468 JSON schemas flush-left)
7485    // and a space-only line is real content. Keyed on the PARENT's font
7486    // context — NOT on the node's own computed font, which is stamped from
7487    // whichever box auto-opened it (a prose paragraph STARTING with inline
7488    // \verb reads as typewriter and would wrongly keep its trailing prose
7489    // whitespace; tokenize/verb.t). Perl's own {verbatim} lands in
7490    // ltx:verbatim (no trim hook) so it never faces this; the raw-fancyvrb
7491    // constructs that do cannot be converted by Perl at all (fvextra
7492    // breaklines exceeds 7 min on a 6-line file) — surpass-Perl scope.
7493    if let Some(parent) = node.get_parent()
7494      && self.get_node_font(&parent).family.as_deref() == Some("typewriter")
7495    {
7496      return Ok(());
7497    }
7498    self.trim_node_left_whitespace(node)?;
7499    self.trim_node_right_whitespace(node)?;
7500    Ok(())
7501  }
7502
7503  fn trim_node_left_whitespace(&self, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
7504    // An empty construction-time marker (`*_Capture_`: the frontmatter position mark, the cover-title marks) is no
7505    // content: the trim reaches past it, as it would were the marker not there.
7506    let mut candidate = node.get_first_child();
7507    while let Some(ref child) = candidate {
7508      if is_empty_capture_mark(child) {
7509        candidate = child.get_next_sibling();
7510      } else {
7511        break;
7512      }
7513    }
7514    if let Some(mut first_child) = candidate {
7515      match first_child.get_type() {
7516        Some(NodeType::TextNode) => {
7517          let content = first_child.get_content();
7518          // Perl: s/^ +// — only trim ASCII spaces, preserve unicode spaces (nbsp, em-space, etc.)
7519          let trimmed_content = content.trim_start_matches(' ');
7520          if !content.is_empty() && (trimmed_content != content) {
7521            first_child.set_content(trimmed_content)?;
7522          }
7523        },
7524        Some(NodeType::ElementNode) if !self.is_typewriter_wrapper(&first_child) => {
7525          self.trim_node_left_whitespace(&first_child)?
7526        },
7527        _ => {},
7528      };
7529    }
7530    Ok(())
7531  }
7532
7533  fn trim_node_right_whitespace(&mut self, node: &Node) -> Result<()> {
7534    // Skip trailing empty <text> font wrapper elements to find the real last content.
7535    // These are artifacts of font change tracking during alignment absorption.
7536    let mut candidate = node.get_last_child();
7537    while let Some(ref child) = candidate {
7538      if (child.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
7539        && child.get_name() == "text"
7540        && child.get_first_child().is_none()
7541        && child.has_attribute("_noautoclose"))
7542        // …and an empty construction-time marker (`trim_node_left_whitespace`)
7543        || is_empty_capture_mark(child)
7544      {
7545        candidate = child.get_prev_sibling();
7546      } else {
7547        break;
7548      }
7549    }
7550    if let Some(mut last_child) = candidate {
7551      match last_child.get_type() {
7552        Some(NodeType::TextNode) => {
7553          let content = last_child.get_content();
7554          // Perl: s/\s+$// (TeX_Paragraph.pool.ltxml:190), all Unicode
7555          // whitespace: a U+2009 after text (babel french), the U+2002 U+200A
7556          // a classed column rule leaves at a cell's end (arydshln `:`/`;`,
7557          // repro kernel-alignment/cell_trim_unicode_space.tex). Like Perl's,
7558          // the trim reaches only the last text node, and the two engines
7559          // split text into nodes differently (SYNC_STATUS "A paragraph's
7560          // trailing whitespace").
7561          let trimmed_content = content.trim_end_matches(char::is_whitespace);
7562          if !content.is_empty() && (trimmed_content != content) {
7563            if trimmed_content.is_empty() {
7564              // Remove AND free the entirely-whitespace text node (see
7565              // `remove_node`: a bare unlink leaks it), purging its
7566              // `node_boxes` entry so a later node at the same address cannot
7567              // inherit the phantom box.
7568              self.discard_subtree(last_child);
7569            } else {
7570              last_child.set_content(trimmed_content)?;
7571            }
7572          }
7573        },
7574        Some(NodeType::ElementNode) if !self.is_typewriter_wrapper(&last_child) => {
7575          self.trim_node_right_whitespace(&last_child)?
7576        },
7577        _ => {},
7578      };
7579    }
7580    Ok(())
7581  }
7582
7583  pub fn add_resource(&mut self, resource: Resource) -> Result<()> {
7584    // let savenode_opt = self.float_to_element("ltx:resource", false);
7585    let savenode_opt = None;
7586    let mut attrib: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::default();
7587    attrib.insert(s!("src"), resource.name);
7588    attrib.insert(s!("type"), resource.mimetype);
7589    attrib.insert(s!("media"), resource.media);
7590    let content_box = Digested::from(Tbox {
7591      text: arena::pin(resource.content),
7592      ..Tbox::default()
7593    });
7594    self.insert_element("ltx:resource", vec![&content_box], Some(attrib))?;
7595    if let Some(savenode) = savenode_opt {
7596      self.set_node(&savenode);
7597    }
7598    Ok(())
7599  }
7600
7601  pub fn process_pending_resources(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
7602    let resources: Vec<Resource> = state::take_pending_resources();
7603    for resource in resources {
7604      self.add_resource(resource)?;
7605    }
7606    state::reset_pending_resources();
7607    Ok(())
7608  }
7609
7610  pub fn make_error(&mut self, error_class: &str, content: &str) -> Result<()> {
7611    let savenode_opt = if !self.is_openable("ltx:ERROR") {
7612      self.float_to_element("ltx:ERROR", false)?
7613    } else {
7614      None
7615    };
7616    self.open_element("ltx:ERROR", Some(string_map!("class"=>error_class)), None)?;
7617    // Perl `Document.pm:makeError` L1346: `openText_internal($self,
7618    // ToString($content))`. Drops the failing token name (`\foo`,
7619    // `\bar`, …) as visible text inside the ERROR element so the
7620    // HTML5 `<span class="ltx_ERROR ...">` is not empty. Without
7621    // this, the user sees a zero-width invisible span where the
7622    // problem source should be.
7623    if !content.is_empty() {
7624      self.open_text_internal(content)?;
7625    }
7626    self.close_element("ltx:ERROR")?;
7627    if let Some(savenode) = savenode_opt {
7628      self.set_node(&savenode);
7629    }
7630    Ok(())
7631  }
7632
7633  // The following "floatTo" operations find an appropriate point
7634  // within the document tree preceding the current insertion point.
7635  // They return undef (& issue a warning) if such a point cannot be found.
7636  // Otherwise, they move the current insertion point to the appropriate node,
7637  // and return the previous insertion point.
7638  // After you make whatever changes (insertions or whatever) to the tree,
7639  // you should do
7640  //   document.set_node(savenode)
7641  // to reset the insertion point to where it had been.
7642
7643  /// Whether `node` is the insertion point's element or one of its ancestors.
7644  fn is_open_node(&self, node: &Node) -> bool {
7645    let mut current = Some(self.node.clone());
7646    while let Some(n) = current {
7647      if &n == node {
7648        return true;
7649      }
7650      current = n.get_parent();
7651    }
7652    false
7653  }
7654
7655  /// [`Self::float_to_element`] (closing form) for an element a frontmatter container (`ltx:abstract`…) refuses,
7656  /// when the insertion point is inside one: the element goes to the nearest open ancestor that admits it, as Perl's
7657  /// `floatToElement` places one (Document.pm:1052-1077), and the insertion point comes back (the saved node is
7658  /// returned for the caller to restore), so what follows stays in the container. Elsewhere `None`: the element is
7659  /// inserted where it stands, by [`Self::find_insertion_point`]'s rules. A `\tableofcontents` inside an abstract
7660  /// (1011.3976, 1602.08755, 2007.03709; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #753).
7661  pub fn float_out_of_frontmatter(&mut self, qname: &str) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
7662    if outside_frontmatter_container(&self.node) {
7663      return Ok(None);
7664    }
7665    self.float_to_element(qname, true)
7666  }
7667
7668  /// Find a node in the document that can contain an element `qname`
7669  pub fn float_to_element(&mut self, qname: &str, closeifpossible: bool) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
7670    let mut candidates: VecDeque<Node> = VecDeque::from(self.get_insertion_candidates(&self.node));
7671    let mut closeable = true;
7672    // If the current node can contain already, we're fine right here - just return
7673    if !candidates.is_empty() && can_contain(&candidates[0], qname) {
7674      // Edge case: Don't resume at a text node, if it is current.
7675      // Don't append more to it after other insertions.
7676      if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::TextNode) {
7677        self.set_node(&candidates[0]);
7678      }
7679      return Ok(candidates.pop_front());
7680    }
7681    // The closing form (`^^`) reaches a container by closing up to it, which only an OPEN node — the insertion
7682    // point's element or one of its ancestors — can be (Perl `closeToNode`, Document.pm:869, walks ancestors). The
7683    // candidates also hold a text node's previous siblings (Perl `getInsertionCandidates`, Document.pm:1020-1032,
7684    // there for the non-closing form to enter), so while the walk can still close they are passed over: neither chosen
7685    // nor counted towards `closeable`. Closing to one reported "Attempt to close … which isn't open" over an unchanged
7686    // tree (a minipage that already holds a float, then `\caption` after its `\end{minipage}` line: 2609.15558, 33998);
7687    // and a sibling that cannot auto-close (a Math, a rule) between two such minipages must not stop the closing walk
7688    // and send the float into the earlier box (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #455).
7689    while let Some(candidate) = candidates.front() {
7690      if closeifpossible && closeable && !self.is_open_node(candidate) {
7691        candidates.pop_front();
7692        continue;
7693      }
7694      if can_contain(candidate, qname) {
7695        break;
7696      }
7697      if closeable {
7698        closeable = can_auto_close(candidate);
7699      }
7700      candidates.pop_front();
7701    }
7702    match candidates.pop_front() {
7703      Some(n) => {
7704        if closeifpossible && closeable {
7705          self.close_to_node(&n, false)?;
7706        } else {
7707          let savenode = self.node.clone();
7708          self.set_node(&n);
7709          // Debug!("Floating from " . Stringify($savenode) . " to " . Stringify($n) . " for
7710          // $qname")   if ($$savenode ne $$n) && $LaTeXML::DEBUG{document};
7711          return Ok(Some(savenode));
7712        }
7713      },
7714      _ => {
7715        if can_contain_node_somehow(&self.node, qname).is_none() {
7716          Warn!(
7717            "malformed",
7718            qname,
7719            s!("No open node can contain element '{}'", qname)
7720          );
7721          // self.get_insertion_context())
7722        }
7723      },
7724    }
7725    Ok(None)
7726  }
7727
7728  // find a node that can accept a label.
7729  // A bit more than just whether the element can have the attribute, but
7730  // whether it has an id (and ideally either a refnum or title)
7731  pub fn float_to_label(&mut self) -> Option<Node> { self.float_to_label_for(None) }
7732
7733  /// [`float_to_label`](Self::float_to_label) for a label that names a counter step no element took (`raw_step`, the
7734  /// step's serial: a raw `\refstepcounter`, `binding::counter::current_raw_refstep`), which a picture may carry: a box
7735  /// drawn as a picture frame is the object such a step numbers (tcolorbox's `\refstepcounter` in its phantom code,
7736  /// tcolorbox.sty:2311 and :1154-1161, placed in the frame at :1925; a `\put` in a `picture`), as LaTeX's `\label`
7737  /// after the step names the step's anchor (latex.ltx:14963-14967 `\@currentlabel`). An object another raw step
7738  /// numbered ([`take_raw_refstep_number`](Self::take_raw_refstep_number)) is not this step's: the label climbs past it,
7739  /// as Perl's does (a second `\put` step in one `picture`; pdflatex prints each step's number, an object this port
7740  /// cannot give, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #813). Any other label climbs past a picture, and past an object a raw
7741  /// step numbered (whose number its `\@currentlabel` is not: a `{gather*}` row's `\label` after the `\labelrel` idiom's
7742  /// immediate one, 2310.19138), to the object its step numbered, as Perl's does (Document.pm:1098-1127; the picture
7743  /// carries no `labels` there). Witnesses: 2506.01072
7744  /// (`\newtcbtheorem`), 2505.20088 (`[auto counter]`), 2402.06608 (`[blend into=figures]`), 2609.20563
7745  /// (`\newtcblisting`). An object inside `ltx:Math` (the box of a `\text{\begin{tcolorbox}…}` in a display) is not
7746  /// the step's either: its id does not survive the math's rendering, so the label climbs out of the math to where
7747  /// Perl's lands: a display, which takes the step's number when it has none
7748  /// ([`take_raw_refstep_number`](Self::take_raw_refstep_number): a `{gather*}` row, `\[…\]`) and keeps its own
7749  /// otherwise (a numbered `{equation}`), or past an inline formula the enclosing unit, whose number `\ref` prints
7750  /// (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #813). Repro `cross-references/math_box_label_climbs_to_the_display.tex`.
7751  pub fn float_to_label_for(&mut self, raw_step: Option<i64>) -> Option<Node> {
7752    self.float_to_label_scoped(raw_step, false)
7753  }
7754
7755  /// [`float_to_label_for`](Self::float_to_label_for) for a label that follows a counter step a group has since
7756  /// undone (`after_undone_step`, `binding::counter::label_follows_an_undone_step`): it names the step still in scope,
7757  /// not the object just closed beside it (Perl's last-child start, Document.pm:1103-1104), so the climb starts at the
7758  /// current node. Where no ancestor takes it, Perl's fallback (:1113-1119, the last child, else the root) stays: a
7759  /// label at the document's own level (lastpage's `\AtEndDocument{\label{lastpage}}`) keeps its old place, where the
7760  /// root taking it gave the root an id and renumbered every generated one. Witness math0107195: a `\label` after an
7761  /// inner `equation`, still inside a theorem, names the theorem ("Theorem 5.3"; Perl and int52a the equation's 16,
7762  /// KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1092; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #856). Repro
7763  /// `cross-references/label_after_an_inner_equation_names_the_theorem.tex`.
7764  pub fn float_to_label_scoped(
7765    &mut self,
7766    raw_step: Option<i64>,
7767    after_undone_step: bool,
7768  ) -> Option<Node> {
7769    let key = "labels";
7770    // The object that printed the step's number itself (an algorithm2e line, `note_raw_refstep_object`) takes the
7771    // label wherever it stands, as `\@currentlabel` is that number until the next step: in the line, or after it, at
7772    // the start of the next line or of a block (`stmt\; \label{x}`, `\While{c}{\label{x} …}`: pdflatex the line's
7773    // number). Its id is made only later (the `\lx@label` hook, sect11.rs). Witnesses 2406.05437 (`step1`, `step2`:
7774    // PDF 14, 17), 1602.05866 (`algline:mainloop`, PDF 8); OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #877.
7775    if let Some(object) = raw_step
7776      .and_then(|serial| self.raw_refstep_objects.get(&serial))
7777      .filter(|object| object.get_parent().is_some())
7778      .cloned()
7779    {
7780      let savenode = self.node.clone();
7781      self.set_node(&object);
7782      return Some(savenode);
7783    }
7784    let may_label = |node: &Node| {
7785      can_node_have_attribute(node, key)
7786        && node.has_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS)
7787        && match raw_step {
7788          Some(serial) => {
7789            node
7790              .get_attribute(RAW_REFSTEP_MARK)
7791              .is_none_or(|numbered| numbered == serial.to_string())
7792              && !within_math(node)
7793          },
7794          None => {
7795            get_node_qname(node) != pin!("ltx:picture")
7796              && node.get_attribute(RAW_REFSTEP_MARK).is_none()
7797          },
7798        }
7799    };
7800    // Perl: start from lastChild of current node if it's an element
