7801    let start = if self.node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) && !after_undone_step {
7802      self
7803        .node
7804        .get_last_child()
7805        .unwrap_or_else(|| self.node.clone())
7806    } else {
7807      self.node.clone()
7808    };
7809    let ancestors: Vec<Node> = self
7810      .get_insertion_candidates(&start)
7811      .into_iter()
7812      .filter(|node| node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode))
7813      .collect();
7814    let mut candidates: VecDeque<&Node> = ancestors.iter().collect();
7815    // Should we only accept a node that already has an id, or should we create an id?
7816    let mut node_opt: Option<Cow<Node>> = None;
7817    while let Some(candidate) = candidates.pop_front() {
7818      if may_label(candidate) {
7819        node_opt = Some(Cow::Borrowed(candidate));
7820        break;
7821      }
7822    }
7823
7824    if node_opt.is_none() {
7825      // No appropriate ancestor?
7826      let sib: Option<Node> = match ancestors.first() {
7827        Some(n) => n.get_last_child(),
7828        None => None,
7829      };
7830      if let Some(sibling) = sib {
7831        if may_label(&sibling) {
7832          node_opt = Some(Cow::Owned(sibling));
7833        } else if !ancestors.is_empty() {
7834          // just take root element?
7835          node_opt = Some(Cow::Borrowed(ancestors.last().as_ref().unwrap()));
7836        }
7837      } else if !ancestors.is_empty() {
7838        // just take root element?
7839        node_opt = Some(Cow::Borrowed(ancestors.last().as_ref().unwrap()));
7840      }
7841    }
7842    if let Some(node) = node_opt {
7843      let savenode = self.node.clone();
7844      self.set_node(&node);
7845      Some(savenode)
7846    } else {
7847      let message = s!("No open node with an xml:id can get attribute {:?}", key);
7848      Warn!("malformed", key, message);
7849      //  $self->getInsertionContext());
7850      None
7851    }
7852  }
7853
7854  /// The object a label after a raw counter step names (the node [`float_to_label_for`](Self::float_to_label_for)
7855  /// found, current) takes the step's number: the `tags` LaTeXML makes for every step
7856  /// (`binding::counter::dialect::label_stepped_counter`), whose `refnum` is what `\ref` prints, as LaTeX's `\ref`
7857  /// prints the step's `\@currentlabel` (latex.ltx:14963-14967). Only an object with no number of its own (no
7858  /// `ltx:tags`: a box drawn as a picture, a listing's line) that may hold one and is not a unit numbered by its heading
7859  /// (an `ltx:title` holder: an unnumbered `\section*` or theorem stays unnumbered). The tag without a role, the number
7860  /// as the object prints it, is not kept: the box printed its number itself (tcolorbox's title "Theorem 1: …"). The
7861  /// object is marked with the step's `serial` (`_raw_refstep`, a bookkeeping attribute), so another step's label does
7862  /// not take it. Perl leaves the label on the enclosing section, whose number `\ref` prints (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS
7863  /// #1038). Witnesses: 2506.01072 (`\newtcbtheorem`), 2505.20088 (`\newtcolorbox[auto counter]`), 2402.06608,
7864  /// 2609.20563 (`\newtcblisting`); guards `perfect_kernel_batch78g`.
7865  pub fn take_raw_refstep_number(&mut self, tags: &Digested, serial: i64) -> Result<()> {
7866    let mut target = self.node.clone();
7867    let qname = get_node_qname(&target);
7868    let own_tags = target
7869      .get_child_elements()
7870      .into_iter()
7871      .find(|child| get_node_qname(child) == pin!("ltx:tags"));
7872    if let Some(own_tags) = own_tags {
7873      // An object that printed the step's number itself and gives no reference form (an algorithm2e line's tag:
7874      // `\nl`'s `\refstepcounter{AlgoLine}` then `\algocf@printnl`, algorithm2e.sty:1662-1667) takes the step's
7875      // reference forms into its tags, after the printed one: `\ref` prints `\theAlgoLine` (pdflatex 14 for
7876      // 2406.05437's `step1`, which named the algorithm, 1; OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #877).
7877      let numbered_here = target.get_attribute(RAW_REFSTEP_MARK) == Some(serial.to_string());
7878      let has_forms = own_tags
7879        .get_child_elements()
7880        .iter()
7881        .any(|tag| tag.has_attribute("role"));
7882      if numbered_here && !has_forms {
7883        self.add_reference_forms(&target, own_tags, tags)?;
7884      }
7885      return Ok(());
7886    }
7887    if !can_contain_qsym(qname, pin!("ltx:tags")) || can_contain_qsym(qname, pin!("ltx:title")) {
7888      return Ok(());
7889    }
7890    let before = target.get_child_nodes();
7891    self.absorb(tags, None)?;
7892    let _ = target.set_attribute(RAW_REFSTEP_MARK, &serial.to_string());
7893    let first = before.first().cloned();
7894    for mut new in target.get_child_nodes() {
7895      if before.contains(&new) {
7896        continue;
7897      }
7898      for tag in new.get_child_elements() {
7899        if get_node_qname(&tag) == pin!("ltx:tag") && !tag.has_attribute("role") {
7900          self.remove_node(tag);
7901        }
7902      }
7903      // The number first, where an object's `ltx:tags` stands.
7904      if let Some(mut first) = first.clone() {
7905        new.unlink_node();
7906        first.add_prev_sibling(&mut new).ok();
7907      }
7908    }
7909    Ok(())
7910  }
7911
7912  /// Records `object` as the one that printed the number of the raw counter step `serial` itself (an algorithm2e line:
7913  /// `\nl`'s `\refstepcounter{AlgoLine}` then `\algocf@printnl`), marking it (`RAW_REFSTEP_MARK`): a label after the
7914  /// step names it ([`float_to_label_scoped`](Self::float_to_label_scoped)) and takes its reference forms
7915  /// ([`take_raw_refstep_number`](Self::take_raw_refstep_number)).
7916  pub fn note_raw_refstep_object(&mut self, serial: i64, object: &Node) {
7917    let mut object = object.clone();
7918    let _ = object.set_attribute(RAW_REFSTEP_MARK, &serial.to_string());
7919    self.raw_refstep_objects.insert(serial, object);
7920  }
7921
7922  /// A `\label{key}` placed on `holder` takes `key` from the elements holding it before that contain `holder` or that it
7923  /// contains: LaTeX's last `\newlabel` wins (latex.ltx `\@newl@bel`: `\global\@namedef{r@key}`, "Label multiply
7924  /// defined"), where the post scan registers in document order, the outer element first (Perl Scan.pm:196-203, ours
7925  /// `latexml_post/src/scan.rs` `register_scanned`), so an earlier label on an element inside a later one won: 2001.00288's
7926  /// `\label{algo2}` after `\KwOut` (its line) and again after `\caption` (the algorithm) printed "Algorithm 1" for
7927  /// pdflatex's "Algorithm 2" (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #1131, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #877). Holders apart from each other
7928  /// keep the key: pdflatex's last `\newlabel` is the last written, the later in the document but for a float LaTeX
7929  /// defers past a later label of the key (not modelled: `[p]` figure then `\section{Two}\label{k}`, pdflatex the
7930  /// figure), and the scan already takes the later; an element
7931  /// the streaming build spilled may be one (spills are closed top-level elements, never `holder`'s ancestors or, below
7932  /// the document root, its descendants), so streaming and eager builds agree. Searched only for a key placed before.
7933  /// Guard `perfect_kernel_batch78t::the_later_label_wins`.
7934  pub fn release_earlier_label_holders(&mut self, key: &str, holder: &Node) {
7935    if self.placed_labels.insert(key.to_string()) {
7936      return;
7937    }
7938    // The document root holds what no element took; its descendants may have been spilled.
7939    let Some(parent) = holder
7940      .get_parent()
7941      .filter(|p| p.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode))
7942    else {
7943      return;
7944    };
7945    let mut nested = self.findnodes("descendant::*[@labels]", Some(holder));
7946    let mut ancestor = Some(parent);
7947    while let Some(node) = ancestor {
7948      ancestor = node
7949        .get_parent()
7950        .filter(|p| p.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode));
7951      nested.push(node);
7952    }
7953    for mut node in nested {
7954      let Some(labels) = node.get_attribute("labels") else {
7955        continue;
7956      };
7957      if !labels.split_whitespace().any(|label| label == key) {
7958        continue;
7959      }
7960      let rest: Vec<&str> = labels
7961        .split_whitespace()
7962        .filter(|label| *label != key)
7963        .collect();
7964      if rest.is_empty() {
7965        let _ = node.remove_attribute("labels");
7966      } else {
7967        let _ = node.set_attribute("labels", &rest.join(" "));
7968      }
7969    }
7970  }
7971
7972  /// The reference forms of `tags` (its tags with a role: refnum, typerefnum, …) appended to `own_tags`, an `ltx:tags`
7973  /// of `target` ([`take_raw_refstep_number`](Self::take_raw_refstep_number)).
7974  fn add_reference_forms(
7975    &mut self,
7976    target: &Node,
7977    mut own_tags: Node,
7978    tags: &Digested,
7979  ) -> Result<()> {
7980    let before = target.get_child_nodes();
7981    let savenode = self.node.clone();
7982    self.set_node(target);
7983    self.absorb(tags, None)?;
7984    self.set_node(&savenode);
7985    for new in target.get_child_nodes() {
7986      if before.contains(&new) {
7987        continue;
7988      }
7989      for mut tag in new.get_child_elements() {
7990        if get_node_qname(&tag) == pin!("ltx:tag") && tag.has_attribute("role") {
7991          tag.unlink_node();
7992          own_tags.add_child(&mut tag).ok();
7993        }
7994      }
7995      self.remove_node(new);
7996    }
7997    Ok(())
7998  }
7999
8000  /// One `ltx:tags` for an object a raw step numbered ([`take_raw_refstep_number`](Self::take_raw_refstep_number))
8001  /// that a later construct tags as well (`\eqno`'s, made after the label in `$$ \refstepcounter{foo}\label{x2} c=d
8002  /// \eqno(B) $$`): the later tags' tags join the step's `ltx:tags`, before its `refnum`, so the object shows "(B)" and
8003  /// `\ref` prints the step's number (pdflatex 42; the `\@currentlabel` `\eqno` leaves alone). The nearest open
8004  /// element holding an `ltx:tags`, from the current node. Repro
8005  /// `cross-references/unnumbered_display_label_takes_the_step_number.tex`.
8006  pub fn merge_raw_refstep_tags(&mut self) {
8007    let mut node = Some(self.node.clone());
8008    while let Some(current) = node {
8009      let tags: Vec<Node> = current
8010        .get_child_elements()
8011        .into_iter()
8012        .filter(|child| get_node_qname(child) == pin!("ltx:tags"))
8013        .collect();
8014      if !tags.is_empty() {
8015        if tags.len() > 1 && current.get_attribute(RAW_REFSTEP_MARK).is_some() {
8016          let mut first = tags[0].clone();
8017          let anchor = first.get_first_child();
8018          for mut later in tags.into_iter().skip(1) {
8019            for mut tag in later.get_child_nodes() {
8020              tag.unlink_node();
8021              match &anchor {
8022                Some(anchor) => {
8023                  let mut anchor = anchor.clone();
8024                  anchor.add_prev_sibling(&mut tag).ok();
8025                },
8026                None => {
8027                  first.add_child(&mut tag).ok();
8028                },
8029              }
8030            }
8031            later.unlink_node();
8032          }
8033        }
8034        return;
8035      }
8036      node = current
8037        .get_parent()
8038        .filter(|p| p.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode));
8039    }
8040  }
8041
8042  pub fn set_box_to_absorb(&mut self, arg: Option<Digested>) {
8043    self
8044      .localized_boxes
8045      .push((self.box_to_absorb.take(), self.box_unended));
8046    // A whatsit the document ended inside of never ended (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #542). Any other box
8047    // shares the state of the one absorbing it: an alignment is its `\lx@begin@alignment`
8048    // whatsit's property, a cell's content opens the cell's `ltx:XMArg` (nucl-th0401019).
8049    self.box_unended = match arg {
8050      Some(ref tbox) if matches!(tbox.data(), DigestedData::Whatsit(_)) => {
8051        tbox.get_property_bool(crate::stomach::UNENDED)
8052      },
8053      Some(_) => self.box_unended,
8054      None => false,
8055    };
8056    self
8057      .localized_box_locators
8058      .push(self.current_box_locator.take());
8059    self.box_to_absorb = arg;
8060    // Capture the locator now, while the box's RefCell is unborrowed — the
8061    // source-map stamping (`open_element`) reads this Copy value instead of
8062    // re-borrowing the box mid-`be_absorbed`. Gated so the normal path is free.
8063    self.current_box_locator = if state::source_map_enabled() {
8064      self.box_to_absorb.as_ref().and_then(|b| b.get_locator())
8065    } else {
8066      None
8067    };
8068  }
8069  /// Whether the box being absorbed never ended ([`crate::stomach::UNENDED`]): the elements it
8070  /// opens auto-close ([`UNENDED_ATTRIBUTE`]).
8071  fn absorbing_unended_box(&self) -> bool { self.box_unended }
8072
8073  pub fn expire_box_to_absorb(&mut self) {
8074    (self.box_to_absorb, self.box_unended) = self.localized_boxes.pop().unwrap();
8075    self.current_box_locator = self.localized_box_locators.pop().unwrap_or(None);
8076  }
8077
8078  /// token-locators: directly set the locator used to stamp the NEXT opened
8079  /// element, without touching the `box_to_absorb` stack. The alignment absorb
8080  /// uses this to give each `tabular`/`tr`/`td` its own (table/row/cell) span,
8081  /// since those elements are opened *before* their content's `box_to_absorb`
8082  /// is set. Transient: each cell overwrites it and the enclosing
8083  /// `expire_box_to_absorb` (the Alignment absorb frame) restores the prior
8084  /// value. See docs/performance/SOURCE_PROVENANCE.md §3.1.3.
8085  #[cfg(feature = "token-locators")]
8086  pub fn set_current_box_locator(&mut self, loc: Option<Locator>) {
8087    self.current_box_locator = loc;
8088  }
8089
8090  /// Resolve a rewrite label: this document's own labels first, then the
8091  /// shared document-wide map a streaming fragment carries
8092  /// (`rewrite_labels_shared`). The two-level lookup replaces copying the
8093  /// whole label index into every fragment — see the field docs.
8094  pub fn lookup_rewrite_label(&self, key: &str) -> Option<String> {
8095    self
8096      .rewrite_labels
8097      .get(key)
8098      .or_else(|| {
8099        self
8100          .rewrite_labels_shared
8101          .as_ref()
8102          .and_then(|shared| shared.get(key))
8103      })
8104      .cloned()
8105  }
8106
8107  pub fn load_labels_for_rewrite(&mut self) -> Result<()> {
8108    for mut node in self.findnodes("//*[@labels]", None) {
8109      if let Some(labels) = node.get_attribute("labels") {
8110        // A labelled node MUST carry an xml:id so `\ref` can resolve to it.
8111        // The `Tag('ltx:*', afterClose:late)` GenerateID hook
8112        // (latex_constructs/sect11.rs) stamps one when the node closes — the
8113        // <ltx:document> root too, which receives a label when a bare
8114        // `\label{…}` appears with no enclosing id'd sectioning (e.g.
8115        // `\input{abs}` then `\label{sec:intro}` before any \section; witness
8116        // 1703.09326; Perl's output is `<document … labels="LABEL:sec:intro"
8117        // xml:id="id1">`). This is the safety net for a labelled node still
8118        // without one: generate it here, exactly as Perl's GenerateID does (an
8119        // id-less root yields "id1" from `generate_id`'s empty-prefix→"id",
8120        // no-ancestor path), never an error.
8121        let id = match node.get_attribute("id") {
8122          Some(id) => Some(id),
8123          None => {
8124            self.generate_id(&mut node, "")?;
8125            node.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS)
8126          },
8127        };
8128        if let Some(id) = id {
8129          for label in labels.split_whitespace() {
8130            self.rewrite_labels.insert(label.to_string(), id.clone());
8131          }
8132        }
8133        // If generate_id still couldn't assign one (a node the model forbids
8134        // an xml:id on), the label is simply unresolvable — drop it silently
8135        // (Perl does not error here either).
8136      }
8137    }
8138    Ok(())
8139  }

8141  fn set_local_font(&mut self, arg: Rc<Font>) { self.localized_fonts.push(arg); }
8142  fn get_local_font(&self) -> Option<Rc<Font>> { self.localized_fonts.last().cloned() }
8143  fn expire_local_font(&mut self) { self.localized_fonts.pop(); }

8145  //**********************************************************************
8146  /// This function computes an xml:id for a node, if it hasn't already got one.
8147  /// It is suitable for use in Tag afterOpen as
8148  ///  `Tag('ltx:para',afterOpen=>sub { GenerateID(@_,'p'); });`
8149  /// It generates an id of the form `<parentid>.<prefix><number>`
8150  /// The parent node (the one with `ID=<parentid>`) also maintains a counter
8151  /// stored in an attribute `_ID_counter_<prefix>` recording the last used
8152  /// `number` for `prefix` amongst its descendents.
8153  pub fn generate_id(&mut self, node: &mut Node, mut prefix: &str) -> Result<()> {
8154    // If node doesn't already have an id, and can
8155    // but isn't a _Capture_ node (which ultimately should disappear)
8156    let qname = get_node_qname(node);
8157    if !node.has_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS)
8158      && model::can_have_attribute(qname, pin!("xml:id"))
8159      && (qname != pin!("ltx:_Capture_"))
8160    {
8161      // Nearest ancestor element carrying @xml:id — a direct parent-chain
8162      // walk, equivalent to the previous `ancestor::*[@xml:id][1]` findnode
8163      // but without a per-call XPath parse+eval (generate_id runs once per
8164      // id-lacking node during finalize; 2026-08-23 audit R5).
8165      let mut found = None;
8166      let mut cur = node.get_parent();
8167      while let Some(p) = cur {
8168        if p.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) && p.has_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
8169          found = Some(p);
8170          break;
8171        }
8172        cur = p.get_parent();
8173      }
8174      // A streamed segment's top nodes are minted under the spine element it splices back under (pass 2).
8175      let anchor = found
8176        .is_none()
8177        .then(|| self.fragment_anchor_id.clone())
8178        .flatten();
8179      let mut ancestor = found.unwrap_or_else(|| self.get_document().get_root_element().unwrap());
8180      //// Old versions don't like ancestor.getAttribute('xml:id');
8181      let ancestor_id = ancestor.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS).or(anchor);
8182      // If we've got no ancestor_id, then we've got no ancestor (no document yet!),
8183      // or ancestor IS the root element (but without an id);
8184      // If we also have no prefix, we'll end up with an illegal id (just digits)!!!
8185      // We'll use "id" for an id prefix; this will work whether or not we have an ancestor.
8186      if prefix.is_empty() && ancestor_id.is_none() {
8187        prefix = "id";
8188      }
8189
8190      // Perl `Package.pm:939` (`'_ID_counter_' . ($prefix ? $prefix . '_' : '')`)
8191      // — empty prefix uses `_ID_counter_` with a single trailing underscore,
8192      // not `_ID_counter__`. Matters for interop with code that reads the
8193      // attribute by exact name (e.g. `Base_XMath.pool.ltxml:940` reads
8194      // `_ID_counter_` for the empty-prefix counter).
8195      let ctrkey = if prefix.is_empty() {
8196        s!("_ID_counter_")
8197      } else {
8198        s!("_ID_counter_") + prefix + "_"
8199      };
8200      let a_ctr = ancestor.get_attribute(&ctrkey).unwrap_or_else(|| s!("0"));
8201
8202      let ctr_int = 1 + a_ctr.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0);
8203      let ctr = ctr_int.to_string();
8204
8205      let id = match ancestor_id {
8206        Some(aid) => aid + ".",
8207        None => String::new(),
8208      } + prefix
8209        + &ctr;
8210
8211      ancestor.set_attribute(&ctrkey, &ctr)?;
8212      self.set_attribute(node, "xml:id", &id)?;
8213    }
8214    Ok(())
8215  }
8216
8217  //%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
8218  // Finally, another set of surgery methods
8219  // These take an array representation of the XML Tree to append
8220  //   [tagname,{attributes..}, children]
8221  // THESE SHOULD BE PART OF A COMMON BASE CLASS; DUPLICATED IN Post::Document
8222  //%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
8223
8224  /// `replace_tree`, minus the free: the detached original stays alive and
8225  /// the CALLER owns it. The math parser needs this — parsing one formula
8226  /// rebuilds its tree while later formulae, queued up front, may sit inside
8227  /// the replaced subtree (a `\text{…$x$…}` inside math), so it defers every
8228  /// free to the end of the parse (`replace_tree_deferred` /
8229  /// `data::defer_discard`); freeing here handed those formulae to the parser
8230  /// detached and lost whole documents (sweep 102: glosmathtools, prftree,
8231  /// t-angles).
8232  pub fn replace_tree_detach(&mut self, new: Node, old: Node) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
8233    match old.get_parent() {
8234      Some(mut parent) => {
8235        let mut following = VecDeque::new(); // Collect the matching and following nodes
8236        while let Some(mut sib) = parent.get_last_child() {
8237          if sib == old {
8238            break;
8239          }
8240          // parent.remove_child(sib); // We're putting these back, in a moment!
8241          sib.unlink();
8242          following.push_front(sib);
8243        }
8244        // Unrecord old's ids BEFORE the copy, so the copy's freshly
8245        // recorded entries (append_tree → open_element_at) survive — the
8246        // copy typically re-uses the same id strings.
8247        self.unrecord_node_ids(&old);
8248        // COPY FIRST, detach `old` after: `new` may sit INSIDE `old`
8249        // (parse_single's single-node shortcut returns an original child;
8250        // tex_box's foreignObject cleanup replaces a node with its own
8251        // grandchild), so `old` must stay intact while append_tree
8252        // serializes the copy. With `following` detached, the copy lands in
8253        // old's slot either way.
8254        self.append_tree(&mut parent, vec![new])?;
8255        let inserted = parent.get_last_child();
8256        // Keep the insertion point out of the discarded subtree (the
8257        // `chopped` half of remove_node; its id bookkeeping happened above).
8258        let mut cursor = Some(self.node.clone());
8259        while let Some(cur) = cursor {
8260          if cur == old {
8261            self.set_node(&parent);
8262            break;
8263          }
8264          cursor = cur.get_parent();
8265        }
8266        // Detach `old` (the original of the copy `append_tree` just
8267        // inserted); `replace_tree` frees it, the parser defers that.
8268        {
8269          let mut old = old;
8270          old.unlink();
8271        }
8272        for mut child in following {
8273          parent.add_child(&mut child)?; // No need for clone
8274        }
8275        Ok(inserted)
8276      },
8277      _ => Ok(None),
8278    }
8279  }
8280
8281  /// Replace `old` by `new` (copied into place) and FREE the original: its
8282  /// ids were unrecorded before the copy and no handle into it is used
8283  /// afterwards (see `remove_node` for why a bare unlink leaks). Callers that
8284  /// must keep the original alive use `replace_tree_detach`.
8285  pub fn replace_tree(&mut self, new: Node, old: Node) -> Result<Option<Node>> {
8286    let inserted = self.replace_tree_detach(new, old.clone())?;
8287    if inserted.is_some() {
8288      self.discard_subtree(old);
8289    }
8290    Ok(inserted)
8291  }
8292
8293  pub fn append_tree(&mut self, node: &mut Node, data: Vec<Node>) -> Result<()> {
8294    for child in data {
8295      match child.get_type() {
8296        Some(NodeType::ElementNode) => {
8297          let mut attributes: HashMap<String, String> =
8298            child.get_attributes().into_iter().collect();
8299          // Perl appendTree: REMOVE xml:id from source node before re-creation.
8300          // This prevents duplicate ID registration. The ID will be re-registered
8301          // by open_element_at when the new node is created with the same ID.
8302          if let Some(xmlid) = child.get_attribute_ns("id", XML_NS) {
8303            attributes
8304              .entry("xml:id".to_string())
8305              .or_insert_with(|| xmlid.clone());
8306            // Unrecord before re-creation (Perl: $child->removeAttribute('xml:id') + unRecordID)
8307            self.unrecord_id(&xmlid);
8308          }
8309
8310          // `get_FOREIGN_node_qname`: `data` may be a tree parsed elsewhere
8311          // (`Document::insert_xml`), whose elements can sit in a DEFAULT
8312          // namespace that is not ours — `<p xmlns="…/1999/xhtml">`. Only here is
8313          // that shape possible, and only here do we pay to resolve it.
8314          let tag_sym = model::get_foreign_node_qname(&child);
8315          let tag = arena::to_string(tag_sym);
8316          // Perl copies every attribute, `_box` included (Document.pm:2110-2116),
8317          // so the new node keeps the copied node's box rather than taking its
8318          // new parent's: a foreignObject re-created by the math parser is
8319          // sized from its own box again (tests/graphics/xytest).
8320          let child_box = self.get_node_box(&child);
8321          let mut new =
8322            self.open_element_at_with_box(node, &tag, Some(attributes), None, child_box)?;
8323          self.append_tree(&mut new, child.get_child_nodes())?;
8324          self.close_element_at(&mut new)?;
8325        },
8326        Some(NodeType::DocumentFragNode) => {
8327          self.append_tree(node, child.get_child_nodes())?;
8328        },
8329        Some(NodeType::TextNode) => {
8330          node.append_text(&child.get_content())?;
8331        },
8332        other => {
8333          log::debug!("append_tree: unhandled libxml NodeType {other:?}");
8334        },
8335      }
8336    }
8337    Ok(())
8338  }
8339
8340  /// Parse an XML / (X)HTML markup string and splice the resulting subtree into
8341  /// the document at the current insertion point.
8342  ///
8343  /// Named as the markup counterpart to [`Document::insert_element`] (Perl
8344  /// `insertElement`): both insert an already-FINISHED thing at the current point.
8345  /// Deliberately NOT an `absorb*` name — in Perl `absorb` consumes a digested
8346  /// Box and has no `XML::LibXML` branch at all (it would die on a node), so
8347  /// borrowing that verb here would imply a kinship that does not exist.
8348  ///
8349  /// This is the Rust analog of Perl BookML's `\bmlRawHTML` idiom, which composes
8350  /// two mechanisms core never chains itself: `XML::LibXML->parse_string`
8351  /// (`LaTeXML::Common::XML::Parser` `parseChunk`, `Common/XML/Parser.pm:36-39`)
8352  /// and `$document->appendTree`
8353  /// (`Document.pm:2093`, foreign-node branch `:2105-2124`). Both halves already
8354  /// exist here — libxml's parser (a direct `latexml_core` dep, used in
8355  /// `common/relaxng/scan.rs`) and [`Document::append_tree`] — so this is pure
8356  /// glue.
8357  ///
8358  /// The markup must be WELL-FORMED, but need not be a single root: several
8359  /// sibling nodes, or bare text, are accepted as a document fragment
8360  /// (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #66 — Perl's `parseChunk` is single-node only). The parsed
8361  /// nodes are re-created one by one through `append_tree`'s model-aware path, so
8362  /// namespaces declared in the snippet (e.g. xhtml) are preserved and `xml:id`s
8363  /// re-registered. Malformed markup is REJECTED, never salvaged — see
8364  /// [`crate::common::xml::parse_chunk`] for what libxml's recovery mode
8365  /// destroys — and surfaces as a clean `Error:` that inserts nothing, degrading
8366  /// the offending binding rather than aborting the conversion (the
8367  /// runtime-bindings failure-isolation contract).
8368  pub fn insert_xml(&mut self, xml: &str) -> Result<()> {
8369    // The parsed Document OWNS the nodes `append_tree` re-creates from, so it
8370    // must stay alive across the call below (bound here, dropped at fn end).
8371    let parsed = match xml::parse_fragment(xml) {
8372      Ok(doc) => doc,
8373      Err(e) => {
8374        // Quote the offending snippet: a binding may insert markup from several
8375        // places, and the reason alone would not say WHICH one to go fix. Capped
8376        // so a runaway string cannot flood the log with a single message.
8377        const SNIPPET_CAP: usize = 200;
8378        let mut snippet: String = xml.chars().take(SNIPPET_CAP).collect();
8379        if xml.chars().nth(SNIPPET_CAP).is_some() {
8380          snippet.push('…');
8381        }
8382        Error!(
8383          "malformed",
8384          "insertXML",
8385          format!("could not parse XML markup: {e}"),
8386          format!("in: {snippet}")
8387        );
8388        return Ok(());
8389      },
8390    };
8391    if parsed.is_empty() {
8392      Error!(
8393        "malformed",
8394        "insertXML",
8395        "XML markup parsed to an empty document".to_string()
8396      );
8397      return Ok(());
8398    }
8399    // `parsed` stays bound until this returns, so it keeps owning the nodes.
8400    self.insert_nodes(parsed.nodes())
8401  }
8402
8403  /// Splice ALREADY-PARSED nodes into the document at the current insertion
8404  /// point. The shared tail of [`Document::insert_xml`] and of any caller that
8405  /// obtained its nodes some other way (a script that parsed once and inserts
8406  /// repeatedly, or that edited the parsed tree before inserting).
8407  ///
8408  /// The caller must keep whatever owns `nodes` alive across this call: libxml
8409  /// nodes are pointers into their document. [`crate::common::xml::ParsedFragment`]
8410  /// exists to make that ownership explicit rather than a comment.
8411  pub fn insert_nodes(&mut self, nodes: Vec<Node>) -> Result<()> {
8412    let mut point = self.get_node().clone();
8413    self.append_tree(&mut point, nodes)
8414  }
8415}
8416
8417// Auxiliary
8418
8419/// Strip characters that may not appear in XML 1.0 content at all: NUL and
8420/// the other C0 controls except TAB/LF/CR, plus the non-characters
8421/// U+FFFE/U+FFFF. libxml's `CString`-based APIs *panic* on interior NULs
8422/// (node.rs:639), and the rest produce non-well-formed output that downstream
8423/// XML consumers reject. Single shared policy for the document sinks
8424/// (`set_attribute`, `open_text_internal`, `open_math_text_internal`).
8425/// Borrow-free in the (overwhelmingly common) clean case.
8426fn xml_sanitize(value: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {
8427  fn invalid(c: char) -> bool {
8428    (c < '\u{20}' && c != '\t' && c != '\n' && c != '\r') || c == '\u{FFFE}' || c == '\u{FFFF}'
8429  }
8430  if value.chars().any(invalid) {
8431    Cow::Owned(value.chars().filter(|c| !invalid(*c)).collect())
8432  } else {
8433    Cow::Borrowed(value)
8434  }
8435}
8436
8437fn serialize_string(string: &str) -> String {
8438  // Basic entities
8439  let mut serialized = string.replace('&', "&amp;");
8440  serialized = serialized.replace('>', "&gt;");
8441  serialized = serialized.replace('<', "&lt;");
8442  serialized
8443}
8444
8445fn serialize_attr(string: &str) -> String {
8446  let mut serialized = serialize_string(string);
8447  // And escape any remaining special code points
8448  serialized = serialized.replace('\"', "&quot;");
8449  serialized = serialized.replace('\n', "&#10;");
8450  serialized = serialized.replace('\t', "&#9;");
8451  serialized
8452}

8523/// The return type of this method is somewhat artisinal, as we have a three-way semantics:
8524/// - `None`: There is no known structure that allows `child` as a descendant of `tag`
8525/// - `Some(None)`: `child` is directly allowed inside `tag`
8526/// - `Some(Some(inter_tag))`: `child` is allowed inside `inter_tag`, which is allowed in `tag`
8527///
8528/// This could also (maybe more naturally?) be represented with a custom 3-valued enum.
8529/// That said, I think it may be wiser to refactor the method entirely, always requiring a `bool`
8530/// check, followed by an explicit request for the `inner_tag` name, which can be `Option<SymStr>`.
8531pub fn sym_can_contain_somehow(tag: SymStr, child: SymStr) -> Option<Option<SymStr>> {
8532  match model::can_contain_sym(tag, child) {
8533    true => Some(None),
8534    false => can_contain_indirect(tag, child).map(Some),
8535  }
8536}

8549// Dirty little secrets:
8550//  You can generically allow an element to autoClose using Tag.
8551// OR you can indicate a specific node can autoClose, or forbid it, using
8552// the _autoclose or _noautoclose attributes!
8553/// The sectioning units `\section`…`\subparagraph` open, which a frontmatter block takes without an error, as Perl's
8554/// builder does (the leniency in `find_insertion_point_qsym`).
8555fn is_lenient_sectioning_unit(qsym: SymStr) -> bool {
8556  qsym == pin!("ltx:section")
8557    || qsym == pin!("ltx:subsection")
8558    || qsym == pin!("ltx:subsubsection")
8559    || qsym == pin!("ltx:paragraph")
8560    || qsym == pin!("ltx:subparagraph")
8561}

8563/// Whether a list item carries its label (`ltx:tags`: a bullet, a number, a description term); a margin list's
8564/// `\item[]` has none.

8566  node
8567    .get_child_elements()
8568    .iter()
8569    .any(|child| get_node_qname(child) == pin!("ltx:tags"))
8570}

8572/// Whether neither `node` nor any of its ancestors is a frontmatter container (`ltx:abstract`, `ltx:acknowledgements`,
8573/// `ltx:keywords`, `ltx:classification`, `ltx:creator`), which the theorem/proof/TOC bridge leaves alone
8574/// (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #689).
8575fn outside_frontmatter_container(node: &Node) -> bool {
8576  let mut cur = Some(node.clone());
8577  while let Some(n) = cur {
8578    if n.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
8579      && with_node_qname(&n, |q| {
8580        matches!(
8581          q,
8582          "ltx:abstract"
8583            | "ltx:acknowledgements"
8584            | "ltx:keywords"
8585            | "ltx:classification"
8586            | "ltx:creator"
8587        )
8588      })
8589    {
8590      return false;
8591    }
8592    cur = n.get_parent();
8593  }
8594  true
8595}

8606/// The sectioning units that close a quote they arrive in (`Document::close_quotes_blocking`): the display units
8607/// `\part` to `\subsubsection`, starred or not (an `\appendix`'s units are these too). The run-in `\paragraph` and
8608/// `\subparagraph` (latex.ltx `\@startsection` with a negative after-skip, article.cls:314-321) are not: pdflatex sets
8609/// the heading and the text after it inside the quote's margins, so they open an `ltx:inline-sectional-block` in the
8610/// quote (`AUTO_OPEN_BRIDGES`; main-session ruling 2026-10-17, OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES #678; 2607.27159
8611/// 2505.18677 2305.11603 1809.03802 2208.14587).
8612fn is_quote_closing_unit(qsym: SymStr) -> bool {
8613  qsym == pin!("ltx:part")
8614    || qsym == pin!("ltx:chapter")
8615    || qsym == pin!("ltx:section")
8616    || qsym == pin!("ltx:subsection")
8617    || qsym == pin!("ltx:subsubsection")
8618}

8620/// Whether `node` may hold a `qsym` it can contain by the model: false only for a display unit
8621/// (`is_quote_closing_unit`) at the `ltx:inline-sectional-block` a run-in `\paragraph`/`\subparagraph` opened in a
8622/// quote (`AUTO_OPEN_BRIDGES`) — a later `\section` in the same quote closes the quote, as one before the run-in heading does
8623/// (2110.03376, 1905.08876; guard `perfect_kernel_batch69a::section_after_a_paragraph_in_a_quote_closes_it`).
8624fn holds_in_quote_block(node: &Node, qsym: SymStr) -> bool {
8625  !(is_quote_closing_unit(qsym)
8626    && get_node_qname(node) == pin!("ltx:inline-sectional-block")
8627    && node
8628      .get_parent()
8629      .is_some_and(|parent| get_node_qname(&parent) == pin!("ltx:quote")))
8630}

8643pub fn can_auto_close(node: &Node) -> bool {
8644  // text or comments auto close
8645  // otherwise must be element
8646  // without _noautoclose
8647  // and either with _autoclose
8648  // OR it has autoClose set on tag properties
8649  match node.get_type() {
8650    Some(NodeType::TextNode) | Some(NodeType::CommentNode) => true,
8651    Some(NodeType::ElementNode) if !node.has_attribute("_noautoclose") => {
8652      if node.has_attribute("_autoclose") {
8653        true
8654      } else {
8655        state::with_tag_property(get_node_qname(node), |props_opt| {
8656          if let Some(props) = props_opt {
8657            props.auto_close.unwrap_or(false)
8658          } else {
8659            false
8660          }
8661        })
8662      }
8663    },
8664    _ => false,
8665  }
8666}

8689/// `class` as a list of NMTOKENs: every whitespace-separated token keeps its
8690/// NameChars (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`, `:`) and loses the rest
8691/// (`\\ { } @ * +` from listings language literals, raw `@` names, `fa-*`);
8692/// emptied tokens drop, and a token the cleaning made a duplicate of an
8693/// earlier one drops too (`C++`, `C+` and `C` all clean to `C`). Idempotent on
8694/// a valid list.
8695fn nmtokens_clean(value: &str) -> String {
8696  let mut out = String::with_capacity(value.len());
8697  let mut seen: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
8698  for token in value.split_whitespace() {
8699    let cleaned: String = token.chars().filter(|c| is_name_char(*c)).collect();
8700    if cleaned.is_empty() || seen.contains(&cleaned) {
8701      continue;
8702    }
8703    if !out.is_empty() {
8704      out.push(' ');
8705    }
8706    out.push_str(&cleaned);
8707    seen.push(cleaned);
8708  }
8709  out
8710}
8711
8712/// XML `NameChar` (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`, `:`, and the non-ASCII
8713/// name ranges, approximated by `is_alphanumeric`).
8714fn is_name_char(c: char) -> bool { c.is_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '-' | '_' | ':') }
8715
8716/// XML `Name` without a colon (an `xml:id`): starts with a letter or `_`, then
8717/// NameChars only.
8718fn is_xml_name(value: &str) -> bool {
8719  let mut chars = value.chars();
8720  match chars.next() {
8721    Some(c) if c.is_alphabetic() || c == '_' => {},
8722    _ => return false,
8723  }
8724  chars.all(|c| is_name_char(c) && c != ':')
8725}

8727/// Perl `eq` on two boxes: the same box object.
8728fn same_box(a: &Digested, b: &Digested) -> bool { a.as_ptr() == b.as_ptr() }

8730/// A box's `mode` property (Perl `$box->getProperty('mode')`).
8731fn box_mode(bx: &Digested) -> Option<SymStr> {
8732  bx.get_property("mode").and_then(|m| match m.as_ref() {

8742/// Whether Perl's `List(…, mode => $mode)` flattens horizontal lists in this
8743/// mode: `horizontal` (List.pm:45-48). A box with no `mode` counts as
8744/// horizontal: a Rust `Tbox` carries none, where Perl's `Box()` records the
8745/// `MODE` it was made in (Package.pm, `mode => $state->lookupValue('MODE')`),
8746/// `horizontal` for paragraph text.
8747fn flattens(mode: Option<SymStr>) -> bool { mode.is_none_or(|m| m == pin!("horizontal")) }
8748
8749/// Perl `$box->unlist`: a list's boxes, else the box itself.
8750/// What [`Document::remove_node_with_box_action`] does with the removed node's
8751/// box in the boxes of its parent and of the parent's auto-opened ancestors:
8752/// [`Document::remove_node`] unlinks it, [`Document::remove_node_keeping_box`]
8753/// keeps it.
8754#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
8755enum NodeBoxAction {
8756  /// The box leaves them: the node's content is gone.
8757  Unlink,
8758  /// The box stays: the node's content lives on in another node.
8759  Keep,
8760}
8761
8762fn unlist(bx: &Digested) -> Vec<Digested> {
8763  match bx.data() {
8764    DigestedData::List(cell) => match cell.try_borrow() {
8765      Ok(list) => list.boxes.clone(),
8766      Err(_) => vec![bx.clone()],
8767    },
8768    _ => vec![bx.clone()],
8769  }
8770}
8771
8772/// `($box->unlist)[-1]`, without copying the list.
8773fn unlist_last(bx: &Digested) -> Option<Digested> {
8774  match bx.data() {
8775    DigestedData::List(cell) => cell
8776      .try_borrow()
8777      .ok()
8778      .and_then(|list| list.boxes.last().cloned()),
8779    _ => Some(bx.clone()),
8780  }
8781}
8782
8783/// What a horizontal `List()` puts in place of `bx` (List.pm:45-48): the boxes
8784/// of a horizontal list, else `bx`.
8785fn flatten_horizontal(bx: &Digested) -> Vec<Digested> {
8786  if matches!(bx.data(), DigestedData::List(_)) && flattens(box_mode(bx)) {
8787    unlist(bx)
8788  } else {
8789    vec![bx.clone()]
8790  }
8791}
8792
8793/// Push `thisbox` (flattened, as a horizontal `List()` would) onto `list`, the
8794/// node's own flat box list; false when `list` is not one (a list someone else
8795/// built, or one being read). Its cached size is dropped: the list grew.
8796fn push_onto_node_box(list: &Digested, thisbox: &Digested) -> bool {
8797  let own = list.as_ptr();
8798  let DigestedData::List(cell) = list.data() else {
8799    return false;
8800  };
8801  let Ok(mut list) = cell.try_borrow_mut() else {
8802    return false;
8803  };
8804  let pushed = flatten_horizontal(thisbox);
8805  // Pushing the list into itself would make it contain itself.
8806  if !list.properties.contains_key_sym(&pin!("node_box"))
8807    || pushed.iter().any(|b| b.as_ptr() == own)
8808  {
8809    return false;
8810  }
8811  list.push_boxes(pushed);
8812  for cached in [
8813    pin!("cached_width"),
8814    pin!("cached_height"),
8815    pin!("cached_depth"),
8816  ] {
8817    list.properties.remove_sym(cached);
8818  }
8819  true
8820}
8821
8822/// Perl `List(@boxes, mode => $mode)` (List.pm:31-55) for a node's box, of two
8823/// or more boxes: a list of that mode, with `\\baselineskip` as its baseline
8824/// when vertical. A horizontal one is marked `node_box`, the node's own flat
8825/// list ([`push_onto_node_box`]).
8826fn node_box_list(boxes: Vec<Digested>, mode: Option<SymStr>) -> Digested {
8827  let nonempty = !boxes.is_empty();
8828  let mut list = List::new(boxes);
8829  if flattens(mode) {
8830    list
8831      .properties
8832      .insert_sym(pin!("node_box"), Stored::Bool(true));
8833  }
8834  if let Some(mode) = mode {
8835    list.properties.insert("mode", Stored::String(mode));
8836    if nonempty
8837      && arena::with(mode, |m| m.ends_with("vertical"))
8838      && let Some(baseline) = state::lookup_dimension("\\baselineskip")
8839    {
8840      list
8841        .properties
8842        .insert("baseline", Stored::Dimension(baseline));
8843      // With the rest of the interline parameters (tex.web §679), as a box's list records them — read when the node
8844      // is built, the parameters in force then.
8845      for (key, register) in [
8846        ("lineskip", "\\lineskip"),
8847        ("lineskiplimit", "\\lineskiplimit"),
8848      ] {
8849        if let Some(value) = state::lookup_register_quiet(register) {
8850          list
8851            .properties
8852            .insert(key, Stored::Dimension(crate::Dimension(value.value_of())));
8853        }
8854      }
8855    }
8856  }
8857  list.into()
8858}
8859
8860/// The `prefixes` that some node of `root`'s subtree uses: an attribute of `root` or of a
8861/// descendant element whose name is `prefix:…`, or a namespace declaration of `prefix` on a
8862/// descendant element. One preorder walk that stops once every prefix is found — it was a
8863/// recursion per prefix, each building a child `Vec` at every node (about 4–5 % of an ordinary
8864/// paper's core time, the 2026-10-16 study's 80-paper gdb sample).
8865fn namespace_prefixes_in_use<'p>(root: &Node, prefixes: &[&'p str]) -> HashSet<&'p str> {
8866  let mut found = HashSet::default();
8867  if prefixes.is_empty() {
8868    return found;
8869  }
8870  let note_attributes = |node: &Node, found: &mut HashSet<&'p str>| {
8871    for key in node.get_attributes().into_keys() {
8872      for &prefix in prefixes {
8873        let plen = prefix.len();
8874        if key.len() > plen && key.starts_with(prefix) && key.as_bytes()[plen] == b':' {
8875          found.insert(prefix);
8876        }
8877      }
8878    }
8879  };
8880  note_attributes(root, &mut found);
8881  let mut cur = root.get_first_child();
8882  while let Some(node) = cur {
8883    if found.len() == prefixes.len() {
8884      break;
8885    }
8886    let mut descend = None;
8887    if node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode) {
8888      for ns in node.get_namespace_declarations() {
8889        let ns_prefix = ns.get_prefix();
8890        if let Some(&prefix) = prefixes.iter().find(|&&p| p == ns_prefix) {
8891          found.insert(prefix);
8892        }
8893      }
8894      note_attributes(&node, &mut found);
8895      descend = node.get_first_child();
8896    }
8897    cur = descend.or_else(|| {
8898      let mut up = node;
8899      loop {
8900        if let Some(next) = up.get_next_sibling() {
8901          return Some(next);
8902        }
8903        match up.get_parent() {
8904          Some(parent) if parent != *root => up = parent,
8905          _ => return None,
8906        }
8907      }
8908    });
8909  }
8910  found
8911}
8912
8913/// An empty construction-time marker element (`*_Capture_`: `ltx:_Frontmatter_Capture_`, the cover-title marks), which
8914/// never reaches the output.
8915fn is_empty_capture_mark(node: &Node) -> bool {
8916  node.get_type() == Some(NodeType::ElementNode)
8917    && node.get_first_child().is_none()
8918    && node.get_name().ends_with("_Capture_")
8919}

8921/// A processing instruction's data, `key="value"` pairs (Perl Document.pm:707-709 `insertPI`): the main "operator"
8922/// first (`class`, `package`, `options`), each only when its value is true to Perl (`$attrib{$_} ? ($_) : ()`: not
8923/// empty, not `0`), then the other keys sorted (`sort keys %attrib`), so the order is the keys' and not the hash
8924/// table's (det354 C3). An operator key with a false value is left out altogether, as Perl's second list excludes the
8925/// three names (review rev78w finding 6).
8926fn pi_data(attributes: &HashMap<String, String>) -> String {
8927  let mut other_keys: Vec<&str> = attributes
8928    .keys()
8929    .map(String::as_str)
8930    .filter(|k| !matches!(*k, "class" | "package" | "options"))
8931    .collect();
8932  other_keys.sort_unstable();
8933  let operator_keys = ["class", "package", "options"].into_iter().filter(|key| {
8934    attributes
8935      .get(*key)
8936      .is_some_and(|value| !value.is_empty() && value != "0")
8937  });
8938  operator_keys
8939    .chain(other_keys)
8940    .filter_map(|key| attributes.get(key).map(|value| s!("{}=\"{}\"", key, value)))
8941    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
8942    .join(" ")
8943}
8944
8945/// An element's `_ID_counter_*` attributes, the counters `generate_id` keeps for the ids minted under it.
8946pub fn id_counters(node: &Node) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
8947  node
8948    .get_attributes()
8949    .into_iter()
8950    .filter(|(key, _)| key.starts_with("_ID_counter"))
8951    .collect()
8952}

8954#[cfg(test)]
8955mod pi_data_order {
8956  use super::{HashMap, pi_data};
8957
8958  /// Perl Document.pm:707-708: `class`/`package`/`options` first, then the rest in key order, whatever order the map
8959  /// holds them in (det354 C3).
8960  #[test]
8961  fn a_pi_lists_its_operator_then_its_keys_sorted() {
8962    for listed in [["zeta", "alpha", "mid"], ["mid", "zeta", "alpha"], [
8963      "alpha", "mid", "zeta",
8964    ]] {
8965      let mut attributes: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::default();
8966      for key in listed {
8967        attributes.insert(key.to_string(), format!("{key}-v"));
8968      }
8969      attributes.insert("package".to_string(), "p".to_string());
8970      assert_eq!(
8971        pi_data(&attributes),
8972        r#"package="p" alpha="alpha-v" mid="mid-v" zeta="zeta-v""#
8973      );
8974    }
8975  }
8976
8977  /// Perl Document.pm:707 keeps `class`/`package`/`options` only when the value is true (`$attrib{$_} ? ($_) : ()`):
8978  /// an empty or `0` one is left out, where it printed as `options=""` (review rev78w finding 6); another key with an
8979  /// empty value stays, as Perl's `sort keys` list takes every other key.
8980  #[test]
8981  fn a_pi_drops_an_operator_key_perl_reads_as_false() {
8982    let mut attributes: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::default();
8983    attributes.insert("class".to_string(), "article".to_string());
8984    attributes.insert("options".to_string(), String::new());
8985    attributes.insert("package".to_string(), "0".to_string());
8986    attributes.insert("dpi".to_string(), String::new());
8987    assert_eq!(pi_data(&attributes), r#"class="article" dpi="""#);
8988    attributes.insert("options".to_string(), "11pt".to_string());
8989    assert_eq!(
8990      pi_data(&attributes),
8991      r#"class="article" options="11pt" dpi="""#
8992    );
8993  }
8994}

8996#[cfg(test)]
8997mod attribute_cleaners {
8998  use super::{is_xml_name, nmtokens_clean};
8999
9000  /// The emitter's `class` cleaner: listings' brace/plus/backslash language
9001  /// literals, raw `@` names and a leaked `\par` become NMTOKENs; a valid
9002  /// list is untouched.
9003  #[test]
9004  fn class_values_become_nmtokens() {
9005    assert_eq!(
9006      nmtokens_clean("ltx_lst_language_{TeX}_LaTeX"),
9007      "ltx_lst_language_TeX_LaTeX"
9008    );
9009    assert_eq!(nmtokens_clean("ltx_lst_language_C++"), "ltx_lst_language_C");
9010    assert_eq!(
9011      nmtokens_clean("ltx_lst_language_C++ ltx_lst_language_C+ ltx_lst_language_C ltx_lstlisting"),
9012      "ltx_lst_language_C ltx_lstlisting"
9013    );
9014    assert_eq!(
9015      nmtokens_clean("ltx_lstlisting \\par\\par ltx_lst_language_\\lexer@cs"),
9016      "ltx_lstlisting parpar ltx_lst_language_lexercs"
9017    );
9018    assert_eq!(nmtokens_clean("fas fa-*"), "fas fa-");
9019    assert_eq!(
9020      nmtokens_clean("ltx_font_bold ltx_align_center"),
9021      "ltx_font_bold ltx_align_center"
9022    );
9023    assert_eq!(nmtokens_clean("{}"), "");
9024  }
9025
9026  /// `xml:id` values: a valid Name is left alone; the rest go through
9027  /// `clean_id` (a leading `.` gets the `X` prefix, a `\par` leak is dropped).
9028  #[test]
9029  fn ids_are_xml_names() {
9030    assert!(is_xml_name("S2.I10.i1"));
9031    assert!(is_xml_name("_x-1"));
9032    assert!(!is_xml_name(".1"));
9033    assert!(!is_xml_name("S2.I10.i1\\par"));
9034    assert!(!is_xml_name("a:b"));
9035    assert_eq!(crate::common::cleaners::clean_id(".1"), "X.1");
9036    assert_eq!(
9037      crate::common::cleaners::clean_id("S2.I10.i1\\par"),
9038      "S2.I10.i1par"
9039    );
9040  }
9041}
